issues.name: PDF renders non-WinAnsi glyphs (e.g. emoji) as "?"
issues.description:
## Deferred to v0.5 (2026-08-21, v0.4 Phase 1 triage)
The PDF writer is deliberately zero-dependency: base-14 Helvetica + WinAnsi with AFM metrics (src/pdf.js). Emoji/CJK need a vendored Unicode TTF with CID font embedding — a substantial writer extension, out of the Phase 1 timebox. Stays Open; revisit alongside v0.5. The '?' fallback is the documented behavior meanwhile.

## Fixed 2026-08-22 (v0.5 cycle)
DejaVu Sans 2.37 (757KB TTF, Bitstream Vera license, vendored with its license text) embedded on demand: a line containing any non-WinAnsi glyph renders whole-line in DejaVu via Identity-H — CIDFontType2 descendant, flate-compressed FontFile2, ToUnicode CMap (copy/paste and search verified independently via poppler pdftotext round-trip of 'Привет мир → ✓'). TTF tables (head/hhea/maxp/hmtx, cmap 4+12, OS/2) parsed by hand — the writer stays zero-dependency. Pure-ASCII docs keep the unchanged Helvetica path (1.3KB, no font objects — tested with a <100KB guard); a Unicode doc carries ~390KB of compressed font. Glyphs DejaVu lacks (CJK) render as visible □, never '?'. Caveats recorded: one face (bold/italic runs on a mixed line go regular), no subsetting.

issues.name: Collapsed left nav cannot be re-opened — #main paints over the expand chevron
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "left nav show/hide caret UAT failed, cannot show after hidden."

## Pain point
Collapsing the left nav with the `‹` chevron in the sidebar header is a one-way door. The `›` expand chevron is drawn in the workspace rail but does not respond to clicks, so the sidebar can only be recovered by clearing `localStorage['weave-nav-collapsed']` or opening a fresh profile. The collapsed state is persisted, so a reload does not recover it either.

## Reproduction
1. Open any workspace view (e.g. `/w/weave/#/table/<Issue>`).
2. Click `#nav-collapse` (`‹`) in the sidebar header. The sidebar hides; the `›` chevron appears at the top of the rail.
3. Click the `›` chevron. Nothing happens — `#app` keeps the `nav-collapsed` class.

## Root cause
`#nav-expand` is `position: fixed; top: 10px; left: 60px; z-index: 60`, i.e. it deliberately overhangs the 52px-wide rail so it sits beside it rather than stacking as a workspace chip (the shape introduced by issue #7).

Its parent `#ws-rail` is `position: sticky`, and **sticky positioning always creates a stacking context**. That traps the chevron's `z-index: 60` inside the rail's own layer. `#ws-rail` itself had `z-index: auto`, and `#main` is a later sibling with `position: relative; z-index: auto` — so `#main` painted *above* the entire rail layer, covering the part of the chevron that overhangs into main's box and swallowing the click.

The button was fully visible (`display: flex`, `visibility: visible`, `opacity: 1`, correct 22×22 rect at 60,10) — only the hit test failed, which is why it looked like a dead control rather than a missing one.

Measured in the live app (Chrome, 1280×800), `document.elementsFromPoint` at the chevron's centre — topmost first:

```
before fix: ["main", "nav-expand", "app", "BODY", "HTML"]
after fix:  ["nav-expand", "main", "app", "BODY", "HTML"]
```

A real (Playwright) click on `#nav-expand` left `#app.className === "nav-collapsed"` before the fix, and `""` after.

## Fix
One declaration — give the rail's stacking context a positive z-index so the whole rail, chevron included, clears `#main`:

```css
/* z-index is load-bearing: position:sticky creates a stacking context, so the
   rail's own layer — not #nav-expand's z-index — is what must clear #main.
   Without it #main (position:relative, later sibling) paints over the expand
   chevron that overhangs the rail, and the collapsed nav can never re-open. */
#ws-rail { …; position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh; z-index: 60; }
```

Raising `#nav-expand`'s own z-index would not have worked — it is scoped inside the context the rail creates.

## Test coverage
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs`:
- `#ws-rail carries a positive z-index so the expand chevron stays clickable` — asserts the rail is sticky *and* declares `z-index > 0`, with the stacking-context reasoning inline.
- `#nav-expand paints inside the rail stacking context, not above it` — asserts the chevron is `fixed` and its `left` overhangs the rail width, which is what makes the rail's layer (not the chevron's) load-bearing.
- `.hidden beats id-selector display rules` — `.hidden { display: none !important }` must keep winning over the `#nav-expand` id rule, or the chevron shows while the sidebar is open.
- `wireNavCollapse wires both directions and persists the state` — collapse→`apply(true)`, expand→`apply(false)`, plus the localStorage read and write.

## Related
Issue #7 ("Collapsed-nav expand control rendered as a workspace chip in the rail") is the change that moved the chevron out over `#main` and created the exposure.

issues.name: Clicking a select / multiselect / workflow cell opens the entity instead of the picker
Computed and read-only fields are styled like editable ones
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "formula, system or uneditable table fields should somehow be differentiated so they are not confused with selectable editable fields."

## Pain point
Lookup, rollup, formula and document cells render as plain text in cells that look identical to editable ones. In a grid where the neighbouring cells are click-to-edit inputs and click-to-pick chips, a user reasonably clicks a rollup expecting something to happen — and (before the sibling picker-cell fix) got navigated to the entity page instead, which reads as a broken control rather than a read-only value.

## Reproduction
1. Open `Quality/Suite` in Table view — `Case Count` is a rollup, `Description` is a document.
2. Nothing distinguishes those cells from `Name` (text input) or a workflow chip: same background, same body colour, same pointer cursor inherited from `.entity-row`.

## Root cause
`editorFor` returned `<span class="computed">` for lookup/rollup/formula, and a second bare `.computed` span for documents. `.computed` had exactly one style rule in the whole sheet — `.computed .wv-tag { … }` for the type badge, which is only appended when `compact` is false, i.e. never in grid view. In compact (grid) rendering the read-only value was completely unstyled.

## Fix
Read-only types are enumerated once and get three signals — a shaded cell, a muted colour, and an inline glyph naming the computation:

```js
const READONLY_FIELD_TYPES = ['lookup', 'rollup', 'formula', 'document'];

function computedMark(type) {
  return { formula: 'ƒ', rollup: 'Σ', lookup: '↗', document: '¶' }[type] ?? '·';
}
```

```css
.wv-grid td.cell-computed { background: var(--tblr-bg-surface-secondary); color: var(--tblr-secondary); cursor: default; }
.computed { cursor: default; }
.computed-mark { margin-right: 5px; opacity: .55; font-size: 11px; }
```

The `title` attribute also became explicit — `"rollup — read-only"`, `"document — edit in the doc editor"` — so hovering explains *why* the cell does not respond.

Both themes checked (`data-bs-theme`): the shading resolves to `rgb(249,250,251)` on light and `rgb(17,24,39)` on dark, distinct from the row background in each, with `cursor: default` in both.

## Test coverage
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs`:
- `computed/read-only field types are enumerated once` — `READONLY_FIELD_TYPES` must contain lookup, rollup and formula.
- `computed cells are visually differentiated from editable cells` — `.wv-grid td.cell-computed` must exist, must set `cursor: default`, and must set a muted colour or shading; the `td` must carry the class and `computedMark` must exist.

issues.name: Description block wastes vertical space above every table
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "reduce size and padding for the add descriptions section."

## Pain point
The "Add description…" strip sits between the view title and the grid on every table, space and workspace page. At 13.5px with a 6px top margin — and a 60px-tall editor with 6px/8px padding once clicked — it pushed the first data row well down the page for a field that is empty on most tables.

## Root cause
Not a defect so much as untuned spacing: `.view-desc` and `.view-desc-edit` were sized like body prose rather than like the secondary metadata line they are.

## Fix
```css
.view-desc      { margin-top: 2px; font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.45; … }
.view-desc p    { margin: 2px 0; }
.view-desc-edit { min-height: 38px; padding: 4px 6px; … }
```

Before → after: `margin-top` 6px → 2px, `font-size` 13.5px → 12.5px, paragraph margin 4px → 2px, editor `min-height` 60px → 38px, editor padding 6px 8px → 4px 6px. An explicit `line-height: 1.45` keeps multi-line rendered descriptions readable at the smaller size.

The autosize floor in `viewHeader` was moved in lockstep — it duplicated the CSS min-height as a magic number:

```js
requestAnimationFrame(() => { ta.focus(); ta.style.height = Math.max(38, ta.scrollHeight) + 'px'; });
```

## Test coverage
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` → `the description block is compact`: bounds `margin-top ≤ 3px`, `font-size ≤ 12.5px`, editor `min-height ≤ 40px` and `padding ≤ 4px`, and asserts the JS autosize floor **equals** the CSS `min-height` so the two cannot drift apart again.

issues.name: The # id column is allocated a full column of width
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "too much space for #ID", with a screenshot of the grid showing `#1 ↗`, `#2 ↗`, `#3 ↗` right-aligned at the far edge of a wide, mostly empty first column. (The pasted image could not be exported from the chat transcript to disk; an equivalent capture of the same view is attached as evidence instead.)

## Pain point
The first grid column holds a short `#12 ↗` permalink and nothing else, but the table handed it a proportional share of the width. The value was also right-aligned, so it floated far from the left edge with a wide gap between it and the Name column — the space read as a rendering error rather than a layout choice, and it came straight out of the Name column, which is the one that actually needs room.

## Reproduction
Open any table in Table view. Measured on `Development/Issue` at a 1280px viewport: id cell width **139.7px** before, **59.0px** after — ~80px per table returned to Name.

## Root cause
The id cell was emitted as `el('td', { class: 'num' }, …)`, reusing the numeric-cell class. `.wv-grid td.num { text-align: right }` is right for actual numbers and wrong for a fixed-width id link, and neither the `<th>` nor the `<td>` constrained the column, so the table's auto layout distributed spare width into it.

## Fix
The id column gets its own semantic class on both header and cell, and collapses to its content:

```js
el('th', { class: 'pid-head' }, '#')
el('td', { class: 'pid-cell' }, el('a', { class: 'open-link', … }, `#${item.publicId} ↗`))
```

```css
/* The id column carries a short "#12 ↗" link — collapse it to its content
   instead of letting the table hand it an equal share of the width. */
.wv-grid th.pid-head, .wv-grid td.pid-cell { width: 1%; white-space: nowrap; text-align: left; padding-right: 6px; }
```

`width: 1%` is the standard auto-layout idiom for "shrink to content" — the table cannot honour 1% without clipping the content, so it falls back to the content width and gives the remainder to the other columns.

## Test coverage
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` → `the # column shrinks to its content and is left-aligned`: asserts `width: 1%`, `white-space: nowrap` and `text-align: left` on `.wv-grid td.pid-cell`, `width: 1%` on `.wv-grid th.pid-head`, that `app.js` emits `class: 'pid-cell'`, and that the old `class: 'num'` id cell is gone.

issues.name: Repeated “+ New space” / “+ New table” clicks stack blank inputs
First workspace rail chip is not aligned with the sidebar wordmark
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "shift workspace leftmost nav chips up so that the center of the first weave workspace is inline with the centreline of the weave wordmark."

## Pain point
The rail and the sidebar are the two things the eye reads first, and their top items did not share a baseline — the weave chip sat 7px below the wordmark it sits beside, which reads as a misalignment rather than a deliberate offset.

Measured at a 1280×800 viewport:

```
wordmark centreline: 25.0px   (#sidebar padding-top 14 + 22px line box / 2)
chip centreline:     32.0px   (#ws-rail padding-top 12 + 40px chip / 2)
```

## Fix
The rail's top padding is now derived from the three values it has to line up with, rather than being an independent constant:

```css
/* Top padding centres the first (weave) chip on the sidebar wordmark:
   #sidebar padding-top (14px) + half the .ws-wordmark line box (22px)
   − half the .ws-weave chip (40px) = 5px. */
#ws-rail { …; padding: calc(14px + 22px / 2 - 40px / 2) 0 12px; }
```

Bottom padding stays at 12px — only the top is load-bearing. Re-measured after: both centrelines at **25.0px**.

## Test coverage
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` → `the first rail chip is centred on the sidebar wordmark`: extracts the `calc()` terms, asserts they are the real sidebar padding, wordmark line-height and chip height (not hard-coded twins), then asserts the two centrelines compute equal. Changing any of the three inputs without updating the calc fails the test.

issues.name: Static UI assets are served without cache headers, so edits need a hard reload
issues.description:
**Found:** 2026-08-16, while verifying UI changes in a live browser.

## Pain point
`/app.js` and `/style.css` were served with **no `Cache-Control` header at all** — only uploaded files got `no-cache`. With no explicit freshness and no ETag, browsers fall back to heuristic caching and keep serving the previous copy, so an edit to the UI appears not to have taken effect.

This cost real time: a live page reported `showPopover.toString().includes('focusAt') === false` — the function in the running page did not contain code that `curl` proved was in the served file. Every keyboard-navigation check against that page was measuring stale code. Anyone developing the UI hits this on their first edit, and the symptom (the feature silently "not working") points at the feature rather than at the cache.

## Reproduction
1. `curl -sD- -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:4400/app.js` → no `Cache-Control` in the response.
2. Load the UI, edit `public/app.js`, reload normally → old behaviour persists until a cache-bypassing reload.

## Fix
`src/server.js`, static branch:

```js
// no-cache, not no-store: the browser may keep a copy but must revalidate.
// Without it heuristic caching serves a stale app.js or style.css after an
// edit, so UI changes only appear on a hard reload.
return send(200, readFileSync(full), {
  'Content-Type': MIME[extname(full)] ?? 'application/octet-stream',
  'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
});
```

`no-cache` rather than `no-store`: the browser may still hold a copy, it just has to revalidate before using it — right for a local-first app that is edited while running.

## Test coverage
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` → `static UI assets are served revalidating`: boots a real server on an ephemeral port and asserts `cache-control: no-cache` on `/app.js`, `/style.css` and `/index.html`.

issues.name: MCP serverInfo.version is hardcoded 0.1.0, not the package version
issues.description:
Found while documenting the MCP surface for the repo-discoverability pass (Feature#79).

`src/mcp.js` reports the server version in the initialize handshake as a string literal:

```js
serverInfo: { name: 'weave', version: '0.1.0' },
```

`package.json` is at `0.3.0`. Any MCP client that surfaces or logs the server version — or that gates behavior on it — sees a version that has been wrong since 0.2.0. The README and AGENTS.md now advertise the MCP server as a headline feature, so the handshake is more visible than it was.

**Fix shape:** read the version from `package.json` (or a single exported constant) rather than repeating it, so it cannot drift again. Lands with a test asserting the handshake version matches the package version.

## Fixed 2026-08-21 (commit bf48425, v0.4 Phase 1)
serverInfo.version now reads package.json at module load; the handshake test asserts it matches.

issues.name: Board card titles clip mid-word with no ellipsis
issues.description:
Found while capturing README screenshots for Feature#79.

On the board view, a card title longer than the card width is cut off at the card edge **mid-word, with no ellipsis and no wrap** — e.g. Development/Feature #1 renders as `Core engine: tables, relations` with the text visibly severed, and #5 as `Automations incl. outgoing w`. The table view truncates the same titles more gracefully.

Visible in `docs/screenshots/board.png`, which is now the board screenshot in the README — so this is on the first page a visitor sees.

**Fix shape:** the card title needs either `text-overflow: ellipsis` with `overflow: hidden` on a single line, or a 2-line clamp. Whichever is chosen should match how the table view truncates, so the two views agree. Both themes to be checked.

## Fixed 2026-08-21 (commit 9e58338, v0.4 Phase 1)
.card-name (the board card title input) gains overflow hidden + text-overflow ellipsis + nowrap — long titles trail off instead of clipping mid-word. UI-contract test asserts the rule; verified live on :4400.

issues.name: Relation targets reject qualified Table#pid refs (only bare #pid, uuid, or name)
issues.description:
Found while linking Quality Cases to their Suite during the repo-discoverability pass (Feature#79).

`engine.findEntity(dbRef, ref)` — the resolver behind every relation target — accepts a UUID, a bare public id (`18` or `#18`), or an exact name, but **not** the qualified `Table#18` form. Everywhere else in weave (`get`, `state`, `doc`, document mentions, the REST entity routes) the qualified form is the canonical way to name an entity.

Verified against `Quality/Case` → `Suite`:

| Target ref | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `#18` | accepted |
| `Screenshots` (name) | accepted |
| `1d912ee4-…` (uuid) | accepted |
| `Suite#18` | **rejected** — `weave: error: Related entity 'Suite#18' not found` |

This hits `weave link` on the CLI, relation values passed to `create` / `update --values`, and the `weave_link` MCP tool — all of which route through `#normalizeRelationInput` → `findEntity` (src/engine.js:652, src/engine.js:480).

**Why it matters now:** the ref contract is advertised as universal in the CLI help ("Refs: entities accept `Table#publicId`…"), in the README, and in the new `AGENTS.md` — an agent that reads those docs and passes `Suite#18` to `weave_link` gets a not-found error for a ref that resolves fine everywhere else. It is also a silent trap: the failure looks like a missing entity, not a malformed ref.

**Fix shape:** have `findEntity` strip a leading `Table` / `Space/Table` prefix when it matches the target table (and reject it when it names a *different* table, which is a genuine error worth reporting clearly). Lands with tests covering all four ref forms against a relation target, plus the mismatched-table case.

Until it is fixed, `AGENTS.md` documents the exception.

## Fixed 2026-08-21 (commit 7a643fe, v0.4 Phase 1)
findEntity resolves qualified `Table#pid` / `Space/Table#pid` refs when the named table IS the target table — a qualified ref naming a different table falls through to name matching rather than resolving by pid (guards against cross-table pid hits). Covered in test/entity-refs.test.mjs incl. the link path.

issues.name: Deleting a table orphaned its soft-deleted rows, crashing the trash
issues.description:
Introduced and fixed the same day (2026-08-16, commits `76bac93` → `4b6a48f`).

Soft delete (Feature #70) made `deleteEntity` recoverable by default. `deleteTable` called it in a loop before removing the table, so its rows were **trashed rather than purged** and survived their own table — entities left in state with a `dbId` pointing at nothing.

Any read of the trash then died:

```
listTrash CRASH: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fieldOrder')
```

`readEntity` looks up `state.tables[e.dbId]` and walks its `fieldOrder`. `deleteSpace` inherited the bug, since it delegates to `deleteTable`.

**Fix.** Dropping the container is not a soft delete — there is nothing left to restore into. `deleteTable` now iterates `listEntities(db.id, { includeDeleted: true })` and purges with `{ hard: true }`, so already-trashed rows go too.

**Guard.** Two regression tests in `test/soft-delete.test.mjs`: "deleting a table purges its rows, live and trashed alike" and "deleting a space purges every row it contained".

issues.name: Space fold caret is an 18px text glyph, below the chrome's icon standard
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "space carrots are still too small and the wrong design".

## Pain point
The space fold control in the left nav was a `▾` text glyph at `font-size: 12px` inside an 18px box, trailing the space label. Two separate faults:

1. **Hit target.** 18×18 is below the 24px floor the rest of the chrome uses, and the glyph itself painted ~7px of ink — it read as a speck, not a control.
2. **Design.** A font glyph cannot match the stroke weight, cap style or optical size of the surrounding Tabler chrome, which is stroked-icon throughout. It also sat *after* the label, so with variable-length space names the carets never lined up in a column.

## Fix
- New shared `chevron()` helper in `public/app.js`: a stroked SVG chevron (`viewBox 0 0 24 24`, `stroke-width 2`, round cap/join, `currentColor`) — the Tabler house shape, sized from its CSS box rather than a font metric.
- `.nav-caret` is now 24×24 with a 15px glyph, `flex-shrink: 0`, and **leads** the space label (standard disclosure position), so caret centres line up down the whole nav regardless of name length.
- Added `aria-expanded` (it was a button with no state), a `:focus-visible` ring, and a hover that also lights on row hover.

## Verification
- `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` +3 cases: 24px minimum target, drawn-chevron-not-glyph (with round caps asserted at the definition), caret precedes the label.
- Live (Chrome, light + dark): caret measures 24×24, contains an `<svg>`, is `parentElement.firstElementChild`; click folds `4 → 2` visible tables, `transform: matrix(0,-1,1,0,0,0)` (−90°), `aria-expanded` flips `true → false`, second click restores 4.
- Full suite 182/182 green.

issues.name: Rail loads with a doubled gap: an empty #ws-list still eats flex gaps
issues.description:
**Reported:** 2026-08-16 UAT (Kyle) — "sometimes the page loads with too much padding on the leftmost workspace nav".

## Pain point
Intermittent — the workspace rail loaded with a visibly oversized gap under the brand mark, then the chips settled. The intermittency is the tell: it is a load-time layout shift, not a static padding error (`#ws-rail` top padding is a literal `calc()` of constants and measured a stable `2px` across six cold loads on three routes).

## Root cause
`#ws-list` is populated by an async workspace fetch, but it is a **flex item of `#ws-rail` from first paint**. `#ws-rail` spaces its chips with `gap: 8px`, and an empty flex item still consumes a gap on *each* side — so while the fetch is in flight the rail carries 16px of dead space under the mark instead of 8px, and everything below it is parked high.

Measured live (`#ws-new` top, 1280×800):

```
#ws-list empty      → 64px   (mark bottom 48 + 8 gap + 0 + 8 gap)
#ws-list populated  → 140px
```

So the "+" chip also jumps 76px when the fetch lands.

## Fix
```css
#ws-list:empty { display: none; }
```
One declaration — `display: none` removes it from the flex flow entirely, so it stops claiming gaps until it has content.

## Verification
- `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` +1 case: the rail spaces with `gap`, therefore `#ws-list:empty` must be `display: none`.
- Full suite 182/182 green.

issues.name: A throwing mention resolver killed the whole document render
issues.description:
Found and fixed while writing the reference test suite (2026-08-16, commit `0efa36b`).

`renderMarkdown` called the mention resolver without a guard, so an exception from the resolver escaped and took down the **entire** document — not just the bad reference. Every surface that renders markdown shares that path: `POST /api/markdown`, `/e/:id/doc.html`, and the PDF writer.

This was reachable in practice. The resolver reaches into workspace state and `findTable` throws on an ambiguous bare name — two tables called `Task` in different spaces, and any document containing `[[table:Task]]` would fail to render. The server's own resolver had a `try/catch`, but a renderer must not depend on every caller being careful; `renderMarkdown` is exported and callable directly.

**Fix.** The resolver call is wrapped at the parser boundary. A throwing resolver now falls through to the same broken chip as a null result, and the rest of the document renders.

**Guard.** `test/references.test.mjs` → "a resolver that throws does not take the document down", which asserts the text before and after the bad reference still renders.

issues.name: Number cells paint the browser native stepper chip
issues.description:
Kyle (2026-08-16, screenshot in chat): focusing a number cell showed Chrome rounded up/down stepper chip inside the field.

It is UA chrome, not Tabler chrome: it ignores the --tblr-* tokens, floats over the cell right padding, and duplicates typing + arrow keys, which already work on input[type=number].

Fix: public/style.css suppresses it in both engines - input[type=number]::-webkit-inner-spin-button / ::-webkit-outer-spin-button { -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; margin: 0 } and input[type=number] { -moz-appearance: textfield; appearance: textfield }.

Guarded by test/ui-contract.test.mjs -> "number inputs show no native spinner chip".

issues.name: Webhook automation test is flaky under a busy port range
issues.description:
Observed 2026-08-16 during the Feature #41/#42 work: `node --test test/**/*.test.mjs` failed once on extras.test.mjs -> "webhook automation fires on state change" while preview servers were being started and stopped in the same minute. Three immediately following full runs were green (211/211), and extras.test.mjs alone is green.

The test stands up a listener on an ephemeral port; the likely cause is a port collision or a fire-and-forget webhook POST racing the assertion rather than a defect in the automation itself. Worth pinning the listener to a fixed-free port or awaiting the delivery before asserting, so a busy machine cannot redden the suite.

## Fixed 2026-08-21 (commit c984726, v0.4 Phase 1)
The webhook assertion polls received.length to a 5s deadline (25ms steps) instead of one fixed 150ms sleep — a busy machine can hold the fire-and-forget fetch past any single beat. Port was never the issue: the listener already binds ephemeral (listen(0)).

issues.name: npm test ran a different, broken command from CI
issues.description:
**Found:** 2026-08-16 while validating before a merge to main.

## Pain point
`npm test` — the entry point a new contributor to a public repo types first — ran a *different command* from CI and every doc, and it was broken:

```
npm test                          → 1 test, 0 pass, 1 fail
node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'  → 225 pass, 0 fail
```

## Root cause
`package.json` had `"test": "node --test test/"`. The bare path resolves `test` as a module specifier, so Node picks up a **`test.json` beside the repo root** — a gitignored workspace data file that the README's own quickstart can create — loads it as a test module, and the whole run dies before a single suite executes:

```
TypeError [ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING]: Module ".../weave/test.json"
needs an import attribute of "type: json"
```

Meanwhile `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` all specify the glob form. **CI stayed green the entire time because CI never used the npm script** — so the one broken path was the only one a newcomer would take, and nothing in the pipeline could see it.

## Fix
Point the script at the documented command, and pin all five surfaces together with a test that asserts `package.json`, the CI workflow, README, CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS.md name the same string. Drift now fails the suite.

## Lesson
A convenience alias for a validated command is a second, unvalidated command. Either CI runs the alias, or a test asserts the alias equals what CI runs.

Commit `1ab05d7`. Suite 226/226 green via both invocations; CI green on main.

issues.name: Idle inline-edit cells cast a Tabler input shadow with nothing to cast it
issues.description:
## Report (Kyle, 2026-08-16)

"weird shadows under text fields, fix this" — screenshot of the Development/Feature table, row #13, showing a faint dark line hugging the underside of the Name cell.

(Screenshot was pasted in chat; no file bytes were available to attach a copy at record time.)

## Root cause

Tabler's `.form-control` sets `box-shadow: var(--tblr-shadow-input)` = `0 1px 1px rgba(31,41,55,.06)`.

`public/style.css` `.inline-edit` deliberately strips the chrome off a grid cell so it reads as plain text:

```css
.inline-edit { border-color: transparent; background: transparent; }
```

It never reset the shadow. So an idle cell had a transparent border and a transparent background but still cast a 1px drop shadow — a smudge under the text with no visible object above it. Measured live on Development/Feature before the fix:

| property | computed |
|---|---|
| border-color | rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) |
| background-color | rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) |
| box-shadow | rgba(31, 41, 55, 0.06) 0px 1px 1px 0px |

## Fix

```css
.inline-edit:not(:focus) { box-shadow: none; }
```

Scoped to `:not(:focus)` on purpose: Tabler's focus ring rides the same property (`.form-control:focus` → `var(--tblr-shadow-input), 0 0 0 .25rem rgba(primary,.25)`), so an unscoped `box-shadow: none` would have silently removed the focus indicator from every cell.

## Verification (live, :4400)

| state | box-shadow |
|---|---|
| idle, light | none |
| idle, dark | none |
| focused (real click) | rgba(31,41,55,.06) 0 1px 1px, rgba(6,111,209,.25) 0 0 0 4px + primary border |

Note: `:focus` does not match while the browser pane window is unfocused — the focused-state reading required a real click, not `el.focus()`.

## Test

`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` → "an idle inline-edit cell casts no shadow". Asserts both halves: the reset exists on `.inline-edit:not(:focus)`, and it is NOT declared unscoped on `.inline-edit` (which would kill the focus ring). Full suite green: 227 pass / 0 fail.

issues.name: The entity ⋮ sat in the upper-left corner while every other view puts it at the right end of the title row
issues.description:
## Report (Kyle, 2026-08-16)

"why is this menu in a different place on the table vs entity view. raise an issue and fix" — screenshot of the entity page's upper-left corner, showing the sidebar-collapse chevron `‹` with the entity `⋮` sitting immediately to its right, above the breadcrumb.

(Screenshot was pasted in chat; no file bytes were available to attach a copy. `before.png` / `after.png` attached to this record reproduce the two states from the live app at 1280px.)

## Root cause

Every view built by `viewHeader()` — table, board, list, space — renders a crumb row and then a `.wv-toolbar.view-title-row` whose trailing element is the `⋮`. The entity page never used `viewHeader()`; it hand-rolled its own header and pinned the same control to the upper-**left** corner of `#main`:

```js
], { title: 'Entity actions', extraClass: 'entity-dl-corner' });
main.append(
  dlBtn,
  el('div', { class: 'crumb crumb-offset' }, …),
  el('div', { class: 'entity-head' }, nameInput),
);
```

```css
.entity-dl-corner { position: absolute; top: 6px; left: 2px; z-index: 25; }
.crumb-offset { margin-left: 26px; }   /* only existed to clear the corner button */
```

Measured live on `Development/Issue` at 1280px, offsets from `#main`'s box:

| view | ⋮ left | gap to right edge | ⋮ top | on the title row? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| table (`#/table/…`) | 1178 | 32 | 47 | yes (title top 42) |
| entity (`#/entity/…`) | 2 | 1208 | 6 | no (title top 52) |

1176px apart, and on a different row from the title. The same control, two places.

## Fix

The entity header becomes the shape `viewHeader()` builds — a `.view-header` block holding a crumb row and a toolbar row that ends in the menu:

```js
], { title: 'Entity actions', align: 'right' });
main.append(
  el('div', { class: 'view-header' },
    el('div', { class: 'crumb' }, …),
    el('div', { class: 'wv-toolbar entity-head' }, nameInput, dlBtn)),
);
```

```css
.entity-head { align-items: center; margin-bottom: 0; }        /* was baseline / 4px */
.entity-head input.name-edit { flex: 1; min-width: 0; max-width: 640px; }  /* was width: 100% */
.entity-head .dl-wrap { margin-left: auto; }
```

`.entity-dl-corner` and `.crumb-offset` are deleted — the second only ever existed to indent around the first.

Two details that are load-bearing:

- `align: 'right'` on the `dotsMenu` call. A right-edge trigger with a left-aligned panel drops the panel off-screen; this is the same flag the table and space menus already pass.
- `flex: 1; min-width: 0` instead of `width: 100%` on the name input. At `width: 100%` the input consumes the whole flex line and `flex-wrap` pushes the ⋮ onto a second row.

## Verification (live, 1280px)

Both views measured in the same page session, offsets from `#main`:

| metric | table | entity | before (entity) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ⋮ gap to right edge | 32 | 32 | 1208 |
| ⋮ top | 47 | 47 | 6 |
| title top | 42 | 42 | 52 |
| crumb top / left | 20 / 26 | 20 / 26 | 20 / 52 |
| ⋮ centred on the title row | yes | yes | no |

Pixel-identical. The open panel lands at x 1070–1248 in a 1280 viewport — on-screen, as `align: 'right'` intends. Re-measured with `data-bs-theme="dark"`: same geometry, button colour `rgb(107, 114, 128)`.

## Test

`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` → "the entity ⋮ sits at the right end of the title row, like every other view". Asserts the corner rules are gone from both files, that the ⋮ is the trailing child of the entity head row inside a `.view-header`, that `.entity-head` aligns like `.wv-toolbar`, that `margin-left: auto` is what pushes the menu right, and that the call site passes `align: 'right'`.

The pre-existing case "the entity menu sits in the corner with a vertical ellipsis" encoded the defect as a contract — its corner-geometry half is removed and the surviving glyph half is now "the overflow menu is a vertical ellipsis".

Full suite green: 228 pass / 0 fail.

issues.name: Boot painted the first frame before the theme was applied
issues.description:
Found while shipping Feature #45.

`wireThemeToggle()` ran **after** `withPageLoader(() => loadSchema().then(renderRoute))`, so the first render happened with no `data-bs-theme` on `<html>`.

Anything that reads the theme on every paint recovered silently. Anything that reads it **once, when it is built**, was born light and stayed light under a dark page:

| Symptom | Measured (dark page, body rgb(17,24,39)) |
| --- | --- |
| mermaid diagram inside a document | node fill rgb(236,236,255), label rgb(51,51,51) — the light palette |
| editor chrome | recovered, because `retheme()` calls `setTheme` on toggle — which does not re-render an existing SVG |

Fix: `wireThemeToggle()` moved above the first render. After: node fill rgb(31,32,32), label rgb(204,204,204).

Guarded by "the theme is applied before the first render" in `test/vditor.test.mjs`, which asserts the boot ordering rather than the symptom.

issues.name: Autosave writes one activity entry per typing pause
issues.description:
Surfaced by Feature #45. Every 600ms debounce flush writes a `doc-updated` activity row, so the Activity panel fills with identical "Description document updated" lines — a few minutes of smoke testing produced 7 in a row.

The activity log is meant to be a history worth reading. Per-pause granularity makes it a keystroke log.

Options worth weighing:
- Coalesce consecutive `doc-updated` entries for the same entity+field inside a time window (say 5 minutes) into one row, updating its timestamp.
- Or record document edits as a session: first write opens the entry, later writes within the window extend it.

Not urgent — it is noise, not data loss. Filed so the editor rollout to grid/board/list (many editors, many pauses) does not multiply it first.

## Fixed 2026-08-21 (commit 7a643fe, v0.4 Phase 1)
#logActivity folds a doc-updated landing right after another doc-updated for the same field (10-min window) into the prior entry, in place — preserving entityId:index activity ids. The coalesced entry keeps the session-start prevLength, so delta spans the whole editing session. Engine test covers coalescing + window expiry.

issues.name: POST /entities silently drops flat field values (PATCH accepts them)
issues.description:
## What happens

`POST /api/tables/:table/entities` passes the request body straight to `createEntity(dbRef, input)` (`src/server.js:339`), which only ever reads `input.values`, `input.name`, `input.doc` and `input.docs` (`src/engine.js:591-616`). Any field named at the top level is **silently discarded** and the call still returns **201** with a blank entity.

`PATCH /api/entities/:id` is lenient about exactly the same shape — `weave.updateEntity(m[1], body.values ?? body)` (`src/server.js:365`). So the write path accepts flat values and the create path does not, with no error either way.

## Reproduction (live, 2026-08-17)

```
POST /w/weave/api/tables/Case/entities
{"Name":"a resized column survives a reload","Status":"Passing","Suite":"d89e9a9b-…"}

201 Created
{"publicId":331,"fields":{"Name":null,"Description":"","Status":"Passing","Suite":null}}
```

`Name` and the `Suite` relation are gone. `Status` is *not* evidence the payload landed — `"Passing"` is the workflow's default state, which would have been set for an empty body too.

The identical PATCH with `{"values":{…}}` populated all three fields correctly.

## Why this matters

It is silent data loss on the primary create path, and it has already happened in this workspace: **Feature #66** is a blank row (`Name: null`, `Description: ""`, `Status: planned`) created 2026-08-16T19:26:52Z with nothing but a `created` activity entry — the exact signature of a flat-payload create. Agents writing through REST are the most likely victims, since the 201 reads as success.

## Suggested fix

Make create as lenient as update — in `createEntity`, treat unrecognized top-level keys as values (`input.values ?? rest`), mirroring `body.values ?? body`. The stricter alternative (reject unknown top-level keys with a 400) also closes it, but breaks anyone already relying on `name`/`doc`.

Either way it wants a server test asserting a flat-payload create either lands its values or fails loudly — never 201-with-nothing.

## Found while

Verifying Features #41 / #42 (column drag-reorder and drag-resize) end to end.



## Fixed 2026-08-17 — commit `d0037f7`

Create is now as forgiving as update. `createEntity` keeps a documented key set (`values`, `name`, `doc`, `docs`); **everything else in the input object is treated as a field value**, so a flat `{Name, Estimate}` POST behaves like the flat PATCH that already worked. An explicit `values` still wins when both are supplied, matching the existing precedence where `input.name` loses to `values.Name`.

A misspelled field no longer disappears. It reaches `#applyValues` and throws `not-found`, so **POST and PATCH now answer a bad field identically** (404 naming the field) instead of one 404-ing and the other returning 201-with-nothing.

### Verified on the running instance

The original repro payload, replayed against :4400 after the restart:

```
POST /w/weave/api/tables/Case/entities
{"Name":"POST /entities accepts a flat body, like PATCH does","Status":"Passing","Suite":"d89e9a9b-…"}

201 Created  → #363
fields: {"Name":"POST /entities accepts a flat body, like PATCH does",
         "Status":"Passing","Suite":{"name":"Engine",…}}
```

Name and the relation both land. That row is this fix's own Quality case.

### Coverage

Two cases, both new:
- `createEntity accepts values at the top level` — Engine suite (flat create, precedence when both shapes are given, reserved keys still reserved, typo throws)
- `POST /entities accepts a flat body, like PATCH does` — Server suite (201 + re-read from the server, and create/update agreeing on a bad field)

Suite green at the commit: 257 tests, 0 failures (1 pre-existing skip — `slash commands (browser)`, playwright not installed).

### Still outstanding

**Feature #66** is still the blank row this bug produced. It needs its real content or deletion — the fix stops new blanks, it does not backfill the one already there.

issues.name: Slash menu inserted empty blocks for every line-prefix command
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle 2026-08-16: "code blocks broken".

Every **line-prefix** command in the slash menu produced nothing usable, because the menu inserted a bare marker with no content. Round-tripped through Lute:

| Command | Inserted | Stored markdown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | `# ` | `"#\n"` — trailing space trimmed, no heading |
| Quote | `> ` | `"\n"` — vanished |
| Bulleted / Numbered / Task list | `- ` etc. | `"\n"` — vanished |
| Code block | ```` ```\n\n``` ```` | empty fence, collapsed |

Inline commands (bold, italic, code, link, table, mermaid) were unaffected — they carry placeholder text, so the construct had content to survive on.

**Fix:** every line-prefix command now inserts placeholder content (`# Heading`, `> Quote`, `- List item`, ```` ```\ncode\n``` ````). The block is real and visible, and the writer types over it.

**Second defect, same report:** `dist/js/highlight.js/third-languages.js` was pruned out of the vendored tree but Vditor requests it immediately after `highlight.min.js`, so every document containing a code block issued a 404. Now vendored (21KB).

**Why no test caught it:** every editor contract was asserted at source level. What a menu item produces depends on Lute, contenteditable and Vditor IR reconciliation — none of it inferable from reading app.js. Now covered by `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`, which drives a real browser through all 17 block commands plus the entity link.

issues.name: Code blocks are not syntax highlighted inside the editor
issues.description:
Split out of Issue #34 — the 404 there is fixed, this remains.

A fenced block renders correctly in the IR editor: dark surface, monospace, copy button, `class="language-js"` on the `<code>`. But highlight.js never tokenizes it — measured live, the element contains **0** `<span>` children, so every token is one colour.

State when measured (after vendoring `third-languages.js`, so nothing 404s):

| Signal | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `typeof window.hljs` | `object` — the library loaded |
| `highlight.min.js` | 200, 1,025KB |
| `styles/github.min.css` | 200 |
| `<code>` class | `language-js` |
| `<span>` count inside `<code>` | 0 |

Unclear whether Vditor deliberately leaves IR code blocks untokenized (they are editable text under the cursor) or whether the highlight pass needs an option we are not passing. weave documents were never highlighted before the editor either — `renderDocumentPage` emits plain `<pre><code class="language-x">` — so this is a missing improvement, not a regression.

Worth one look at Vditor `preview.hljs` options before concluding it is by design.

## Fixed 2026-08-21 (commit 3138628, v0.4 Phase 4)
Diagnosis overturned the report: hljs was never broken — Vditor highlights the rendered preview and deliberately leaves the editable marker-pre plain under the caret. The zero-span measurements traced to weave's own slash menu inserting a bare fence (plaintext fallback). Fix: slash Code block seeds a language, and rendered document pages now load vendored hljs when language-tagged code exists (theme via prefers-color-scheme). Playwright-verified; 426-test suite.

issues.name: Code block under the caret smeared its slab and rendered twice
issues.description:
Reported by Kyle with a screenshot: a focused code block showed a black rectangle over the language tag, an empty grey bar, and the block again below it.

**Cause.** Expanding an IR node sets every marker to `display: inline` (`.vditor-ir__node--expand .vditor-ir__marker`), and a code block's editable source is a `<pre>` carrying that class. Inline, its slab paints outside the line box — measured live at 1200px, the source pre sat at y=154 h=55 inside a node starting at y=167 — and the rendered `.vditor-ir__preview` stayed visible below it, so the same code appeared twice.

**Fix.** The source is `display: block` again while expanded, and the preview steps aside while its source is on screen. Three stylesheets also disagreed about the code surface (Tabler paints every `<pre>` dark, highlight.js gives `<code>` a light chip, vditor greys marker-classed elements), which left the source text unreadable while editing and a blue band across the block in dark mode; weave now sets the slab, the ink and the transparent `<code>` explicitly.

Guarded by `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` — "an expanded code block is one block, not a smear over a duplicate". Verified live in both themes, at rest and under the caret.

issues.name: Code block copy button was hidden behind pre:hover
issues.description:
Vditor ships `.vditor-copy { display: none }` and reveals it only on `.vditor-reset pre:hover` — undiscoverable, and unreachable by touch. Measured before the fix: the button existed in the DOM with a 0x0 rect.

**Fix.** Always present, upper right, quiet (.45 opacity) until hovered — in the editor, and on every rendered document page (`renderDocumentPage` builds one per `pre:not(.mermaid)`, using the clipboard API, hidden in `@media print` so PDFs never carry a button).

Guarded by `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` and `test/markdown.test.mjs`.

issues.name: The document editor showed its own scaffolding (H1/H2 gutter badges, section head)
issues.description:
Kyle: "H1 and h2 header level sections need not be visible".

Vditor labels every heading with its level in the left gutter (`.vditor-ir .vditor-reset > h2:before { content: 'H2' }`, floated into a -29px margin), and weave printed the field name above each document as a section head. Both are chrome about the document rather than the document.

**Fix.** The heading badges are removed outright (`content: none`). The section head — which also carries the collapse caret, the permalink, the downloads and the save state — keeps its space in the flow but only paints on `:hover` / `:focus-within`, so nothing shifts when it appears.

issues.name: Simultaneous boots race the WAL switch: busy_timeout was set too late
issues.description:
Observed twice 2026-08-21 while restarting :4400 and :4477 together: the second boot died with "'./uno.db' is not a SQLite database (database is locked)". Root cause: #open set `busy_timeout` AFTER `journal_mode = WAL` — and the WAL switch is exactly the statement that needs to wait when another process briefly holds the lock during its own boot.

## Fixed same day
`busy_timeout = 5000` now precedes the WAL switch. Regression test spawns three concurrent child-process boots on one workspace (the sub-ms window does not trip deterministically — the test pins the contract, the fix is SQLite semantics). Filed and fixed in the v0.4.1 update.

issues.name: Intermittent single-test failure in full suite (unreproduced, monitoring)
issues.description:
**One intermittent full-suite failure, never reproduced.** 2026-08-21 ~21:38: first full run reported `pass 425 / fail 1`; the TAP stream captured no `not ok` line (squeez-compressed output), immediate rerun 426/0. Six clean full runs since (413, 427 at HEAD in isolated worktrees; 460 on the working tree). Not the 3 editor/slash failures of 2026-08-22 — those were uncommitted editor WIP in the shared working tree.

Monitoring: if a 1-fail run recurs, capture the full TAP log to a file BEFORE rerunning (`node --test ... > log 2>&1`) and attach it here. Suspects: timing-sensitive server/browser tests (4s+ durations in editor-phase4-browser).

Filed during v0.5 P0 gate G0 so the observation survives; gates stay on isolated-worktree runs, which have never flaked.

## Fixed 2026-08-22 (commit b12e9a8)
The drop now relocates the header and every row's cell with insertAdjacentElement — nothing repaints, scroll and focus stay put; local db.fields order follows; the PATCH runs behind the gesture and only a failure redraws to truth.

**Correction 2026-08-22:** the 'Fixed' state and the reorder note above landed here by a numbering mix-up (they belong to [[Issue#42]]) — reverted to Open; this record still tracks the unreproduced full-suite flake it was filed for (see also [[Issue#44]], likely the same class).

issues.name: Column drag-reorder repaints the whole grid: clunky, flickery
issues.description:
Kyle UAT 2026-08-22: 'field table reorder works but is clunky and doesnt smoothly update without flickery refresh.' The drop handler redraws the full table; the columns should move in place (reorder DOM cells or FLIP-animate) with the schema write in the background. Relates to shipped [[Feature#41]].

## Fixed 2026-08-22 (commit b12e9a8)
Not the mechanics — the COMMIT: every resize ended in loadSchema + showDatabase, so the column snapped to auto width for the round-trip and back, reading as broken. Now: header + cells adjust inline, schema write in the background, repaint only on failure; updateField learned the date costume alongside (the uno Kickoff case). Contract test pins th.style.width + cell.maxWidth + the failure fallback.

**Correction:** the resize narrative above belongs to [[Issue#43]]. This issue's own fix (same commit b12e9a8): the drop relocates header + row cells with insertAdjacentElement — no repaint, scroll and focus stay put; local order follows; the PATCH runs behind the gesture; only failure redraws.

issues.name: Column drag-resize is broken
issues.description:
Kyle UAT 2026-08-22: 'field resize is broken — add most tests and validation for this.' Shipped as [[Feature#42]] (grip on the column edge, dblclick auto-fit); regressed or never held under current grid markup. Reproduce, fix, and pin with thorough tests (engine width validation + UI contract on grip wiring + live behavior).

## Fixed 2026-08-22 (commit b12e9a8)
Not the mechanics — the COMMIT: every resize ended in loadSchema + showDatabase, so the column snapped to auto width for the round-trip and back, reading as broken. Now the header and its cells adjust inline (th.style.width + cell maxWidth), the schema write runs in the background, and only a failure repaints. updateField also learned the date costume (found via uno Kickoff). Contract test pins the in-place commit + fallback; engine width validation already covered (min-width floor, null = auto-fit).

issues.name: Slash-command browser tests flake under the full suite
issues.description: A different slash test fails on roughly every other FULL-suite run (slash: table / bullet / number / inline across runs) while the file alone is repeatably green — the browser fixture starves under 500 concurrent tests. Same class as [[Issue#27]]. Fix shape: serialize the browser tests (concurrency 1 for that file) or a retry-once wrapper on fixture startup.

issues.name: Pickers opened inside a dialog render behind the backdrop (popover z-index 200 < modal 1050)
issues.description:
Found while building the field dialog: `.chip-pop` (the picker/menu popover) sat at z-index 200 while `#modal-back` is 1050, so a workflow state's category picker, or the relation picker in Add field, opened invisibly behind the modal — read as 'submenu nesting broken'.

Fix (6354921): `.chip-pop` z-index 1200, above modal (1050) and the new tray (1040). ui-contract test 'field dialogs open in the right-hand tray and popovers stack above it' pins the ordering.

issues.name: Column resize sticks in Safari/Firefox — the draggable header starts a native drag mid-gesture
issues.description: Kyle 2026-08-23: 'resize field is stuck in some browsers'. Cause: th is draggable (column reorder); WebKit/Gecko begin the native drag a few px into the resize and the pointer stream ends. Fixed 47ff5d1: grip captures the pointer (setPointerCapture), suspends th.draggable for the gesture, listens on the grip incl. lostpointercapture; `.col-resize { touch-action: none }`.

issues.name: Editing a field snaps the table back to the top-left
issues.description: Kyle 2026-08-23: 'editing a table fields snaps me back to the beginning of the table, fix'. Cause: the after-save showDatabase redraw reset page and grid scroll. Fixed 47ff5d1: `keepScroll()` records window scroll + the grid scroller's scrollLeft and restores them after the redraw.

issues.name: Vditor renders at most 8 slash-menu rows, hiding whole groups
issues.description:
`genHTML` in the vendored bundle caps the hint at eight rows: `e.forEach(function(e,n){if(!(n>7)){…}})`. A grouped catalogue of twenty means REFERENCE and FORMAT sit under a fold with nothing to scroll — measured: slashHint(query) returned 20 items, the DOM held 8 buttons.

**Fix.** The vendored `public/vendor/vditor/dist/index.min.js` carries a one-number patch, `if(!(n>7))` → `if(!(n>63))` (one occurrence in the file), plus weave CSS giving the panel `max-height: 68vh; overflow-y: auto` and a keydown handler that scrolls the highlighted row into view — Vditor moves the highlight on ↑/↓ but never scrolls to it.

**Pinned by a test** (`test/vditor.test.mjs`: "the vendored hint renders the whole catalogue, not the first eight rows") so a re-vendor that drops the patch fails loudly instead of silently truncating the menu.

issues.name: A raw HTML block cannot be inserted through Vditor's hint (document comes back empty)
issues.description:
Measured: picking a Raw HTML slash item that inserted `
html
` produced a document of `"\n"`. Vditor spins what it inserts through Lute in a context that drops an html block outright, while `setValue` round-trips the same markdown untouched. **Fix.** Raw HTML travels as an invisible marker (U+2063), the same mechanism the reference commands use, and the editor's input handler swaps the marker for the block with a whole-document write. The swap runs in a **microtask**: a headless page is backgrounded and Chrome throttles both timers and animation frames there, so a setTimeout/rAF swap never landed under test — and would leave the marker sitting in a real writer's document until something else woke the page. Also found while testing: the browser suite's `runSlash` read the document 120ms after Enter, which is not a clock in a backgrounded page. It now polls until the document settles.

issues.name: Entity page renders no fields at commit b7c4334
issues.description:
## Found 2026-08-23 while landing Feature #118

At commit **b7c4334** (`editor: the slash menu becomes a menu`), the entity page renders the crumb, the title and the async collection grids — and nothing else. `.entity-fields` never reaches the DOM, so no value rows, no document sections, no files. Every table is affected (checked `Decks/Deck#1` and `Product/Task#1`), and no error surfaces in the console: something between the collection loop and `left.prepend(fields)` in `renderEntityView` throws and is swallowed.

**Evidence** — pristine b7c4334 worktree served against `uno.db` on :4468:

```
/e/Deck#1  → {"fields": false, "body": "Slides3 Decks/Slide → …"}   // only the related grid
/e/Task#1  → {"task_fields": false, "n": 0}                         // nothing at all
```

The same page rendered from the working tree (the same commits **plus** the uncommitted entity-page work) is correct: `{"fields": true, "rows": 5}`. So the fix is already in someone's working copy — this is a **broken intermediate commit on main**, not a live defect. Filed because main was landed red-in-the-UI: the test suite is green at b7c4334, so nothing caught it.

**Ask:** commit the entity-page fix, and consider a UI-contract test that asserts `.entity-fields` renders for a plain entity — the suite passes today with the body missing.


## Verified fixed 2026-08-26 at HEAD (3328213)

The entity page renders. Checked live on the running instance against
`Issue#41` in the weave workspace: `.entity-fields` is in the DOM with its
field rows under it. No commit since b7c4334 touches `entity-fields` by name —
the fix rode in with the 1,311-line entity-page rework that followed it.

**The ask this ticket made is still unmet, and it is the useful half.** There
is no UI-contract test that a plain entity renders its fields:
`test/ui-contract.test.mjs` asserts `class: 'entity-fields'` with a source
regex, which is the same gate class that let a red-in-the-UI commit land green
in the first place. See [[Issue#63]] for the same lesson learned again — its
fix ships with `test/picker-browser.test.mjs`, a real-browser suite, precisely
because reading source could not see the defect. An `.entity-fields` case
belongs in that suite or one like it.

issues.name: Registry links were written once and never repaired: a field row could belong to the wrong table forever
issues.description:
## Symptom

Kyle, 2026-08-23: *"why aren't tables registered to fields and fields registered to tables?"*

They are — `Workspace/Fields` carries a `Table` relation whose inverse is `Workspace/Tables.Fields` — but in this workspace the two sides disagreed:

| Table | Real fields | Registered | Wrong |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Handbook/Guide` | 4 | 3 | `Description` missing |
| `Development/Issue` | 4 | 5 | carried Guide's `Description` row |

`Fields#2` — the row describing Guide's `Description` column — pointed at the **Issue** row. Opening a table's entity view therefore showed the wrong list of fields, in both directions.

## Root cause

`#syncTableRow` and `#syncFieldRow` wrote their parent link **only on the row-creation path**:

```js
// creation
values: { Description: …, ...(spaceRow ? { Space: spaceRow.id } : {}) }
// update path — Name and Definition only, no link
const patch = {};
if (this.entityName(row) !== f.name) patch.Name = f.name;
if (definable) patch.Definition = { type: f.type, config: f.config };
```

Two consequences:

1. A row created **mid-bootstrap**, before its parent's row existed, got no link at all (`spaceRow` falsy → the key is simply omitted) and nothing ever went back for it.
2. A link that drifted for any reason was **never repaired**, because the update path never looked at it.

The row surface guards against a *live* move (`A field cannot move between tables`, `A table cannot move between spaces yet`), so this could only enter through legacy data or a bootstrap ordering gap — and once in, it was permanent.

## Fix

- `#syncTableRow` / `#syncFieldRow` now re-assert the link on **every** sync, via a shared `#relIds(row, table, fieldName)` helper. Since `#ensureMetaTables` re-runs the syncs on every load, an affected workspace heals the first time a fixed engine opens it — this one did.
- New verbs: `registryReport()` lists drifted, missing, and orphan rows without changing anything; `rebuildRegistry()` re-runs the syncs, hard-deletes rows describing nothing, and returns `{ repaired, remaining }`.

## Tests

`test/fields-registry.test.mjs` grows 9 → 14: a field row pointed at the wrong table is repaired; a field row with no table is repaired; a table row with no space is repaired; every field of every table is registered to it and only to it (both directions); and `registryReport()` names a drifted link rather than hiding it.

## Verification

`weave.db` on open, after the fix: 0 problems, and every table's registered field list matches its schema exactly — Guide 4/4, Issue 4/4.

issues.name: Every description was indented 35px by a gutter that is not there
issues.description:
Kyle: "do not autoindent description text box."

Vditor writes `padding: 10px 35px` INLINE on the writing surface — a gutter it reserves for the heading-level badges weave removes — so a document sat 35px in from its own section head. Measured at 1200px: section head x=320, first paragraph x=355, and the stylesheet rule setting `padding: 0` never applied because an inline style outranks it.

**Fix.** `padding: 0 !important` on `.doc-editor .vditor-ir pre.vditor-reset`, pinned by a ui-contract test that checks for the !important specifically (dropping it would silently restore the indent). The document outline rail is positioned at `left: -26px` outside the editor box and is unaffected.

issues.name: A reference chip was transparent, so the literal [[…]] showed through it
issues.description:
The chip layer paints a chip over each `[[Table#12|Name]]` to hide the literal, and the CSS gives it `background: var(--tblr-bg-surface)`. It never took: the chip is an `<a class="mention mention-entity doc-ref-chip">` and `.doc-preview a.mention, .doc-ref-layer a.mention` (0,2,1 with the element selector) outranks `.doc-ref-layer .doc-ref-chip` (0,2,0). Measured computed background: rgba(6,111,209,.08) — a tint, not a ground — so the reference text and the chip label were both visible, overlapping.

**Fix.** `.doc-ref-layer a.doc-ref-chip { background: var(--tblr-bg-surface); }` — same specificity as the tint, later in the file. Found while wiring the # entity search, whose whole point is that picking a record leaves a chip behind.

issues.name: Double-click-to-fit measured the column, not its content — and the width did not hold
issues.description:
**"table resize double click does not snap to properly"** (Kyle, 2026-08-24).

Double-clicking a column's resize grip is supposed to fit the column to its content. It fitted to the width the column already had, plus 18px — so each click crept a little wider and nothing ever became readable.

## Two defects

**1. The fit could not see the content.** `fitColumnWidth` measured `cell.scrollWidth` / `inner.scrollWidth`. A grid cell clips with `max-width` + `overflow:hidden` + ellipsis, so it never reports overflow — measured live on uno Task, every column returned `scrollWidth === clientWidth`. Worse, a text cell holds an `<input>`, whose width is the browser's default box and says nothing about its value.

**2. The committed width could not hold.** Auto table layout treats a bare `width` on a header as a suggestion and squeezes it away the moment the grid is wider than its card — which is every grid with a document column. The measured fit was written to `th.style.width` and the rendered column stayed at 78px.

## Fix (commit 189a71f, Gerrit change 42)

- The column's content is cloned into an off-grid measurer (`.wv-measure`), inputs swapped for spans carrying their text and metrics, and the widest clone is the fit.
- Colspan cells (the "+ New" row, an expanded document) are skipped — they are the whole grid, not the column.
- Widths are written as `width` + `min-width` + `max-width` on the header and every cell, at render and on the in-place commit, so a resize or a fit holds.

## Evidence

Live on :4400, uno `Task.Name`: **78px → 176px**, longest value unclipped. Before/after screenshots of the grid are attached.

## Tests

`test/column-fit.test.mjs` (Playwright, skips when absent): fit covers the value without overshooting; fitting twice is idempotent; a fit holds in a grid wider than its card; the fit reaches the schema; the "+ New" row never inflates it. Three of the five were red before the change. `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` asserted `scrollWidth` — the very measurement that caused the defect — and now asserts its absence. Full suite green in an isolated worktree: 605 pass / 0 fail / 3 skipped.

issues.name: The sidebar workspace name was dead text, not a link home
issues.description:
**"allow clicking the workspace name to take you to the workspace entity page in addition to the workspace selector chip"** (Kyle, 2026-08-24).

The sidebar wordmark (`#ws-name`) was a `<span>` — dead text at the top of every page. Getting to the workspace page meant the rail chip or a breadcrumb, neither of which is where the eye goes first.

## Fix (commit da03e3a, Gerrit change 44)

- The wordmark ships as an `<a>`; `buildWsRail` sets its `href` from `wsHomeHref()`, so a non-default workspace links to `/w/<name>/` and not the hub root, and sets a title naming the workspace.
- A real href means cmd-click and middle-click open the workspace in a tab, like any other link.
- Hover and `:focus-visible` earn an underline (3px offset) and keep the wordmark's own color. The `--tblr-primary` blue that `a.nav-space:hover` uses goes muddy against the dark navy sidebar — checked in both themes, screenshots attached.

## Tests

`test/nav.test.mjs`: a real browser click from an entity page lands on the workspace page (title reads the workspace name, the page carries the workspace-wide Activity table); the wordmark is an anchor with `href="/"` and a pointer cursor; plus source contracts for the markup, the rail's href assignment, and the hover affordance. The click test was red against the `<span>`. Full suite on the staged tree: 619 pass / 0 fail / 4 skipped.

issues.name: 🎨 Outline rail: specks that scrolled away, pressed against the text
issues.description:
**Raised by Kyle, 2026-08-24**, on the entity page's document panel.

Four defects in the Issue #87 dash rail, all visible in one screenshot of a Handbook guide:

1. The rail named nothing. A dash carried its heading only in a native `title` tooltip, so the map said "where am I" and never "what is here".
2. The rail scrolled with the document instead of floating beside the reader — by the time you were three screens down, the map was three screens up.
3. The document text ran up against the gutter with no breathing room.
4. Dashes were 3px tall, up to 12px wide, and did nothing on hover.

**Fixed 2026-08-24 (commit a4a864a, Gerrit change 40, Verified +1).**

- `.doc-rail` spans its section; `.doc-rail-track` inside it is `position: sticky` at the reading line. A long map caps at the viewport and scrolls the reader's own section back into view.
- Hovering the rail opens the headings as labels; `display: none` until then, so a resting dash keeps the tick's own width and the browser test that measures dash widths still measures dashes.
- Dashes: h1 17px (was 12), 4px tall; a hovered tick grows 1.3x from its left edge.
- `.doc-section` takes an 18px `padding-left`. The fold carets were already positioned against the editor host, so they rode into the indent for free.

Gates: `test/doc-rail.test.mjs` (13 pure + contract), `test/editor-phase4-browser.test.mjs` gains "hovering the rail opens the headings themselves" and "the rail floats: scrolling leaves the track near the reading line". Full suite green in an isolated worktree.

issues.name: 🎨 Text cells spelled their markdown out loud
issues.description:
**Raised by Kyle, 2026-08-24**: "table description previews should not show raw markdown".

Space and table descriptions are markdown living in a `text` field — the description box on the space page is a markdown editor — and the registry grids painted the value straight into an `<input>`. The Spaces grid read:

```
**Official documentation and how-tos** — the pages
```

**Fixed 2026-08-24 (commit fe54365, Gerrit change 41, Verified +1).**

A text cell holding markup now wears the marks at rest and hands the source back the moment it is clicked — the pattern the formatted-number cell already used (Issue #97). `WeaveEditorLib.inlineTokens()` is the pure half: bold, italic, code, strike, links and `[[refs]]`, flat, first mark that closes wins. Every emphasis mark is flanked, so `2 * 3 * 4` stays arithmetic and `snake_case_name` stays a name.

Gate: `test/inline-text-cell.test.mjs` (6 tests).

issues.name: 🎨 A row's Docs cell described one document and hid the rest
issues.description:
**Raised by Kyle, 2026-08-24**: "documents should be shown as chips with type".

The Docs cell flattened the FIRST document field to 90 characters and printed it. A Task carrying Description, Spec and test showed a slice of one and no sign of the other two — and clicking through always opened the first field's tab.

**Fixed 2026-08-24 (commit 361660e, Gerrit change 46, Verified +1).**

Every document field is a chip: its name, then the kind of thing it holds — `md`, an `html` app, a `json` model, an `mmd` diagram — with empty ones dimmed and labelled `empty`. Clicking a chip opens that document's tab (`state.expandedDoc` remembers which one was asked for). `WeaveEditorLib.docKind()` is the pure half, reading the same signals `isHtmlDocument` already reads.

Gates: `test/doc-chips.test.mjs` (7 tests); the stale `ui-contract` assertion about the snip was rewritten, not deleted.

issues.name: PUT /api/schema drops option colors, widths, icons and formats on any edited table
issues.description:
**The declarative door loses the visual half of the schema.**

`describeSchema()` emits `width`, `optionsFull` (option colors), `icon`, `noun`, `hiddenFields`, `systemFields`, date `format`/`time`, the number costume keys, document `kind` and attachments `multiple`. `applySchema()`'s `configFromDescriptor` (src/engine.js:813) reads only `options` (names), `states`, `expression`, `via`, `targetField`, `aggregate`, `default` and `depth`.

Applying an **unedited** document is a clean no-op — verified, `plan: []`. The loss shows the moment a document is edited, because an edited field takes the `update-field` branch with a config rebuilt from the descriptor:

```
before: {"options":[{"name":"A","color":"#2ea043"}],"width":240}
edit:   options -> ["A","B"]
after:  {"options":[{"name":"A","color":""},{"name":"B","color":""}]}      <- color and width gone
```

Export-edit-apply is the natural agent workflow for standing up or amending a space, so this silently undoes deliberate visual configuration. It also cannot rename anything (a name is identity) and never writes a table icon, noun, field order or hidden fields.

Fix shape: `configFromDescriptor` carries the full descriptor through (colors from `optionsFull`, width, formats, kind, multiple, state icons), and the table branch applies `icon`, `noun`, `hiddenFields`, `systemFields` and `fieldOrder`. A round-trip test — describe, mutate one option, apply, describe — is the guard.

issues.name: A Definition write without a config key silently does nothing
issues.description:
Writing a field's `Definition` on a `Workspace/Fields` row is the agent-side door to field config (src/engine.js:1507). The honored shape is `{type, config:{...}}`. A near-miss — `{"type":"select","options":["A","B","C"]}`, which is the shape `weave_schema` hands back — passes the type check and reaches `updateField(config: def.config ?? {})` with an empty object, so the intended change is discarded and the call returns 200.

An agent gets no signal that the write did nothing. Refusing a definition that carries no `config` key (or accepting the flat descriptor shape, which is friendlier) is the fix; a silent no-op on a schema write is the worst of the three.

issues.name: A bare icon name paints the word "ticksquare" in the nav
issues.description:
Found by pointing a browser at what an agent had just configured (2026-08-24).

`weave_update_table {db:'Task', icon:'ticksquare'}` returned 200 and the nav painted the literal text **ticksquare** beside the table. The stored value is `iconly:<name>`; `iconEl` (public/app.js) matches `^iconly:(.+)$` and falls back to rendering any other string as text — which is how an emoji icon works, and which turns a bare name into a mistake no validation catches.

The vocabulary had listed bare names, so an agent reading it produced exactly this. Fixed in the same pass: `VOCABULARY.icons` is now `{form: 'iconly:<name>', fallback, names}`, the tool and CLI descriptions and AGENTS.md name the form, and a contract test holds it against `iconEl`'s regex and against the form the UI's own icon picker writes.

Verified live: `iconly:ticksquare` renders as the glyph.

**The general lesson:** a config value that validates can still read wrong. The vocabulary has to carry the *value form*, not only the legal names.

issues.name: Quality mirror drifts from the test files (names escaped, renames stale, count short)
issues.description:
Found while mirroring Feature #140's tests into Quality. The `UI contract` suite (#15, `test/ui-contract.test.mjs`) does not match `node --test` reality:

- **Count is one short.** 127 tests in the file, 126 Case rows after #140 added its two.
- **Twelve names carry a literal backslash** — `\#ws-rail carries a positive z-index…`, `board card titles truncate… (Issue \#20)` and ten more. Something escaped `#` on the way in, so those rows no longer match the test names they mirror.
- **Three names are stale renames**, mirroring tests that were renamed in place:

| Row says | The file says |
| --- | --- |
| row click on a picker cell opens the picker instead of the entity | board and related rows still route a click before opening the entity |
| picker cells advertise themselves as clickable | in the grid every cell advertises that it edits |
| the table grid previews the first document in the Docs cell | the table grid names every document in the Docs cell |

Missing outright: `a fit measures the content, not the box the column already has` (from the column-fit work).

Left alone deliberately when #140 landed — renaming rows that mirror someone else's tests is a sweep, not a side effect. The fix is a reconciliation pass: re-read every test name from every suite file and repair names, adds and counts in one go (all suites, not just this one).

issues.name: 🎫 Picker — Enter selects after typing but not after arrowing (and should it take two?)
issues.description:
> 140 issue return selects on type, for multiselect but return does not
> select on arrow, maybe prezing enter twice is the ideal pattern also for
> both item selected needs better desing and and numbering it shoudl remove
> the selected items fro the list rather than chekcing them

— Kyle, 2026-08-25, against Feature #140 (the picker token box) as shipped in f215334.

## The report

In a **multiselect** picker, Enter commits the armed option when you have typed a query, but Kyle observes it does **not** select the option he arrived at with ↑/↓. The two ways of arming the same row behave differently, which is the kind of inconsistency that makes a keyboard surface untrustworthy.

## Lead, not a diagnosis — this needs reproducing in a browser first

Reading `public/picker-core.js`, Enter resolves its target as:

```js
const pick = vis[state.active] ?? (state.query.trim() ? vis[0] : null);
```

`ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` write `state.active`, and `public/app.js` draws the armed row from that same `state.active` against the same `core.visible(st)` list — so on a source reading the two paths agree and Enter *ought* to fire after arrowing. Do not treat the code as the answer: reproduce the gesture and capture what `state.active` actually holds at the moment Enter is pressed.

One thing the source does establish: a multiselect picker **opens with nothing armed** — `blank()` sets `active: -1` unless the mode is single. So the very first Enter, with no typing and no arrowing, falls through to `{ type: 'commit' }` and closes the box. If Kyle's ↑/↓ ended back at `active: -1` (`ArrowLeft` sets it to -1 when the caret walks into the chips), Enter would commit rather than select, and that would look exactly like the reported bug.

## The proposal in the same note

> maybe pressing enter twice is the ideal pattern also for both

Worth designing rather than patching: **first Enter selects the armed option, second Enter saves and closes** — the same grammar in multiselect and in single/workflow. It removes the current split where Enter means "add" in one mode and "commit" in the other, and it gives the empty-search Enter (which already saves) a consistent sibling. Decide it against the grammar in `picker-core.js`, where it is testable as 16-odd pure cases rather than as a DOM.

## Where the work lives

- `public/picker-core.js` — `keyDown()`, the pure grammar. Any change lands here first, with cases.
- `public/app.js` — `searchPicker`, which feeds the grammar keys and runs the effect it hands back.
- `test/picker-core.test.mjs` — the existing grammar cases.


## Fixed 2026-08-26 (change 67, commit 7a1cfe8)

**Reproduced first, and the lead in this ticket was wrong.** `state.active` held
exactly what the source said it held; arrowing was never broken. On
`Product/Task#3` (`Tags: bug`), served from the working tree at :4400:

| Gesture | What happened before the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `↓` | armed row 0 — **"bug"**, the tag already set |
| `Enter` | toggled it: the field emptied |
| `↓↓` → `Enter` | armed "feature", added it correctly |

So Enter after arrowing did fire. It un-picked, because the row the arrow
landed on was one already chosen — and a chosen option sat in the list wearing
a ✓ ([[Issue#64]]). "Enter does not select on arrow" and "chosen items should
leave the list" were one defect seen from two sides.

**The fix is #64's.** `core.visible()` now drops staged options in a multi
picker, so every armed row is one you can add and Enter has a single meaning.
Un-picking is ⌫ on the chip (Kyle's call, 2026-08-26). One more trap closed on
the way: Enter on a search matching only what is already chosen used to fall
through to the save and close the picker — it now does nothing.

Because a pick disarms the list, pick-then-Enter saves. That is the "press
Enter twice" pattern this ticket floated, arrived at without charging two
keystrokes for every pick.

**Guarded by** `test/picker-browser.test.mjs` — new, and the point of it: the
gesture is driven through real key presses in Chromium. Every source-level
assertion in `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` passed while the field emptied itself.

issues.name: 🎫 Picker — a chosen option should leave the list, not sit in it wearing a tick
issues.description:
> 140 issue return selects on type, for multiselect but return does not
> select on arrow, maybe prezing enter twice is the ideal pattern also for
> both item selected needs better desing and and numbering it shoudl remove
> the selected items fro the list rather than chekcing them

— Kyle, 2026-08-25, against Feature #140 (the picker token box) as shipped in f215334.

## The report

> it should remove the selected items from the list rather than checking them

Today a multiselect picker keeps every option in the dropdown and marks the chosen ones with a `✓` (`public/app.js`: the `chip-pop-check` span). Kyle wants a chosen option to **leave the list** — it is already visible as a chip in the box above, so listing it again says the same thing twice and pushes the options you can still pick further down.

## What to settle before building

- **Removing it changes what Enter-on-a-selected-row means.** Toggling off currently happens by picking the ticked row again; if the row is gone, un-picking is only ⌫ on the chip. That may be the right trade — the chips are right there — but it should be a decision, not a side effect.
- **The list will reflow under the cursor** as options leave it. Whatever is armed has to stay armed, or arming has to move somewhere predictable, or every pick will select the wrong next thing.
- Single select and workflow are unaffected: they hold one chip and close on the pick.

## Where the work lives
