features.name: Column drag-reorder + field-settings header dialog
features.description:
## Design review — four options, 2026-08-16

Requested by Kyle: "build me a report with 4 distinct options for how to set up the UX of our field configuration panel" + "show mock ups". Full report (self-contained HTML, live mockups at weave's sampled dark tokens): `~/Documents/queue/2026-08-16-141726-weave-field-config-panel-design-review.html`. Mockup renders attached.

### Baseline observed on the running app (Product/Task)
Two surfaces behind the grid header `+`, and **neither can edit a field**:
- **Add field** — blocking modal: name input, native `<select>` of 13 bare type names, one type-dependent text input.
- **Manage fields** — full-page takeover replacing the grid: read-only Field/Type/Details table, delete only.

Seven faults the options are scored against: F1 no edit path (changing options = delete + recreate = **data loss**); F2 config is a typed mini-language (`Open:not-started, …` into a placeholder); F3 type list is 13 undescribed words; F4 managing fields costs the grid; F5 relations split into their own dialog; F6 the column header is inert; F7 no preview, no reorder.

### The four options

| | Option | Idea | Fixes | Build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Header-anchored popover | The column header is the control; add and edit share one popover | F1 F2 F3 F5 F6 (7/8) | smallest |
| B | Right-hand schema dock | Persistent inspector in the entity side-column slot; field list + config, grid re-renders live | all seven (8/8) | medium |
| C | Schema page, made editable | Keep the page but add expand-in-place rows, drag handles, staged changes applied as one migration | 6/8 — uniquely offers reviewable migrations | largest |
| D | No panel — fields are rows | Feature #52 dogfooded: a field is an entity in a space-level `Fields` table, configured with the ordinary grid | 6/8 — free comments/activity/search, one entity API | largest (engine) |

### Recommendation
**A escalating into B, on D's model.** Ship A first — smallest build, kills F1 immediately, reuses `showPopover()`/`.chip-pop` from the Issue #9 chip picker. Then grow B: a "more" row opens the same editor in the right dock where reorder and formula/rollup/lookup get real width. One editor component, two containers.

**Skip C.** Its only unique asset is staged migrations, and that value lives in the engine (a dry-run type-coercion API), not in a page — build the dry-run and surface it as an inline warning inside A/B.

**D is the storage layer, not a competitor.** Keep it on #52 and have A/B read fields through one accessor now, so fields-as-entities lands later without touching the panel.

### Open for Kyle
1. Dock on the left or the right? (Feature #82 left the same question open for the entity side column — both should match.)
2. Does a type change coerce data or refuse? Default: refuse with a row count until the dry-run exists.
3. Popover on header click, or a header `⋮`? Default: `⋮`, leaving plain click free for sort (not yet built).


### Decision — Kyle picked the hybrid (2026-08-16)

> "why cant we do both B and D? or some hybrid"

**Both, because they were never alternatives.** B is a surface, D is a model. The hybrid is one idea, not two builds: **a field is an entity, and the dock is the entity inspector pointed at it.** The entity inspector already ships (Fields → Comments → Activity, Feature #82) — point it at a `Field` row and the schema dock exists, with history, comments and restorable delete inherited rather than built.

Three surfaces over one model, sharing one `<FieldConfigEditor>` component:

| Surface | For | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Column `⋮` → dock | the 90%: rename, retype, edit config | A survives as the *gesture*; the popover itself is dropped |
| Fields table view | bulk, cross-table, filters, saved views | ordinary table view over the Fields table |
| Field entity page | docs, comments, full history | ordinary entity page |
| (Agents) | MCP · REST · CLI | same entity CRUD, no new API |

**What the hybrid resolves:** B's missing audit trail and agent path (the entity supplies both), B's lack of bulk/cross-table (the Fields view), and D's "generic grid cells are bad config editors" (the cell hosts the same editor as the dock) and D's broken gesture (column `⋮`).

**What it does not resolve:** D's bootstrap problem — the Fields table needs fields to describe fields, so one primitive engine-level descriptor must exist below the entity layer. Still the hardest part. B's width cost also remains (needs a collapse toggle).

**Sequencing — three phases, no rework:**
1. Dock on current storage. `FieldConfigEditor` per type; rename/retype/reorder. Kills the data-loss fault immediately.
2. Fields become entities. Swap the accessor's internals — dock code unchanged. Activity, comments, restore and the agent API appear without touching the panel.
3. Zoomed-out surfaces: Fields table view, saved views, bulk edit, Field entity page — free, they are ordinary views over the phase-2 model.

**The one rule that makes it cheap:** in phase 1, nothing outside a single `fieldConfig` accessor may read or write a field definition. If that holds, phase 2 is an internals swap. If it leaks, phase 2 is a rewrite and "both" really does cost B + D.

C remains skipped — its only unique asset (staged migrations) belongs in the engine as a dry-run type-coercion API, surfaced as an inline warning in the dock.

Mockups H1 (dock), H2 (Fields table), H3 (architecture) attached; full report is §5 of `field-config-design-review-v2.html`.


## Shipped 2026-08-16 — option A

Commit 8cb9647. Each column header carries a quiet ⋮ opening one popover (edit field / move left / move right / insert / hold-to-delete), reusing showPopover so it matches every other picker in the grid; the header is also a drag handle. Reorder is a schema write: engine updateTable now takes fieldOrder and refuses anything short of a full permutation, so a dragged column survives reload and no column can be dropped silently. Editing is a PATCH to /tables/:t/fields/:f — verified live on Development/Issue that adding a "Critical" option to Severity kept all 26 rows' values (fault F1 closed).

Deliberately NOT shipped: type change (still refused — needs the dry-run coercion API), and the right-hand dock (option B) which grows from this same editor. Open question 1 (dock side) stays open; question 2 answered as "refuse"; question 3 answered as ⋮, leaving plain header click for sort.

Guarded by 7 UI-contract cases.

features.name: Auto-fit + drag-resize column widths
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-16

Commit d4e6c45. Width is per-field config (engine: config.width, floor MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH = 60, null = auto), applied to both the header and its cells so the shared 260px cap cannot re-clip a widened column. The grip is the column's own right edge: drag to size, double-click to auto-fit — auto-fit clears the width and hands the column back to the browser rather than writing a measured guess. One write, on release, tracked on the window so the drag can outrun a 6px target. A test asserts the client floor equals the engine floor.

Verified live on Development/Issue: drag stored 218px and re-rendered header + cells, double-click cleared it, neither gesture sorted the column.

Guarded by 5 UI-contract cases + 1 engine case.



## Re-verified 2026-08-17 — the feature was fine, the server was stale

Reported as not working. It works; the running instance did not have it.

The long-lived server on :4400 was started **14:25:07**, and this feature landed at **14:42:51** (commit `d4e6c45`) — along with every other commit from that afternoon (`8cb9647`, `b2c7c4a`, `36f57b9`, `1ab05d7`, `8f1437a`, `c277e2a`). A 5-hour-old process was serving `public/app.js` from before the grid work existed, with nothing in the UI to say so.

The symptom read exactly like a broken write: the drag sized the column, `PATCH /fields/:id` returned **200** with `{"config":{"width":104}}`, and the re-render dropped it — because the stale server never understood `config.width` and `/api/schema` returned the field with no width at all.

Against a fresh server on the same data, both gestures are correct:

| Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drag `Status` left 60px | header `width:104px`, cells `max-width:104px` |
| Drag `Severity` before `Status` | order `Name, Severity, Status`, persisted through re-render |
| Double-click grip | width cleared, column back to auto |

This is Feature #54's territory (service management + status visibility) — a local instance that silently serves whatever it booted with is the actual defect here.

## Coverage gap closed

`a field carries a column width` only ever exercised one in-memory `Weave`, so the store was never in the loop — the width round-trip through disk had no test. Added **`a resized column survives a reload`** (`test/engine.test.mjs`), which reopens the workspace and asserts both that a width persists and that clearing it persists as auto. It passes: persistence was already correct, it was simply unguarded.

Engine suite: 21 → 22 cases, matching `node --test` (242 total, green).

Found along the way: **Issue #33** — `POST /entities` silently drops flat field values.

features.name: Date system: formats, datetime, date math, chrono-node parsing, flatpickr dialog
features.description:
## Merge note (2026-08-21, v0.4 planning)
[[Feature#78]] (smart date field: type-or-pick with natural-language parsing) folded into this record — this is the canonical date-system feature. #78's shape (input that is both editable formatted text and a calendar, per Kyle's reference screenshot) is a requirement here, alongside formats, datetime, chrono-node parsing and date math. #78 soft-deleted.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 3a1dae6, v0.4 Phase 5) — absorbed [[Feature#78]]

**Costume** (same rule as [[Feature#97]]): date config `format` (iso | us | eu | long) + `time`; display formats the stored wall-clock parts, never the local zone's reading — '2026-08-21' cannot render as Aug 20. ISO in storage, always.

**Date math in formulas:** dateadd(date, n, unit), datediff(a, b, unit), year/month/day, now() — joining today() and days().

**Type-or-pick cell** (the #78 shape): a text input that reads 'today', 'tomorrow', 'in 2 weeks', 'next friday', 'jun 21', US/EU numerics — beside a native calendar (datetime-local when the field carries time). A typed phrase names a day; an existing time of day survives it.

**Deviation, recorded:** chrono-node was the named parser but ships as an ESM module tree with a dayjs dependency and no self-contained bundle — vendoring it violates the zero-dep/no-build mandate for ~200KB where a page of code covers the phrases people actually type. nl-date.js is hand-rolled, pure, loads as a classic script AND imports into node tests (13 parser assertions). Flatpickr likewise skipped: the native picker is the 'pick' half.

Verified live: typing 'next friday' into Leads/Close Date saved 2026-08-28 and re-rendered 'Aug 28, 2026'. Suite 366/366.

features.name: Vditor edit-in-rendered-view markdown editor
features.description:
Edit-in-rendered-view ("Typora-like") markdown editing for document fields, replacing the plain `<textarea>` in the doc surfaces.

## Inkstone evaluated and rejected (Kyle asked, 2026-08-16)

[shuaiplus/inkstone](https://github.com/shuaiplus/inkstone) is a **self-hosted Markdown notebook application**, not an embeddable editor. Four blockers, any one of which is disqualifying:

| Blocker | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Not a component | No embeddable build and no standalone browser bundle — it ships accounts, folders, its own note storage, sync, sharing and AI. Adopting it means running a second product beside weave, with a second data model. |
| Cloudflare-shaped storage | D1 + R2/KV + Durable Objects + IndexedDB. weave is one local `node:sqlite` file, no cloud, no accounts. The parts that make Inkstone good — sync, search, version history — are the parts bound to Workers. |
| Build step | React + Vite + TypeScript, `npm run build`. House rule is zero runtime deps, no build step, third-party **vendored pinned** into `public/vendor/`. There is nothing prebuilt to vendor. |
| Licence | LGPL-3.0-only against weave's MIT. Shipping LGPL JS inside our own bundle carries relinking and source obligations — a licensing decision, not a technical one. |

It would also duplicate what weave already has: a markdown renderer, an FTS5 index, `[[Table#12]]` mentions, and per-entity MD/HTML/PDF documents.

Worth stealing from it as ideas, not code: typewriter mode, focus mode, split view with synchronised scrolling, and an outline pane.

## The candidate that does fit

[Vditor](https://github.com/Vanessa219/vditor) — MIT, prebuilt `dist/index.min.js` + CSS that runs from a plain `<script>` tag with no bundler, and its **IR (instant rendering)** mode *is* edit-in-rendered-view. Vendors cleanly into `public/vendor/` beside mermaid and Tabler.

Integration caveat to settle first: Vditor lazy-loads some extras (mermaid, katex) from a public CDN by default. Its `cdn` option must be pointed at the vendored copy, or a workspace that is meant to be offline and telemetry-free starts making third-party requests. Verify with the network panel before this ships.

Alternative if Vditor's weight is unacceptable: ToastUI Editor (MIT, UMD bundle, WYSIWYG + markdown modes).


## Vendoring audit (2026-08-16) — Vditor is heavier and less compatible than it looked

Measured from the published tarball, not from memory:

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Licence | MIT ✅ |
| Build step | none — `dist/index.min.js` runs from a `<script>` tag ✅ |
| Core | `index.min.js` 296 KB + `index.css` 48 KB + images 108 KB |
| **Markdown engine** | `dist/js/lute/lute.min.js` — **3.7 MB**, lazy-loaded from `options.cdn` at runtime |
| Vendored total | ~4.2 MB, against a current `public/vendor/` of 3.0 MB |

Vendoring lute is not optional: the no-telemetry rule forbids letting the editor fetch it from a public CDN.

### The blocker is not size, it is a second renderer

Vditor renders with **lute** (Go compiled to JS, shipped as one minified blob). weave renders with `src/markdown.js` — for `/e/:id/doc.html`, `.md`, `.pdf`, and `POST /api/markdown`. Adopting Vditor means the same document is parsed by two different implementations: what the editor shows and what the export produces can diverge, with no single source of truth.

Worse for the stated goal — "a live-preview always-rendered surface we implement our custom tools on top of" — the custom tool is the typed `[[…]]` reference (shipped, commit `4167eb7`). lute has never heard of `[[space:Development]]`, and it is a compiled artifact we cannot teach. In instant-rendering mode the editing surface *is* lute's DOM, so weave's own reference chips would not render in the one place they matter most.

### Recommendation: build the surface on weave's own renderer

`POST /api/markdown` already returns weave-rendered HTML and is already used for view descriptions. An always-rendered, autosaving editor over it:

- rendered HTML is the resting state; clicking a block swaps that block for a textarea; blur re-renders it
- autosave on a debounce, the way the doc textarea already saves
- `/` opens the picker in the active block and inserts `[[…]]`, which becomes a live chip on blur

What it costs: writing the block editor. What it buys: no dependency, no 4.2 MB, the editor and the export agree **by construction**, and weave's own syntax renders live — which no third-party editor can give us.

Keep as fallback if Kyle prefers a library: ToastUI Editor (MIT, UMD), which has the same two-renderer problem but a much smaller footprint.


## Surface design review — four options with mockups, 2026-08-16

Kyle asked for mockup options for the embedded editor. Full review (self-contained HTML, live mockups at weave sampled dark tokens): `~/Documents/queue/2026-08-16-153717-weave-embedded-md-editor-design-review.html`

Scored against six faults of today's `docsEditor()` textarea: E1 blind writing, E2 manual save, E3 no live `[[...]]` affordance, E4 no outline, E5 170px height in a grid row, E6 mermaid/HTML unpreviewable.

| | Option | Idea | Fixes | Build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Block-swap live editor | Rendered at rest; click a block, only that block becomes a textarea; blur re-renders; autosave; `/` picker | E1 E2 E3 E6 | largest |
| B | Split view, synced scroll | Source left, weave-rendered right, scroll-locked; textarea unchanged | E1 E6 | small |
| C | Read/Write toggle + autosave | Keep the textarea, add a segmented control, save on debounce + blur, delete the Save button | E2 E5 | hours |
| D | Vendored Vditor IR | The library route | E1 E5 E6 | closed by the vendoring audit above |

**Recommendation: ship C this week, build A behind it, keep B as a third toggle state on the entity page.** C kills the fault that actually loses work (E2) and every part of it is scaffolding A reuses. A is the only option that makes weave own `[[...]]` syntax live while writing — the whole reason not to buy an editor. D stays closed: two renderers, ~4.2 MB, and the reference chip cannot render inside lute DOM.

Build order for A, each step with the test that holds it: (1) autosave + toggle, (2) block splitter with a byte-exact split/join round-trip, (3) click-to-edit + blur re-render through `POST /api/markdown`, (4) `/` picker inserting typed references, (5) split as a third state.

Awaiting Kyle on four questions: is C enough or is A the goal; grid row vs entity page; autosave cadence; does D stay closed permanently.

## Constraint corrected by Kyle, 2026-08-16 — the surface is ALWAYS rendered

The 22:37 four-option review above is **superseded**: its options B (split view), C (Read/Write toggle) and D (Vditor) are all ruled out by the constraint as Kyle actually stated it.

> The md is always shown rendered, in the preview, even when edited. There is no edit mode, no save, and no side-by-side plaintext view. Because of this, all md-native formatting must also be accessible under the slash command.

Fibery-shaped. Superseding review (self-contained HTML, live mockups incl. the full `/` menu): `~/Documents/queue/2026-08-16-154539-weave-always-rendered-md-editor-design-review.html`

### What makes it buildable without a library

`src/markdown.js` documents its own **closed** vocabulary — headings, paragraphs, fenced code (incl. mermaid), blockquotes, hr, ordered/unordered lists with 2-space nesting, task lists, tables, raw HTML; inline bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links, images, and `[[Table#123]]` / `[[Table#123|label]]` / typed `[[space:...]]` mentions. An editor for someone else markdown must survive arbitrary syntax; an editor for ours has a finite block list — which is also exactly what the `/` menu has to offer.

### The remaining decision: where the truth lives

| | Architecture | Fidelity risk | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | HTML is the truth — contenteditable + DOM to markdown serializer | **Unbounded** — every paste, browser quirk and IME artefact becomes markdown | Cheapest to start, worst to trust |
| 2 | **Blocks are the truth** — md to typed block list, blocks to md | **Bounded** — per-block serialization against the closed vocabulary, so the round-trip test can be exhaustive | **Recommended** |
| 3 | Text is the truth — hidden syntax, Typora style | None — source IS the truth | Fails the constraint: syntax reveals on the caret line, a per-line edit mode |

### Recommendation: architecture 2 (blocks)

The only shape where "always rendered" and "correct on export" are both true by construction, and the only one where the `/` menu is not a translation layer — the menu **is** the block vocabulary. Each block type becomes a component: mermaid renders live, tables get row/column controls, a reference chip is an atomic inline node that cannot be half-deleted.

### The `/` menu is the whole formatting surface

Twenty commands in four groups — Insert (text, H1-H6, bulleted, numbered, task list, quote, code, mermaid, divider, image, raw HTML, table), Reference (entity, table, space/workspace), Format applied to the selection (bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, link) — each row showing the markdown it produces, so the menu teaches the syntax it hides. Esc leaves the literal `/` text; markdown input rules and ⌘B/⌘I keep working alongside it.

### Build order, test per step

1. `parseBlocks` / `serializeBlocks` — **byte-exact round-trip** over the renderer vocabulary AND every document already in the workspace. 2. Read-only block rendering — equals `/e/:id/doc.html`. 3. Caret editing + autosave on idle/blur, Save button deleted. 4. `/` menu, all commands. 5. Block components (table, code, mermaid, atomic chip). 6. Drag-handle reorder — the markdown diff is exactly the moved block.

Steps 1-2 merge before anything is editable: if the round-trip is not byte-exact on the existing corpus, nothing above it is safe, and that is knowable in a day.

Open for Kyle: input rules alongside `/` (default both); selection toolbar (default no); raw HTML editable in place or island (default island); grid row too or entity page first (default entity page); outline rail off heading blocks (default yes).


## Shipped 2026-08-16 — Vditor 3.11.3, instant-rendering mode

Kyle chose Vditor over Milkdown/Crepe (the written recommendation) with the gaps filed as follow-up work. The rendered document IS the editing surface: no edit mode, no preview toggle, no save button, no side-by-side plaintext. All markdown formatting moved under a `/` slash menu, because the toolbar is hidden.

### How it is wired

| Concern | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Distribution | Vendored pinned at `public/vendor/vditor` (MIT). **5.0MB**, pruned from a 22.6MB package: core + `lute.min.js` (3.7MB, the parser) + en_US + ant icons + highlight.js + light/dark content themes. mathjax/graphviz/echarts/katex/abcjs/markmap/emoji were left out. |
| Offline | `cdn: '/vendor/vditor'` — Vditor's default is `unpkg.com`. A test asserts no `unpkg`/`jsdelivr`/`cdnjs` string survives in `app.js`. |
| mermaid | **One copy, not two.** Vditor asks for `${cdn}/dist/js/mermaid/mermaid.min.js?v=11.16.1`; the server aliases that path onto the vendored 11.4.1 build. Verified live: 200, 2,571,900 bytes, diagram renders. Saves 3.5MB and removes the dedupe gap entirely. |
| Saving | `input` → 600ms debounce → `PUT /entities/:id/doc`, keyed per entity+field, flushed on `beforeunload` and on route change. Status is one glyph: `·` pending, `✓` written, `!` failed. |
| Section chrome | The card header is gone. A quiet uppercase label, a caret, a hover-revealed permalink and a `⋯` download menu (md/mmd/pdf/html — these were view modes, now exports). Collapse persists per entity+field. |
| Themes | Editor chrome, content theme and highlight style all follow `data-bs-theme`; `retheme()` runs on toggle. |

### Verified live (not asserted)

- Typing persisted to the database with a `doc-updated` activity entry, no save action.
- Slash menu opens on `/`, filters (`/mer` → Mermaid diagram), and inserts on click and on Enter.
- IR markers behave Typora-style: `## ` collapses to 0×0 and the heading renders at 23px/600.
- Dark mode: document background transparent against the page, mermaid renders its dark palette.

### Scope not covered here

Grid/board/list rows still use the plain `<textarea>` doc editor (Feature #8). Rolling the editor into those surfaces is its own feature — many editor instances per page is the main perf risk.

features.name: Fields as entities in space-level Fields table
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 31bba89, v0.4 Phase 2)

**The binding, decided.** A Fields row names its table by RELATION — `Table`, many-to-one to the Tables registry (#12), inverse `Fields` on every table's row. The relation was the right binding over a plain name because the registry rows already existed to point at.

**The registry is the schema surface.** One row per field of every user table: create a row (Name + Table + Definition) and the column exists — materialisation runs through addField, so the #85 shared-normaliser invariant guarantees the column is one addField would accept. Rename the row → column renames. Edit its Definition → config changes (same-type only: a definition cannot change its type; delete and recreate). Hard-delete the row → column deleted (soft refused with the reason; the table's Name field row refuses deletion outright).

**Completeness over editability.** Relations, lookups, rollups and formulas appear as rows — the registry is complete — but their Definition stays empty: their config names resolved tables, which only the schema verbs understand. `Type` is a synced text label; writing it is refused ('change the definition, not the label').

**Depth.** The registry Definition sits at depth 4 so it can describe field-type columns; a depth-4 field column is the one shape it cannot hold and stays empty rather than failing the verb.

Verified live on :4400 (test workspace): backfilled rows for existing fields; POST a Fields row with a select Definition → the real column appears on the table. 9 registry tests; suite 323/323. Note: REST paths do not decode %2F — use unqualified refs or ids over HTTP (pre-existing, unrelated).

features.name: SQLite storage engine (node:sqlite) powering all workspaces
features.description:
## Decision (2026-08-16)
Per the DB selection report (~/Documents/Queue.nosync/2026-08-16-105014-weave-db-selection-report.html):
- **D1 Engine**: node:sqlite (DatabaseSync) — sole candidate passing zero-dep + sync-API mandates. Fallback: better-sqlite3 (same sync idiom).
- **D2 Node floor**: accept 20 → ≥22.16 (Node 24 LTS recommended). FTS5 verified working on this machine (22.23.1).
- **D3 Human-readability**: binary .db + exportJSON/importJSON stays the byte-compatible interchange layer.
- **D4 Timing**: migrate now.

## Plan
SqliteStore: WAL + synchronous=FULL, row-level dirty-hinted writes (kills the 46ms/10.5MB-per-mutation amplification at 12k entities), :memory: for tests, auto-migration of legacy .json workspaces to sibling .db (original json preserved), hub discovery of .db + stem dedupe, PRAGMA data_version refresh so CLI+server coexist (fixes Issue #1), FTS5 startup probe failing loud with Node-version remedy, entities_fts index populated (search switch is a later feature), engines >=22.16, README/docs updated.

Kyle (2026-08-16): carets beside each space name in the left nav expand/contract that space (its table list). Persist per-space collapsed state.



## UAT round 2 — the caret trails the label (Kyle, 2026-08-16)

> "update the spaces carrot to look more like this" — reference image: **`Routines ›`**

Shipped in `d0309f7`. Three changes, and one deliberate non-change.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position | leads the label | **trails** it — `HANDBOOK ›` |
| Stroke | `2` (chrome weight) | **`1.5`** hairline |
| Glyph | `M6 9l6 6l6 -6` (down) | **`M9 6l6 6l-6 6`** (right), CSS-rotated 90° when open |
| Hit target | 24×24 | **24×24 — unchanged** |

**Why the target did not shrink.** Round 1 of this UAT was "space carrots are still too small and the wrong design", fixed by putting the glyph in a full 24px box. The reference reads light because of stroke weight and muted color, not because its target is small, so shrinking the box would re-open round 1's complaint to buy nothing. The contract test `the space caret is a real hit target, not a 18px sliver` still enforces it.

**Why rotation, not two paths.** One glyph turned by CSS cannot drift out of sync with itself, and the turn animates for free on the `transform` transition already declared. Resting state is right; `.nav-caret.open` rotates 90°. The contract asserts the resting caret carries no transform — had the rotation been on the folded state instead, a fully-collapsed nav would show a column of down-chevrons.

Round 1 had moved the caret to lead the label; this supersedes that half and keeps the rest. Both UAT rounds are recorded together in the note above `.nav-caret` in `public/style.css`.

Verified live in both themes on a fresh server — collapsed rows render `HANDBOOK ›` / `WIKI ›`, expanded rows turn down, and `aria-expanded` plus the Expand/Collapse title track the state.

Contract test `the caret leads the space label` was **rewritten**, not deleted, into `the caret trails the space label and rotates to open` (Quality/Case #269 renamed to match). UI contract suite: 61 cases, green.

## Note on the deploy

The reason the earlier grid features looked broken was a stale `:4400` process serving boot-time `app.js` (see Feature #42's note). That server has been restarted, so :4400 now serves current code — but this keeps happening, and **Feature #54** (launchd auto-start + status visibility) is the durable fix.

## Not changed

The space label itself is still `11px` uppercase with letter-spacing; the reference shows title case at a larger size. That is the nav's section-label style rather than the caret, and the ask was the caret — say the word if the label treatment should follow the reference too.

features.name: Self-hosting: positioning as an Airtable/ClickUp/Fibery alternative + deployment guide in README
features.description:
## What changed (2026-08-16)

README repositioned weave as an **open-source, self-hostable alternative to Airtable, ClickUp, and Fibery** that replaces the SaaS tools and workflows a team's work already lives in, and gained a full **Self-hosting** section alongside the existing local Quickstart.

Edits, all in `README.md` (docs only — no engine/server/CLI change; `node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'` 92/92 green before and after):

1. **Header tagline** — "A local, open-source, agent-accessible work platform ... in the spirit of Fibery/Notion/Airtable" -> "An open-source, self-hostable alternative to **Airtable, ClickUp, and Fibery**".
2. **Why** — added a paragraph on replacing SaaS (Airtable bases/grids, ClickUp tasks/boards, Fibery connected DBs with docs + automations), no per-seat bill, no vendor holding the export button. Added a **Yours to host** bullet linking to the new section.
3. **Quickstart** -> **Quickstart (local)**, to sit beside the server path.
4. **New `## Self-hosting` section** (4 steps: systemd service on 127.0.0.1 -> front door -> backup -> update). Full text below.
5. **Security notes** rewritten — the old text said "it is a personal, local tool. Do not expose the port publicly", which contradicted a self-host story. Now states plainly that there is no built-in auth and no per-user permissions, that the 127.0.0.1 bind keeps a local install private, and that a self-hosted install must sit behind a proxy or private network that does the authenticating.

## Design decisions

- **Everything documented works against 0.3.0 as shipped — no code change was required.** The recipe keeps the server on its default `127.0.0.1` bind and puts the front door on the same host, so no `--host` flag is needed.
- **The proxy IS the auth layer.** weave has zero accounts, so the section says outright that whoever reaches the port has full read/write on every workspace, and that Caddy `basic_auth` is one shared credential where every user is an admin (SSO proxy — Cloudflare Access / oauth2-proxy / Authelia — named as the alternative for distinct identities).
- **Two front-door options, private-first.** Tailscale (`tailscale serve --bg 4400`) listed before Caddy: nothing exposed publicly, no certificate to manage.
- **Backup loops over `*.db`**, not just the named workspace — `serve` provisions the `weave.db` docs workspace beside the data file, so a single-file backup would silently drop it. `.backup` over `cp` because it is safe on a running WAL database.

## Known gap (not addressed here)

**No Docker recipe.** `bin/weave.js serve` never passes a `host` through to `startServer` (`src/server.js:444` accepts `host = '127.0.0.1'`; `bin/weave.js:124` calls `startServer(w, { port })`), so there is no way to bind `0.0.0.0` from the CLI. A container would need `--network host` (Linux only), which is worse than omitting it. Adding a `--host` / `WEAVE_HOST` flag (with a test) would unlock Docker and proxy-on-a-different-host; deliberately left out of this docs-only change.

## Full text of the new Self-hosting section

A server install is the local install plus a front door. Any always-on Linux box
with **Node ≥ 22.16** will do — there is nothing to build and nothing to install
from npm.

**1. Run it as a service.** Keep it bound to `127.0.0.1`; step 2 is what the
network actually talks to.

```bash
sudo git clone https://github.com/grunion-ai/weave /opt/weave
sudo useradd --system --home /var/lib/weave --create-home weave
```

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/weave.service
[Unit]
Description=weave
After=network.target

[Service]
User=weave
WorkingDirectory=/opt/weave
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/weave/bin/weave.js serve --port 4400 --data /var/lib/weave/workspace.db
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now weave
```

**2. Put a front door on it.** weave has no accounts and no login of its own —
whoever reaches the port has full read/write on every workspace — so the proxy
or private network in front of it *is* the authentication. Pick one:

*Tailscale* — private to your devices, nothing exposed to the internet, no
certificate to manage. One command on the server:

```bash
tailscale serve --bg 4400
```

*Caddy* — a public hostname with automatic TLS and a shared password. Create the
hash with `caddy hash-password`, then:

```caddyfile
# /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
weave.example.com {
	basic_auth {
		you $2a$14$replace-with-your-bcrypt-hash
	}
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:4400
}
```

Basic auth is one shared credential for everyone — weave has no per-user
permissions, so every person who gets in is an admin. If you need distinct
identities, put an SSO proxy (Cloudflare Access, oauth2-proxy, Authelia) in that
slot instead.

**3. Back up the data directory.** Everything lives in `/var/lib/weave`: one
`.db` per workspace (yours, plus the `weave.db` docs workspace provisioned
alongside it) and one `files/` directory of attachments.

```bash
for db in /var/lib/weave/*.db; do
	sqlite3 "$db" ".backup '/backups/$(basename "$db" .db)-$(date +%F).db'"
done
rsync -a /var/lib/weave/files/ /backups/files/
```

Use `.backup` rather than copying the file — it is safe while the server is
running and folds in the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars. `node bin/weave.js export
--data <file>` writes the same workspace as human-readable JSON if you want a
copy you can read without weave.

**4. Update** with `git pull` — there is no migration step or build:

```bash
sudo git -C /opt/weave pull && sudo systemctl restart weave
```

features.name: Soft delete: recoverable delete, trash view, restore, purge
features.description:
Shipped 2026-08-16 (commit `76bac93`). Split out of Feature #38, which retains the filters half.

**Rule.** Deleting an entity is recoverable by default: the row keeps its id, publicId, values, documents and relation links, and simply stops being "in the table". Purging (`hard`) is the explicit, irreversible opt-in.

**Engine.** `listEntities`/`query` take `{ includeDeleted }` (default false). A private `#liveEntity()` gates relation, lookup and rollup resolution plus dotted-path traversal, so a deleted row cannot leak back through a relation, be counted by a rollup, or match a `Rel.Field` filter. `search` skips deleted rows and `store.js` drops them from the FTS5 index while keeping the `entities` row, so restore is lossless. `restoreEntity()` clears the flag; both delete and restore are idempotent and logged to activity (`deleted` / `restored`).

**All four surfaces agree.**

| Surface | Delete | Restore | Trash | Purge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| REST | `DELETE /api/entities/:ref` | `POST /api/entities/:ref/restore` | `GET /api/tables/:ref/trash` | `DELETE …?hard=1` |
| CLI | `delete <ref>` | `restore <ref>` | `trash [table]` | `delete <ref> --hard` |
| MCP | `weave_delete_entity` | `weave_restore_entity` | `weave_trash` | `weave_delete_entity {hard:true}` |
| UI | ⋯ → Move to trash | Undo toast / trash page | 🗑 badge → `#/trash/:dbId` | Delete forever (hold) |

**UI decisions.** Hold-to-confirm was theatre for a reversible act, so the entity menu offers a plain "Move to trash" with Undo in the toast; the hold survives only on purge, the one irreversible control. The 🗑 badge appears only when the trash is non-empty. The badge fetch is defensive (`.catch(() => ({total:0}))`): `public/` is served from disk while the server process is long-lived, so a page can outrun its routes — observed live, a 404 on `/trash` stopped every table from opening until the server was restarted.

**Tests.** `test/soft-delete.test.mjs`, 13 cases across engine, REST, MCP and CLI. Suite green at 141. `test/engine.test.mjs` was updated: the old CRUD test asserted delete throws on re-read, which is now the `--hard` contract.

features.name: Workspace rail: larger weave mark (30px → 42px)
Workspace rail: larger weave mark (30px → 42px)
features.description:
Shipped 2026-08-16 (commit `76bac93`), requested by Kyle: "increase the size of the left most nav weave logo".

The rope mark rendered at 30px inside a 40px chip in a 52px rail — small against the "weave" wordmark beside it. Now 42px in a 46px chip, filling the rail.

**Gotcha worth keeping.** `#ws-rail` is a column flexbox, so *height* is the main axis and a declared chip height is only a maximum: the 46px chip silently shrank to its 42px content, pulling the mark 2px off the wordmark centreline. `.ws-icon` now sets `flex-shrink: 0`. The `#ws-rail` top-padding `calc()` keeps the chip centred on the wordmark and the UI contract test asserts the calc's terms are the real sidebar padding / wordmark / chip numbers — so changing the chip size without changing the calc fails the suite.

Verified live at :4455 in both themes: chip 46×46, image 42px, centreline 25px = `#sidebar` padding 14 + wordmark 22/2.

features.name: Grid-native create controls: “+” in the header bar, “+ New” as the last row
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-16 (Kyle) — "replace table fields field with a + button after the last field" … "integrate it into the header bar and integrate the new entity into the table design as well."

## What changed
Both create affordances moved out of the page header and into the grid itself:

| Action | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add a field | `⚙ Fields` button in the view header | `+` closing the grid's header bar |
| Add an entity | `+ New` button in a detached sticky bar below the card | `+ New` as the grid's last row |

The table now reads as one surface that grows to the right (fields) and downward (entities), instead of a table flanked by controls.

## Design notes
The `+` opens a **menu**, not a bare add-field dialog. It replaces `⚙ Fields` in table view, so going straight to "add a field" would have stranded relation creation and field deletion. It offers **+ Field**, **+ Relation**, **⚙ Manage fields**.

Board and list views have no grid to host either control, so they keep the header buttons — the same conditional the codebase already used for `+ New`:

```js
state.route.view === 'table' ? null : el('button', { … }, '⚙ Fields'),
```

The header row gained a column, so the two full-width rows (the expanded document row and the new-entity row) now span a single derived `colCount` instead of a restated `cols.length + 2` — the kind of duplicated constant that silently under-spans when a column is added.

The popover implementation was extracted into a shared `showPopover(trigger, rows)` used by both the chip picker and this menu, so anchoring, flip-on-overflow, outside-click dismissal and keyboard behaviour exist once.

## Test coverage
`table view moves both create controls into the grid`, `the field "+" keeps relations and field management reachable`, `full-width grid rows derive their span from one column count`, `grid create controls are styled`, `one popover implementation serves every anchored menu`.

features.name: Keyboard-only record entry: Tab across fields, arrows + Enter in choosers
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-16 (Kyle) — "when creating a table record allow tab navigation between fields and arrow + enter navigation between selection."

## What changed
A record can now be filled in without touching the mouse.

**Tab across fields** already worked structurally (every cell control is a native `input`/`button`/`select`), and is now verified: from the Name cell, Tab walks col2 → col3 → the docs button, landing on each field's own control.

**Arrows + Enter inside a chooser** did not exist — the popover had no keyboard handling beyond Escape. `showPopover` now:

- moves focus into the popover on open, landing on the **current value** when there is one (via the `.chip-pop-check` marker) rather than always the first option;
- `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move focus between options, wrapping at both ends;
- `Enter`/`Space` commit — the options are real `<button>`s, so this is native behaviour rather than a re-implementation;
- `Escape` closes and hands focus back to the trigger;
- `Tab` closes and lets focus continue along the row.

**Focus survives the redraw.** Committing a value calls `onSaved`, which re-queries and calls `drawDatabase` — replacing every row in the grid. Without intervention the keyboard user is dropped to the top of the document and Tab restarts from the page start. `showPopover` records the triggering cell (`{eid, col}`) in `state.refocus` and `restoreGridFocus()` puts focus on the replacement control after the redraw.

Verified live, end to end:

```
focus chip → Enter        → popover opens, focus on "Fixed✓" (current value)
ArrowDown                 → "Open"
ArrowUp                   → "Fixed✓"
Escape                    → popover closed, focus back on the trigger
ArrowDown → Enter         → committed "In Progress"; after the redraw focus is
                            on the replacement chip in the same cell
```

Keyboard focus is now styled as loudly as hover (`.chip-pop-row:focus` plus a `:focus-visible` ring) — arrows move focus, not hover, so a hover-only highlight left the keyboard user unable to see their position.

## Test coverage
`popover options are keyboard navigable`, `focus survives the redraw a pick causes`, `the focused popover row is as visible as the hovered one`.

features.name: Hold-to-confirm destructive actions, replacing window.confirm
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-16 (Kyle) — "include a built in confirmation animation as part of the delete button instead of the built in browser are you sure."

## What changed
`window.confirm()` is gone from the UI. Destructive actions are now **press-and-hold**: the button fills over 900ms and fires only when the fill completes. Releasing early cancels.

```js
function holdToConfirm(label, onConfirm, { holdingLabel = 'Hold to confirm…' } = {}) { … }
```

The mechanism is a CSS transition, and the asymmetry is the safety property:

```css
.hold-fill                   { transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 0s; }  /* collapse: instant, no event */
.hold-btn.holding .hold-fill { transform: scaleX(1); transition: transform .9s linear; }
```

`transitionend` on the *fill* is what invokes the action. Because collapsing is untransitioned it fires no event, so an early release cannot complete the action. The handler additionally guards on `armed` and `propertyName === 'transform'` so a stray transition cannot delete anything.

The sweep is a `scaleX` transform rather than an animated `width`: animating a layout property thrashes layout on every frame, while a transform composites. `transform-origin: left` makes it sweep from the left edge. The label is a sibling element, not a child of the fill, so nothing is distorted by the scale.

Cancels on `pointerup`, `pointerleave` and `blur`. Keyboard users hold `Enter` or `Space` (keydown arms, keyup cancels). Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the hold shortens to 600ms rather than disappearing — the deliberate gesture is the point.

Verified live on a throwaway field:

```
hold 300ms then release → fill at 213px, class cleared, label restored, field intact
hold 1400ms             → field deleted (confirmed against the server schema)
```

## Where it is used
Permanent, irreversible actions only: **field deletion** and **Delete forever** in the trash. `Move to trash` is a plain click — soft delete is reversible, so a hold would be friction without a purpose.

## Test coverage
`no window.confirm anywhere in the UI`, `hold-to-confirm fires only on a completed hold` (including the untransitioned-collapse assertion), `both destructive actions use it`.

features.name: Entity actions menu in the corner with a vertical ellipsis
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-16 (Kyle) — "move the entity 3 dots menu to the leftmost corner, make the 3 dots oriented vertically."

## What changed
- `.entity-dl-corner` moved from `top: 10px; left: 12px` to `top: 6px; left: 2px` — the true upper-left corner of the main column. `.crumb-offset` came down from 34px to 26px to match.
- The glyph changed from the horizontal `⋯` to the vertical `⋮`, with `.dots-btn` giving it button metrics that suit a tall narrow glyph (`padding: 2px 5px; line-height: 1.1`) instead of inheriting the wide default.

## Test coverage
`the entity menu sits in the corner with a vertical ellipsis` — asserts the corner offsets, the glyph, that no horizontal ellipsis is left behind, and that `.dots-btn` carries its own metrics.

features.name: Rich-text descriptions on every workspace, space and table
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-16 (Kyle) — "include RTF descriptions for each workspace, space and table in the current environment."

## What changed
Every workspace, space and table in the running environment now carries a markdown description, rendered through `POST /api/markdown` in the view header.

| Workspace | Spaces | Tables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weave` | Handbook, Wiki, Quality, Development | Guide, Fields, Article, Suite, Case, Issue, Feature |
| `uno` | Product, People | Project, Task, Person |
| `test` | — | — |

Coverage before: 3 workspaces undescribed, 1 of 6 spaces undescribed, 9 of 10 tables undescribed. After: **nothing undescribed** (verified by reading every record back).

They are written to be useful rather than restating the name — what the record is for, what the fields mean, and the constraint that governs it. The `Suite` description states the rollup-equals-reality rule; the `Issue` description states the enrichment rule; `Project` carries a field table explaining what each rollup computes.

features.name: Repo discoverability: SEO'd README, comparison docs, agent-facing metadata, community health files
features.description:
## What shipped (2026-08-16)

Public-repo discoverability pass: the repo is now optimized to be found and evaluated by both people and agents searching for an open-source, self-hosted alternative to Airtable / Fibery / Notion / ClickUp.

### README

- Keyword-leading H1 subtitle and a keyword-dense opening paragraph (the repo description is what Google uses as the meta description; the README carries the long-tail terms).
- Badge row: license, Node floor, **runtime dependencies: 0**, self-hosted, MCP server included.
- Anchor nav (Quickstart · Comparison · Agents & MCP · Self-hosting · FAQ).
- **Screenshots** — hero table view plus a 2x2 grid (board, entity documents, relation map, ⌘K search), generated at 2x by `scripts/screenshots.mjs`.
- Two comparison tables: against the SaaS weave replaces (Airtable / ClickUp / Fibery) and against the open-source field (NocoDB / Baserow / Grist / Teable).
- A **"What weave is not"** section stating the no-auth / no-hosted / no-plugins / young-project limits up front, and pointing at the mature alternatives.
- A **FAQ** written against real long-tail queries ("Is weave a good open-source Airtable alternative?", "Is there a self-hosted Fibery alternative?", "Do I need Docker, Postgres, or npm install?", "How do I migrate off it?").

### Agent-facing surfaces

- `AGENTS.md` — repo map, the rules for changing the repo, the 23 MCP tools grouped by purpose, entity-ref forms, and the round-trip-saving notes an agent needs.
- `llms.txt` — llmstxt.org-style machine-readable index of the documentation set.
- `CITATION.cff` — structured metadata for indexers.
- `package.json` — rewritten description, keywords expanded 8 → 21 (alternative-to terms, self-hosted, MCP, agent terms).

### Community health files

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md` (threat model stated up front — the no-auth design position is documented as working-as-intended, with in-scope classes listed), `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, GitHub issue templates (bug / feature, plus a config routing security reports privately), a PR template, and a `tests` CI workflow (Node 22.16 + 24 x ubuntu + macOS, no install step).

### Long-form comparison docs

`docs/comparison/airtable.md`, `docs/comparison/fibery.md`, `docs/comparison/alternatives.md`, plus `docs/README.md` as the documentation index. These are the pages that rank for "X alternative" searches, and each is honest about what weave lacks.

### Tooling

`scripts/screenshots.mjs` regenerates every README screenshot from a running server, resolving tables and entities **by name** against `/api/schema` so it works on any workspace. Playwright is imported dynamically so the zero-dependency test suite still loads without it. Covered by `test/screenshots.test.mjs`.

### Verification

`node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'` — 142 passing (138 before, +4 from the new suite). Every relative link in the new and changed markdown was checked to resolve; the README was rendered through GitHub's markdown API and reviewed.

features.name: Brand loader animation: the h3 rope twisting into place
features.description: ## Brief (Kyle, 2026-08-16) > "lets create a weave loading animation using the weave logo showing the parts twisting into place" ## What exists now Four loader directions, all generated from the SAME source of truth as the static mark (`brand/build-logos.mjs`) — same `rope()`, same mask cuts, same palette. Motion is SMIL, so a loader is one inline SVG: no JS, no build step, works in `` and as a CSS background, and animates in Firefox (where CSS `d:` does not). | Variant | Motion | Resolves? | Note | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `travel` | Rope translates one weave period (2 x pitch), seamless loop | No — infinite | Honest for unbounded waits | | `twist` | Amplitude 0 → 4, hold, fade out | Yes — settles on the mark | The literal brief; **recommended** | | `spin` | Amplitude cosine 4 → −4 → 4, edge-on at zero | No — continuous | Calmest; survives 16px | | `draw` | Dash draw-on, crossing locks, unweaves | Yes, then undoes | Most literal to the name | ## Enabling change `rope(n, pitch, amp = 4)` gained an amplitude knob. Every amplitude emits an IDENTICAL path command sequence, so two ropes can be interpolated with ``. amp 0 = both strands flat on the centerline; amp < 0 = strands swapped. The h3 mark is unchanged (amp 4 is the default). ## Two defects found and fixed while building 1. **Gap eats the line at flat.** As the rope flattens the strands converge; a full-width mask cut swallowed the line and left the crossing floating in the hole. The cut now tapers with amplitude (closed below |amp| 2) and the crossing fades with it — at amp 0 the mark is one clean edge-on line. 2. **Round caps painted stray dots.** With `pathLength="100"` + `stroke-dasharray="100"`, the pattern wrapped at the far end of the path and a zero-length dash with a round cap still paints a dot — crumbs on the hidden frames. Fixed by widening the off-gap to 110 so on+off (210) exceeds offset+pathLength (204). ## Verification - `brand/build-logos.test.mjs`: 17 tests (8 new), whole suite 142 green. - Playwright filmstrips: each loader paused at 6–8 points in its cycle to check mask registration mid-animation. This is how both defects above were caught — the invariants alone did not show them. - Contact sheet `brand/docs/round6-loaders.html`, generated by `brand/build-loader-sheet.mjs` from the live generators, so the decision page cannot drift from the code. ## Open — awaiting Kyle Variant decision. Once picked: emit the chosen loader as a build VARIANT, wire it into the app's loading states, and record the choice in `brand/README.md` as decision 7. ## Kyle picked `draw` — 2026-08-16 > "I like the draw option but currently there is a middle transparent piece this is unnecessary and distracting simplify the draw" **Diagnosis.** The static mark composes the crossing as a THIRD path laid over the top. Under a draw-on that path has no honest moment to arrive: the strands reach the crossing at t≈0.22 but the crossing faded in at t=0.50, so the middle of the mark was a hole for a quarter of every cycle. **Fix — one fewer element, not a retimed fade.** Mask A now cuts the under-strand and then paints the crossing back in WHITE, so strand A stays continuous through it. The crossing is simply part of the strand and draws with it; B keeps its cut, so the over-under still reads. Draw order flipped (B first, A over it). The loader is now two paths and no timing to tune — no frame can show a hole. **Verified.** 18 tests green (2 new: element count/no-opacity, and mask-A restore order + paint order). Rest state pixel-diffed against `weaveSvg` at 256²: AE 443 / 65536 = 0.68%, all antialiasing at the crossing edges — the finished mark is unchanged. 12-frame filmstrip confirms continuity at every step. **Still open:** emit as a build VARIANT + PNG/rasters, wire into the app's loading states (there is no loading state in `public/app.js` today — it needs designing), record as decision 7 in `brand/README.md`. ## Shipped — 2026-08-16 **Decision 7: weave-on**, on a 2000 ms loop, in both strand pairs (`weave-loader-dark.svg` blue+sky, `weave-loader-light.svg` blue+ink), built by `loaderSvg()` as ordinary build variants and copied to `public/brand/`. **Wired in as the default page-load state.** `route()` is wrapped in `withPageLoader()`, so every route change and boot itself goes through it. Two rules that pull against each other: - it only appears once a wait passes 200 ms, so fast navigation pays nothing; - once it appears it always finishes at least one whole cycle — hiding waits out the remainder of the cycle it is in. The SVGs are fetched and inlined rather than used as ``, because only an inline SVG exposes `setCurrentTime`; restarting the clock on show is what makes the whole-cycle rule exact rather than approximate. **README hero.** GitHub's image proxy does not run SMIL, so `brand/render-gif.mjs` builds `weave-loader-{dark,light}.gif` from the same generator, paired in the README with `` + prefers-color-scheme. **Verified in a live browser, not just in assertions.** Measured: 80 ms work → never appears; 300 ms → appears at 210 ms and hides at clock 2.00 s (1.00 cycles); 900 ms → 1.00 cycles; 2600 ms → 4.00 s (2.00 cycles). Two defects the contract tests could not see were caught this way and are now guarded: 1. the inlined SVG has no intrinsic size, so as a flex item it rendered 0x0 — every test passed while the loader was invisible; 2. `#ws-rail` declares z-index 60, so the wash stopped at the chrome. **Tests:** 193 in `test/**` + 19 in `brand/`, all green. New suite `Quality/Suite` "Page loader" (11 cases); "Brand" now 19.

features.name: Table and space ⋮ overflow menus (CSV export + delete)
features.description:
Shipped 2026-08-16 (commit `4b6a48f`), requested by Kyle.

A single `dotsMenu()` helper now builds every ⋮ menu — entity, table and space — replacing the entity page's hand-rolled one. It takes link items, button items, hold-to-confirm items and dividers; `align: 'right'` hangs the panel off the right edge so a menu at the end of the header toolbar stays on screen. Opening one closes the others; clicking away closes it.

| View | Menu contents |
| --- | --- |
| Table | Export CSV · Delete table (hold) |
| Space | One `Export <Table>.csv` per table it holds · Delete space (hold), labelled with the table count |
| Entity | Download .md / .html / .pdf · Move to trash (plain, with Undo) |

**Decisions.** CSV left the table toolbar entirely rather than appearing in both places. A space has no CSV of its own — it is a container — so it enumerates its tables instead of inventing a bundle format (which would need a zip dependency; the house rule forbids one). `deleteSpace` cascades to its tables, so the label says so: "Delete space + 2 tables".

features.name: Entity side column: Fields → Comments → Activity
features.description:
Shipped 2026-08-16 (commit `4b6a48f`), requested by Kyle: "activity and comments can be moved under fields".

The entity side column now reads top-down as metadata about the entity: **Fields** (what it is) → **Comments** (what people said) → **Activity** (what happened). The main column is left to the document panels, which are the reason to open an entity at all.

Open question for Kyle: the side column is on the **right** (`.entity-grid { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 320px }`). The request said "left hand side"; the stacking under Fields was the unambiguous part and is done. Flipping the column to the left is a one-line grid change plus swapping the append order.



## Superseded 2026-08-23 ([[Feature#117]])
Fields left the side card for a draggable block at the top of the body; the side column is Comments → Activity.

features.name: Typed [[…]] references to entities, tables, spaces and the workspace
features.description:
Shipped 2026-08-16 (commits `4167eb7`, `0efa36b`). Groundwork for the "/" reference picker.

A document could only point at an entity. It can now point at anything addressable, in a form that stays readable in raw markdown — Kyle's choice between readable and id-based:

| Syntax | Points at |
| --- | --- |
| `[[Feature#70]]` | an entity (unchanged) |
| `[[table:Development/Feature]]` | a table — bare `Feature` works when unambiguous |
| `[[space:Development]]` | a space |
| `[[workspace]]` | this workspace |
| `[[space:Development\|the team]]` | any of them, with a label |

**Shape.** The parser splits kind from target and nothing more; the resolver decides what each kind addresses and where it links, so exactly one place knows the URL shapes. That changed the resolver contract from `(dbName, publicId)` to `(kind, ref)`.

**Two invariants, both tested rather than asserted in prose:**

1. *Failure is always a broken chip.* No resolver, a null result, an ambiguous bare table name, a trashed entity, a deleted table, or a resolver that throws — each costs its own chip and nothing else. A document is user input and must not be able to take a page down.
2. *One renderer, two surfaces.* The in-app preview (`POST /api/markdown`) and the standalone document page (`/e/:id/doc.html`) emit byte-identical chips. This is the argument against adopting a second markdown engine (see [[Feature#45]]), so it is pinned by a test.

**Details worth keeping.** Links are workspace-absolute (`/#/space/…`, `/w/<ws>/#/…` when scoped) because a bare `#/space/…` from a document page at `/e/:id/doc.html` only sets the hash on that page. Kind prefixes are case-sensitive so a reference has one spelling. References inside inline and fenced code stay literal, so the syntax is documentable. Each kind carries a class and a leading glyph (`#` `▦` `◇` `⬡`) via `::before`, identically in both stylesheets.

Tested by [[table:Quality/Suite]] "References" — 28 cases.

features.name: Cloudflare-hosted private instance (full DB, Access-gated) + repo data hygiene
features.description:
**Host Weave on Cloudflare's free plan as Kyle's private working instance** — the latest build carrying his full workspace data, reachable from anywhere, gated so unrecognised devices must authenticate. Local stays the same code against the same data for testing. The **public GitHub repo** is the artifact that gets stripped: code and bootstrap documentation only, never data or deployment specifics.

## The three artifacts

| | **Cloudflare** (Kyle's, private) | **Local** (Kyle's, testing) | **GitHub** (public) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | the instance he actually uses, from anywhere | dev + testing against real data | let others run their own Weave |
| Code | latest build | same build | source of truth |
| Data | **full DB — every workspace** (`weave`, `uno`, …) | same data, pulled as a snapshot | **none** |
| Documentation | live in the `weave` workspace | same | `src/weaver-seed.js` builds a fresh one |
| Deploy config | real account, Access policies, tokens | n/a | template only; real values gitignored |
| Reachable by | Kyle + agent, Access-gated | localhost | anyone (code only) |

The stripping boundary is the **repo**, not the deployment. Kyle's instance carries everything; the public artifact carries nothing personal.

## Access control: whitelist, password otherwise

Cloudflare Access sits in front of the Worker as an edge gate — **zero application code**. Weave never learns what a user is, so the user/role model stays an open product decision instead of being forced by deployment.

| Principal | Policy | Weave code changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Known devices / IPs | Bypass — no prompt | none |
| Kyle, elsewhere | One-time PIN to his email (no IdP setup needed) | none |
| Agent | Service Auth token (`CF-Access-Client-Id` + `-Secret`) | none |
| Everyone else | blocked at the edge, never reaches the Worker | none |

Free for up to 50 users, indefinitely. Service tokens are a first-class Access primitive for non-human callers and need no IdP flow. One-time PIN is the simplest "password" — no identity provider to configure.

**Explicitly out of scope:** users, roles, permissions, sharing, multi-tenancy. Per Kyle (2026-08-16): *"we have not yet defined users or user role definitions and I am not ready to do this and don't want to rush it."* Access provides the gate without prejudicing that design.

## Canonical direction: Cloudflare is primary

Because the point is to *use it anywhere*, the Cloudflare instance is where work happens and therefore holds truth. Local is downstream: pull a snapshot to test against realistic data, discard local edits. Writing in both directions without a sync design produces drift and silent data loss.

Practical consequence: **redeploying code must never reset data.** The Durable Object's storage persists across Worker deploys, so this holds naturally — but any seed/import path must be idempotent and guarded, never a blind `save(state, { all: true })` on boot.

## Storage: Durable Objects with the SQLite backend, not D1

D1's API is asynchronous; `Store` is synchronous (`DatabaseSync`, `src/store.js:86`), and stateless Workers would re-`load()` the whole workspace on every request.

| Weave requires | D1 | DO SQLite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Synchronous SQLite (`src/store.js:86`) | async only → rewrite `load`/`save` | `ctx.storage.sql.exec()` is **synchronous** |
| Warm state between requests | stateless → full reload per request | isolate stays warm; in-memory `state` persists |
| FTS5 `entities_fts` (`src/store.js:102`) | supported | supported, incl. `fts5vocab` |
| "One workspace = one .db file" | shared DB, awkward mapping | **one workspace = one Durable Object** |

The structural fact that makes this cheap: `src/engine.js` (1,497 lines) never touches SQLite. `Store` loads the workspace into a plain JS object graph and saves dirty rows back, so the swap is confined to `src/store.js` (229 lines, ~24 call sites) and does not propagate async through the engine.

Transactions are the one API divergence: DO rejects raw `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` (`src/store.js:145,189`); use `ctx.storage.transactionSync()`.

## Multi-workspace routing — new work

Carrying the full DB means the hub must serve several workspaces, so this is **not** a single Durable Object. One DO per workspace, plus a way to enumerate them: Workers has no `readdirSync`, so the filesystem discovery at `src/server.js:58` cannot run.

Options: a workspace registry DO, or a static binding list in `wrangler.toml`. A registry keeps `POST /api/workspaces` (`src/server.js:268`) working on the deployed instance, which matters if Kyle wants to create workspaces from his phone. Decide during implementation.

## Free-plan headroom (verified 2026-08-16)

| Resource | Free limit | Weave today | Headroom |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DO SQLite storage | 5 GB | ~380 KB, 393 entities across all workspaces | ~14,000× |
| Rows read | 5M/day | single-tenant | ample |
| Rows written | 100k/day | single-tenant | ample |
| Requests | 100k/day | single-tenant | ample |
| DO duration | 13,000 GB-s/day | — | ample |
| Worker script (gzip) | 3 MB | vendor assets served as Static Assets, not bundled | fits |
| R2 (attachments, `files/`) | 10 GB | < 1 MB | ample |
| Cloudflare Access | 50 users | 2 principals | ample |

## Port surface — ~700 of 3,774 lines

| File | Lines | Work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/store.js` | 229 | `DatabaseSync` → `ctx.storage.sql`; `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` → `transactionSync()`. Second backend behind the existing `Store` interface, not a fork |
| `src/server.js` | 466 | `node:http` `createServer` → `fetch()` handler; static serving → Static Assets binding; workspace hub → DO routing |
| `src/engine.js` | 1,497 | only the `node:fs` calls (attachments, JSON export) → R2. Logic untouched |
| `src/formula.js`, `markdown.js`, `pdf.js`, `ids.js` | 819 | **zero changes** — pure JS, no Node built-ins |
| `src/mcp.js` | 308 | does **not** port — stdio transport (`src/mcp.js:253`). MCP-over-HTTP is separate work, and is what would let the agent use the hosted instance |

`Store` keeps one interface with two implementations: `node:sqlite` for self-hosters (preserving the copyable single-file property and the zero-dependency, no-build-step positioning) and DO SQLite for Cloudflare. Wrangler is deploy-time tooling, not a runtime dependency.

## Repo hygiene — must land before first deploy

Already correct: `.gitignore` covers `*.db`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm`, `files/`, and legacy `uno.json`/`weave.json`. No workspace data is tracked. `src/weaver-seed.js` gives a clean bootstrap so a fresh clone builds its own documentation workspace rather than inheriting Kyle's.

**Not yet covered — new leak surface introduced by this feature:**

| Artifact | Risk | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wrangler.toml` | account ID, DO/R2 binding names, routes | commit a `.example`; gitignore the real one |
| `.dev.vars` | local secrets | gitignore |
| Access service token (Client ID/Secret) | full agent-level access to the instance | never on disk in-repo; Wrangler secret / Access dashboard only |
| Custom domain / route | reveals the private endpoint | keep out of committed config |

Precedent: **Issue #10** — "Public squash briefly included weave.json workspace data." The same class of mistake, one layer up. Gitignore entries land **before** the files are created, not after.

## Primary risk: 10 ms CPU per request

Free Workers cap CPU at 10 ms per invocation (paid: 30 s default); memory 128 MB on both. Ordinary CRUD against a warm DO with in-memory state fits comfortably. Expected to hit the ceiling first:

1. Initial data import of the full DB into DO storage — full reconcile plus FTS rebuild (`src/store.js:168`)
2. PDF export of a long document — `src/pdf.js` is pure JS, so every millisecond is own CPU
3. Any future bulk import

Mitigation is chunking bulk work across requests; the initial import is one-time and can be scripted incrementally. Failing that, Workers Paid ($5/mo) lifts CPU to a 30 s default.

## References

- Durable Objects pricing / free tier: https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/
- DO SQL storage API (synchronous, FTS5): https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sql-storage/
- Workers limits (10 ms CPU free): https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/
- Cloudflare Access policies + Service Auth: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/policies/access/
- D1 pricing (evaluated, not chosen): https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/

Related: **Feature #67** (self-hosting positioning + deployment guide), **Feature #79** (repo discoverability), **Issue #10** (workspace data in a public artifact).

- **CFStore shipped** (commit 1c94037): Durable Object SQLite backend behind the existing Store interface — same schema/row-level save/FTS, transactionSync() instead of BEGIN/COMMIT, changedExternally()=false. Engine gains `new Weave({store})` injection; store.js's node:sqlite throw deferred to first file-backed open so the engine bundles into workerd. 6 contract tests over a node-side ctx.storage shim (test/store-cf.test.mjs); suite 434/434 at HEAD.
- **Account probe dispatched** to the cloudflare-wrangler agent: auth check, free-plan DO-SQLite/R2/Access verification, scratch deploy+teardown.
- **Next**: worker entry + server fetch() port + registry-DO routing (P2-b), then wrangler-dev G2 rerun and the Access-gated deploy (G3).


## Progress 2026-08-22 (v0.5 P2-b, commit 458d7a8)
- **One dispatcher, two runtimes**: the ~500-line route core extracted to `src/routes.js` (pure request→response, zero node imports); `src/server.js` is now a thin node adapter (body stream, sockets, `public/` statics). All existing server tests pass unchanged through the adapter.

Also: `compatibility_date` in wrangler.toml.example backdated to 2026-06-02 (the newest wrangler 4.95.0's workerd accepts). G2 rerun dispatched.
