features.name: The `field` field type: a value that is a field definition
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-16 (Kyle) — "the new field type called field has predefined options and its definition also defines the down-hierarchy field, in this case we can do pure D and the config becomes the field entity page as the control surface."

## Why this type exists

It terminates the meta-model's recursion. A space-level `Fields` table needs fields to describe fields (Feature #52), and every earlier design answered that with a bespoke descriptor sitting below the entity layer. This type removes the special case: the innermost descriptor is an ordinary engine primitive whose predefined options come from `DEFINABLE_TYPES`, a plain array in `src/engine.js`. Nothing is circular.

It also collapses the config UI. Because `field` is a field type like any other, its editor registers through the same dispatch as `select`'s chip picker — so the Field entity page *is* the control surface, with no bespoke `FieldConfigEditor` component. That is what makes pure D viable and made the B/D hybrid (design review §5) unnecessary.

## Shape

| Aspect | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Value | `{ type, config }` — a field definition — or `null` |
| Predefined options | `DEFINABLE_TYPES`, engine-supplied, exposed as `config.types` so a UI never hard-codes a list |
| Definable | text, number, date, daterange, checkbox, url, email, select, multiselect, workflow, document, field |
| NOT definable | relation, lookup, rollup, formula |
| Recursion bound | `config.depth`, default 1 (describes a leaf), 2 = workspace → space → table, capped at 4 |

**The load-bearing invariant.** A `field` value and a real field are validated by the *same* normaliser: `normalizeSelfContainedConfig()` was extracted out of `addField` and is now shared. A definition therefore cannot describe a field `addField` would refuse to create. A test pins the two outputs as `deepEqual` — if they ever drift, it fails.

**Why relation/lookup/rollup/formula are excluded.** Their config names fields of a specific *resolved* table, which a down-hierarchy definition does not have yet. They are refused at definition time with a clear reason rather than stored and left to blow up at materialisation.

## Grid treatment
A `field` cell follows the `document` precedent — computed chip (`⌗`) plus the definition read as a sentence (`select · 3 options`), not the generic text fallback, which could only ever produce an invalid definition. Editing happens on the entity page.

## Verification
12 tests in `test/field-type.test.mjs`; full suite **225/225** green. Commit `36f57b9`.

## Not yet built — next commit
**Down-hierarchy materialisation.** This lands the definition and its validation, not the act of creating the column on the target table. The open design question is the binding: how a Fields row names the table its definition materialises onto. Options are a relation to a Tables entity, or a plain field naming the table within the space.

Also open (from the design review): whether `Field Types` becomes an entity table for docs (Feature #61). If it does, `field`'s picker becomes a relation to it and each option chip carries its own help text — but `DEFINABLE_TYPES` must stay the primitive floor, or the recursion's terminator moves back inside the entity layer and the bootstrap problem returns.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 8fbe4bc, v0.4 Phase 2)

The two halves the engine commit (36f57b9) left open:

**The entity page is the control surface (pure D).** The grid chip prints the engine's own display sentence ('select · 3 options' — #displayValue, not a duplicated client formatter). On the entity page the chip opens the definition editor: type <select> fed from the schema payload (describeSchema now exposes `types`/`depth` on field fields — a UI never hard-codes the list), config as JSON seeded from `item.raw` (the display string and the definition ride different keys). A refused definition throws through the modal, so the dialog stays open showing the normaliser's real reason. Verified live: seed → edit → save re-renders 'select · 4 options'; invalid JSON keeps the dialog with 'Config is not valid JSON'.

**Materialisation is addField, named.** `materializeField(tableRef, name, def)` is deliberately thin: the definition was validated by the same normaliser addField runs, so the shared-normaliser invariant does the guaranteeing and the verb only performs the act. Tested end-to-end: a definition stored on a Fields row materialises onto another table and accepts values.

**Deliberately not taken here:** the binding — how a Fields row names the table its definition lands on. That is [[Feature#52]]'s design (relation to a Tables entity once [[Feature#12]] exists vs a plain field), and taking it now would pre-empt the hierarchy design. 15 field-type tests, suite 287/287.

features.name: Live [[…]] entity chips inside the editor
features.description:
**The known cost of choosing Vditor** (see the editor comparison, 2026-08-16).

`[[Table#123]]` renders as a live chip on document pages and in previews, because weave's own renderer resolves it. Inside the editor it stays literal text — Vditor parses markdown with **Lute**, a Go parser compiled to JS, so weave's own syntax cannot be taught to it the way a ProseMirror/remark editor (Milkdown, Tiptap) allows a custom node.

Today the slash menu inserts the literal `[[Table#1]]` as a stopgap.

Paths worth evaluating, cheapest first:
1. **Decorate after render** — post-process the IR DOM, swapping resolved references for chip elements, and restore the text on edit. Fragile against Vditor re-renders, but no fork.
2. **`hint.extend` with `[[`** — an entity picker that completes the reference correctly (search across tables, insert `[[Table#123|Name]]`). Solves *authoring* even if the chip never renders live. Cheapest real win.
3. **Fork/patch Lute** — a vendored parser change. Highest cost, only if chips must be live.

Blocks nothing today; it is the reason the written recommendation was Crepe. Feature #15 (permalink links) and the agent-native hierarchy epic both lean on this.


## Update 2026-08-16 — the authoring half is shipped

The slash menu's **Entity link** command now runs the ⌘K search and inserts a real, resolving reference: `[[Space/Table#12|Name]]`, qualified so a table name shared by two spaces cannot resolve to the wrong one. `openCommandK` grew `{ onPick, onDismiss, entitiesOnly }`, so one search surface serves both navigation and referencing rather than the editor growing a second picker.

Covered by `test/slash-commands.test.mjs`, which asserts the picked reference RESOLVES — it reads the server-rendered `doc.html` and requires `mention mention-entity` with no `mention broken`.

**What remains is the rendering half**, which is the actual Lute limitation: inside the editor the reference stays literal `[[…]]` text. It renders as a live chip on document pages and previews, because weave's own renderer resolves it — Vditor's parser does not know weave's syntax.

So option 2 from the original list ("an entity picker that completes the reference correctly — cheapest real win") is done. Options 1 (decorate the IR DOM after render) and 3 (fork Lute) remain open for live chips.

One rough edge from the shipped path: inserting the reference replaces the document via `setValue`, which puts the caret at the end rather than after the chip.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit f41efab, v0.4 Phase 4)
Live [[…]] chips inside the editor as an overlay DECORATION layer — Lute owns the contenteditable, weave never mutates it. Resolves via POST /api/markdown (batched, cached, 250ms debounce, visible paragraphs only); degrades to literal text while the caret is inside the reference. Two traps pinned by tests: Vditor clears its host on build (layer re-attaches), and the caret splits text nodes making refs invisible to per-node scans — root.normalize() at pass start (spec carries live ranges across the merge; this was a real suite flake, fixed at root). Verified live: [[Leads#1]] renders as a chip in the IR editor.

features.name: Document outline: dash rail with place tracker
features.description:
Kyle's ask, 2026-08-16: "narrow dashes on the left which parallax for long document and show sections when clicking", plus an automatic heading outline with a place tracker.

Vditor ships its own outline panel (`outline: {enable, position:'left'}`) and it is deliberately **disabled** — it is a conventional text list, not the dash minimap, and it would fight the rail for the left gutter. What Vditor does give free is the heading tree and scroll sync to build on.

Design (from the plan of 2026-08-16, now simpler because the doc iframe is gone):
- One dash per heading, width/opacity/indent by level, positioned proportionally down a rail fixed in the left gutter.
- The active dash tracks scroll position — that is the place tracker.
- Past the density where dashes would collide, the strip drifts opposite the scroll at a damped rate so every heading stays reachable in a long document.
- Hover/click reveals section labels; click scrolls to the heading.

Now reads the editor's live DOM rather than an iframe's document, so the original plan's cross-frame harvesting is no longer needed.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 4367650, v0.4 Phase 4)
The dash rail: entity doc panels only, ≥3 headings, dash length by level, place tracker follows scroll, click jumps (instant, not smooth — backgrounded tabs never run rAF). Vditor's own outline stays disabled, as decided on this record. Verified live.

features.name: Collapsible headings inside documents
features.description:
Kyle's ask, 2026-08-16: headings should collapse, with the state remembered.

No candidate editor collapses sections natively — not Vditor, not Crepe, not Tiptap. It is ours to build in all worlds.

Shape: a fold affordance on each heading in the IR surface, hiding every block until the next heading of the same or higher level; state persisted per entity+field (the same pattern the document *section* collapse already uses: `weave-doc-collapsed:<entity>:<field>`); a deep link to a heading expands its ancestors first.

Constraint specific to Vditor: the fold must live in the DOM/decoration layer, never in the stored markdown — a collapsed heading must not change a single byte of the document.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 1db4bf3, v0.4 Phase 4)
Fold carets in an overlay gutter; folding hides blocks until the next same-or-higher heading via a class — a browser test pins getValue() byte-identical across fold/unfold (folding is VIEW state, never content). Persisted per entity+field in localStorage keyed level:text; folded-away headings leave the rail ([[Feature#87]]).

features.name: The embedded editor in grid, board and list rows
features.description:
Feature #8 put document editing inline in table, board and list rows. Those surfaces still use the plain `<textarea>` doc editor; only the entity page got the real editor.

This is deliberate, not an oversight: a Vditor instance is heavy (the parser alone is 3.7MB, loaded once, but each instance builds three panes and its own DOM), and a 40-row table with a doc editor per row is the stress case. Rolling it out blindly would be the first thing to make weave feel slow.

Wanted before rollout:
- Measure instance cost — mount time and memory for 1, 5, 20 editors on one page.
- Lazy strategy: render read-only markdown until a row is focused, mount the editor on demand, tear down on blur.
- Then the two editing models collapse into one, which is the actual goal — right now a document edits differently depending on which view you are in.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 67a1f9c, v0.4 Phase 4)
The recorded blocker (a Vditor per row) dissolved under measurement: ONE shared instance, mounted into the focused row's doc cell, unmounted on blur — warm mount/unmount 2ms median (5ms cold). Every keystroke syncs back to the textarea, so Save and redraw-preservation keep working. Found and fixed the leak destroy() misses: +1428 DOM nodes per 12 cycles of duplicate icon sprites appended to <body> — mount now dedupes, sprite count pinned ≤1 by test. The textarea-keep fallback was prepared but not needed.

features.name: Math and extra diagram engines are not vendored
features.description:
The vendored Vditor tree is pruned to 5.0MB from 22.6MB. Left out: mathjax (6.4MB), graphviz (1.9MB), katex (1.5MB), echarts (1.0MB), markmap, abcjs, smiles-drawer, wavedrom, plantuml, flowchart.js, emoji images.

Consequence: a document containing `$...$` / `$$...$$` math, or a graphviz/echarts/plantuml block, renders as plain text in the editor instead of a formula or diagram. Vditor requests the missing asset, gets a 404, and fails quietly.

Mermaid is unaffected — it is aliased onto weave's vendored 11.4.1 and verified rendering.

Decide per format rather than restoring the lot: KaTeX (1.5MB) is the plausible one if anybody writes math in weave; the rest are unlikely to earn their weight. Until then this is a documented limit, not a bug.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit e9d4896, v0.4 Phase 4)
Decision executed: KaTeX 0.16.47 vendored (js + css + mhchem + 20 woff2 fonts, 624KB) at the exact paths Vditor requests — mhchem is load-bearing: Vditor chains katex→mhchem→render, so without it NO math renders. $…$ and $$…$$ now render in editor and document pages; graphviz/echarts/plantuml/mindmap/abc/flowchart stay out, documented in the README Documents row + vendored credits (Vditor itself added to credits — was missing). Verified live: E=mc² renders.

features.name: Activity is a workspace system table, with enriched document events
features.description:
Kyle: "we still need an activity table at the workspace level" — "activity is a protected, not end-user-definable table reachable from the main workspace page and includes all activity events across the workspace" — "any change to a document must be registered as an activity fully enriched".

**Enriched document events.** `docChange()` records what an edit did rather than that it happened: `field`, `length`, `prevLength`, `delta`, `line` (1-based, where the edit starts), `linesAdded`, `linesRemoved`, and `preview` (the first line that differs, 120 chars). Common head/tail trimming gives the shape of a single edit — what an autosave almost always is — and degrades honestly when the edit is not local. Applies to `setDoc`, `appendDoc` and the document path in `setValues`. An identical write now records nothing and does not bump `updatedAt`.

**The table.** `activityFeed({ entityId, tableRef, kinds, since, limit, offset })` reads over the history every entity already carries, so the workspace feed and an entity's own list are the same rows filtered differently — they cannot drift. Event id is `<entityId>:<index>`, which makes one event addressable as a link; `getActivity(id)` reads it back. Served at `GET /api/activity` and `GET /api/activity/:id` — no POST, because an event is something that happened, not something anyone declares.

**The view.** `#/activity` is the whole table (When / Event / Detail / Record / Name), `#/activity/<entityId>` narrows it, `#/activity/<entityId>:<n>` lands on and highlights one event. Reached from the workspace page under a `system` chip. The entity pane is that table seen through one record: 10 rows, each linking to its own event.

**Not yet done** (Kyle's later refinement, still open): Activity as a *system field* automatically related to every table, hidden from table view by default the way created/modified are. That needs the system-field mechanism, which created/modified do not have either.

Tests: `test/engine.test.mjs` (detail shape, feed, filters), `test/server.test.mjs` (routes, paging), `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (pane cap, links, read-only view).

features.name: Computed fields marked on the field name, not only in their cells
features.description:
Kyle: "script F for formula should be used next to any field name which is configured as formula driven and therefore not user editable".

`fieldNameLabel(f)` hangs the existing `computedMark()` glyph vocabulary — ƒ formula, Σ rollup, ↗ lookup — off the field NAME as a `<sup class="field-mark">`, with a title saying it is computed and not editable. Applied everywhere a field name is printed: grid column headers, the entity page, board and list expanded labels, and the schema table. Rollup and lookup are included because they are non-editable for the same reason; document fields are not, since they are edited in place.

Guarded by `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` — the helper and every one of the five render sites.

features.name: Field menu drops Move left / Move right (drag-and-drop is the reorder control)
features.description:
Kyle: "field move left and move right are not necessary since drag and drop is validated".

The column header is draggable and a drop commits through the same `reorderField()` schema write the menu rows used, so the menu offered a second way to do one thing. Rows removed and the now-unused `cols, i` arguments dropped from `fieldMenuButton`. The ui-contract test that asserted the rows now asserts their absence, and still asserts the drag path.

features.name: Related entities as an interactive sub-table in the entity body
features.description:
Kyle (uno workspace): "we have projects that reference multiple tasks, I want to find the best way to show the table of related tasks as a sub table visible within the project entity where the table is in the main body, the same structure as our main table field rules etc, so you can interact with these related referenced entities."

Today a relation renders as chips in the Fields panel. The ask is the grid itself, embedded in the entity body: the target table columns, inline editing, pickers, column chrome — the same machinery renderTable() builds, scoped to the related rows, so a Project page is where its Tasks are worked on.

Design notes to settle first: which columns an embedded grid shows by default (the target table field order, or a per-relation choice); whether adding a row there creates-and-links in one step; how it collapses on narrow viewports; and whether the Activity pane becomes an instance of the same component (Kyle asked for the activity pane to be "built like a related table").

Milestone unset: past v0.3, and the Milestone select has no v0.4 option yet.

## Shipped 2026-08-17 (ca62f01)

Each collection relation renders as the target table grid under the documents: its columns, editorFor cells, the same picker/computed cell classes and click routing (picker opens the picker, anywhere else opens the row). The inverse column is dropped and documents stay on their own page. "+ New <Table>" creates and links in one step, "+ Link existing" picks an existing row, and each row unlinks on hover. The chips are gone from the Fields panel, which now says so when a table is only a name and a relation.

Engine: `id` became a queryable path alongside publicId/createdAt/updatedAt, so the grid fetches its rows whole in one query rather than one request per chip.

Design questions settled: columns = the target table field order minus documents and minus the inverse; adding creates-and-links; the Activity pane is NOT yet rendered by this component (Feature #95).

features.name: Activity as a system field on every table (hidden by default, like created/modified)
features.description:
Kyle: "each activity should be linked to the activities table as though it was a related field since it should be built like a related table. as a result, the activity section should be a system field which is automatically created and related with every table, even if the user opts not to show it in table view, just like created and modified date."

Shipped so far (Feature #91): the Activity table exists, the entity pane shows its 10 most recent rows, and each row links into it.

Still to build: a system-field mechanism — fields weave owns, present on every table without being declared, addressable in queries and views, hidden from the grid unless opted in. Activity is the first; created and modified belong to it too (they are entity metadata today, with no way to show them as columns). Sequenced with the embedded related-table component, which is what the pane should be rendered by.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 0e8a5ba, v0.4 Phase 2)
Activity joined the system-column set ([[Feature#65]]): per-table show/hide via `updateTable {systemFields}`, rendered as an activity count in the grid. Hidden by default like the timestamps. The related-table treatment (activity rows opening in a panel) lands with [[Feature#48]] — the column is the per-table surface, [[Feature#91]]'s workspace table remains the feed.

features.name: Default value in every field definition
features.description:
Kyle: "include default value config for each field definition as an option".

Every field type gains an optional config.default, applied when an entity is created without an explicit value for it. Needs: per-type validation through the existing #validateValue path (a select default must be one of its options, a date default a real date, a relation default probably disallowed), the add/edit field dialogs, the CLI/MCP add-field config documentation, and export/import round-tripping. Workflow fields already carry a default state, which is the precedent to match rather than duplicate.

## Shipped 2026-08-17 (e3ff795)

`config.default` on text, number, date, daterange, checkbox, url, email, select and multiselect; refused on workflow (its default is a state), computed, document and relation. Validated at definition time through the same #validateValue a row goes through. updateField merges it alongside the type config and takes null as the clear. A create applies defaults only to fields it did not name, and existing rows are untouched. Dialogs offer the input for exactly those types and coerce the form strings back into their own types; describeSchema reports it; the MCP add-field docs name it.

features.name: Number field units & formatting (Fibery-style)
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-21 (Kyle), with a Fibery "Edit Number Field" reference screenshot — "I like the way fibery generalizes units for numbers, lets do something like this."

## The shape being asked for
Number field config generalizes display formatting, Fibery-style:

| Option | Shape | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | number / currency / percent | $1,200 · 12% |
| `unit` | free text, rendered after the value | `30 days`, `4.5 kg` |
| `decimals` | 0–n | `0` → 30, `2` → 30.00 |
| `separator` | boolean 1,000 grouping | 1,200,000 |

Joins the already-shipped per-field `default` ([[Feature#96]]).

## Constraints
- Stored value stays a **plain number** — formatting is display-only, never round-trips into storage or formulas.
- Applies everywhere a number is printed: grid/board/list cells, entity Fields panel, PDF export, and rollup/formula outputs (computed fields inherit the source field config where sensible).
- Config surface: the field-settings header dialog ([[Feature#41]]), engine validation via the existing config path.
- Builds in v0.4 Phase 5 alongside [[Feature#44]] (date system) — both are typed-value-formatting work.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 9f4dcd7, v0.4 Phase 5)
Number config gains the Fibery-style costume: `format` (number | currency | percent), free-text `unit`, `decimals` 0–6, `separator`. Display-only by construction — the stored value stays a plain number, and the formula resolver now hands numbers through RAW (a formatted '$1,200.50' × 2 is NaN; that rule has its own test). Config validates through the shared normaliser (so field-type definitions carry costumes too — [[Feature#85]]), travels in describeSchema, edits in the field-settings dialog ([[Feature#41]]: format select, unit, decimals, 1,000-separator toggle), and idle grid cells wear the costume, swapping to the raw number on click. Verified live: '30 days' and '$1,234,567.50' with raw 30 / 1234567.5 beneath. 6 tests; suite 359/359.

features.name: Undo: step back any entity mutation (engine + REST + CLI + MCP)
features.description:
**Every entity mutation can be stepped back** — field/doc/state/relation edits, creates, soft deletes, comments, file attachments — via engine `undo()`, `GET`/`POST /api/undo`, CLI `weave undo [--steps n] [--list]`, and the `weave_undo` MCP tool. Built so agents get to make mistakes without making a mess.

## Shipped 2026-08-21 (commit 6faf973, v0.4.2)

**The shape.** An inverse-operation log in a new `undo_log` sqlite table (in-memory fallback mirrors the audit-trail pattern, `src/store.js`). Each mutation verb records a sparse before-image of exactly the fields it names; `undo()` pops entries and replays the inverse — relations go back through `#setRelationValue` so both sides stay consistent, everything else restores raw. Undo fires **no automations** (stepping back must not cascade forward) and logs an `undo` activity entry. Automation effects (`set-field`, `append-doc`, `add-comment`) record their own entries, so a triggering edit and its cascade step back together, newest-first.

**Deliberate limits (v1).** Structural/schema work (spaces, tables, fields, registry rows — everything the audit log covers) is not undoable; hard deletes and file deletions are gone for real; the stack caps at 200 entries; no redo. Reader tokens are refused on `POST /api/undo` by the existing role rules; registry-row writes never enter the stack.

**Rollback design (requested by Kyle).** One atomic commit; `undo_log` is additive and invisible to prior builds (store validation only requires `weave_meta`), so `git revert 6faf973` + restart rolls back cleanly with **no data-file migration in either direction**.

**Verified live** on :4400 (v0.4.2): POST create Issue → POST /api/undo → row trashed → purged. 16 tests in `test/undo.test.mjs`; suite 413/413 at HEAD in an isolated worktree.

**Later, if earned:** ⌘Z in the web UI, redo, per-entity undo filtering.

Shape: reuse the existing TOOLS + dispatchTool tables behind an HTTP transport (POST /mcp, streamable-HTTP per current MCP spec); auth rides Cloudflare Access Service Auth headers on the hosted instance and stays open on localhost. stdio remains the local default.

Gate: an agent round-trip against the hosted URL — list tables → create entity → read back → undo.

## Shipped 2026-08-22 (commit 41f69a3, suite 451/451)

features.name: Slide composer: decks compose decklet HTML from versioned slides
features.description:
## Patchset 3 2026-08-23 — vendored decklet moved to the latest build

`src/vendor/decklet` is now pinned to **cf73916** (GitHub tip of grunion-ai/decklet), not the file set copied earlier the same day. That is v0.3.3 **plus what landed after the tag**: `href` links (row anchors + inline marks), `curve`/`arrow` connector rows, the parity collision check, the `localStorage` probe with `⤒ Save a copy`, and the flicker-free `⤓` rasteriser. The package version moves slower than the build, so the vendor README pins the **commit**.

Upstream's own suite is red at cf73916 (6 of 53: connector `to`/`from` validation, HUD contract, empty-footer page counter) — in-flight decklet work, none of it on the path weave composes with. weave's gate is green: 572 tests, 570 pass, 0 fail; `Deck#1` still composes with 0 errors and 0 warnings. Gerrit change 30 patchset 3: `tests PASS -> Verified 1`.

## State 2026-08-23 — Verified, awaiting Code-Review

Gerrit change **30** (patchset 2, rebased on b7c4334): `tests PASS -> Verified 1` via `weave-review.sh`. Full suite 572 tests / 570 pass / 0 fail in an isolated worktree. Not submitted: Code-Review is Kyle's, and change 30 stacks on change 31 (the slash-menu commit), which is also unreviewed.

Live proof: composed over the real `uno` workspace — `Decks/Deck#1 "How weave composes decks"` (3 slides) and `#2` its AFB variant (one slide swapped), `deck.json` reporting 0 errors and 0 warnings.

Tests: `Quality/Suite` **Deck composer** (`test/deck.test.mjs`, 18 cases). Docs: `Handbook/Guide` **Decks: composing slides**.

## The idea

A deck is not a file in weave — it is a **read over rows**.

- **`Slide`** rows carry one decklet slide object each in a `Model` document (`{layout, els:[…]}`; a fenced ```json block is fine).
- **`Deck`** rows carry the deck-wide layer — `Chrome` (`{layouts, master}`) and `Style` (`{tokens, roles, pad}`) — and link the slides they want through a **many-to-many** `Slides` relation, so one slide serves every deck it belongs in.
- **`/e/Deck#N/deck.html`** composes them, on read, into one self-contained editable decklet HTML deck. Nothing is exported, so a deck can never be stale with respect to its slides. `deck.json` returns the composed model plus what the decklet validator makes of it.
- A **slide row answers the same route** with a one-slide preview wearing the chrome of the first deck it belongs to.

## Contract (conventions, not schema)

A table is a **deck** if it has a many-relation named `Slides` pointing at a slide table; a table is a **slide** if it has a document field named `Model`. Deck-side optional fields: `Chrome`, `Style`, `Order` (refs that re-order **and subset** without unlinking anything), `Format`, `Space`. Slide-side: `Layout`, `Version`, `Key`, `Supersedes`.

## Versioning

`POST /api/entities/:ref/version` clones a slide row, bumps `Version`, points `Supersedes` back at what it replaced, and leaves every deck pinned to the row it linked. `?promote=1` swaps the new row into each of those decks **in place**, keeping its position in the running order. Customer-specific slides carry a `Customer` relation; house slides carry none.

## Where it lives

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `src/deck.js` | compose + render + version, all pure reads over the engine |
| `src/vendor/decklet/` | decklet v0.3.3 pinned (MIT, grunion-ai/decklet): `create.mjs`, `validate.mjs`, `template.html` — node builtins only, so zero runtime dependencies still holds |
| `src/routes.js` | `/e/:ref/deck.html`, `/e/:ref/deck.json`, `POST /api/entities/:ref/version` |
| `public/app.js` + `public/style.css` | the entity page frames the composed deck above the fields; slides get **New version** / **New version, promoted** |
| `test/deck.test.mjs` | 18 cases — composition, order, chrome/style, broken-model behaviour, single-slide preview, versioning, the routes, the UI contract |

## In uno

`Decks` space: `Customer`, `Slide`, `Deck` (+ the legacy attachment table renamed `Attached Deck`). Seeded with a real 3-slide deck ("How weave composes decks") and its AFB variant that swaps one slide.

features.name: Ontology: the fifteen entity types, exported from the engine and gated against the docs
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-23 (v0.5)

Kyle, 2026-08-23: *"these are field types, entity types are different. confirm this and build a weave ontology which include glossary; entities have fields but these are not the same."*

The model has two axes and both get called "types". Asking for weave's **entity types** and getting `text`/`number`/`rollup` back is a category error: an entity **has** fields, a field is not an entity, and `text` is not a kind of thing weave stores.

### What landed

- **`ONTOLOGY` exported from `src/engine.js`** — the fifteen kinds of object weave models, each with its layer, definition, identity, where it is actually stored, and the engine verbs that create and read it. It sits beside `FIELD_TYPES` because agents discovering the model need to know what a Table is before what a `rollup` is.
- **`docs/ONTOLOGY.md`** — the ontology table, how the kinds nest, a lifecycle table, the field-type axis contrasted explicitly, and a glossary defining all fifteen entity types plus all eighteen field types (and the terms *entity type* and *field type* themselves).
- **`test/ontology.test.mjs`** — the drift gate, 8 tests: every entry names verbs that exist on `Weave.prototype`; every entry is stored where it claims (state key, entity-embedded, `table.fields`, a real `store` table, or the keystore); parents resolve; the doc's table matches the engine exactly in both directions; the glossary covers every entity type and every field type; the field-type axis lists exactly `FIELD_TYPES` and nothing else.
- Indexed in `docs/README.md` and `llms.txt`.

### The fifteen

Workspace · Space · Table · Field · Entity · Document · Comment · File · Activity · View · Automation · Account · Key · Audit entry · Undo step.

Two things the ontology makes explicit that were only implicit before: a **Table is a user-defined entity type** (the fifteen are the built-in kinds those tables and rows are made of), and a **relation is a paired field, not a separate kind** — the link has no identity you can address.


## Revised 2026-08-23 — the entity is the core kind

Kyle, same day: *"entities include workspaces, spaces, tables, and entities within tables (within a table the entity can be referred to as a record, item, entry, customer, company, account etc endlessly like in Airtable) these are naming conventions but do not change the core ontology of what an entity is. Each entity has a dedicated entity view containing its fields."*

The first cut listed fifteen sibling kinds, which flattened the model's actual spine. Corrected: **an entity is the one core kind**, and workspaces, spaces, tables and rows are all entities differing by LEVEL. The engine already worked this way — `createSpace` writes a row in `Workspace/Spaces`, `createTable` one in `Workspace/Tables`, `addField` one in `Workspace/Fields` — so the ontology now says what the meta-model has done since Feature #12/#52.

`ONTOLOGY` is now `{ core, levels, constituents, apparatus, aliases, collisions }`:

- **core** — Entity: id, public id, fields, and a dedicated entity view at `/e/<id>`.
- **levels** — Workspace › Space › Table › Field › Row, each `isEntity: true`, each naming its registry table (or saying why it has none).
- **constituents** — Value, Document, Comment, File, Activity: no identity apart from their entity, no entity view.
- **apparatus** — Saved view, Automation, Account, Key, Audit entry, Undo step: real objects, not entities. "Saved view" is now named to keep it clear of the entity view.
- **aliases** — record, item, entry, customer, company, account, task, deal, ticket, contact. Names for rows, not kinds.
- **collisions** — `account` is both an alias and a kind; the glossary now disambiguates rather than dropping either.

The gate grew from 8 tests to 11. The one that matters most creates a space, a table and a field and reads each back as an entity carrying fields and a public id — the claim is checked against the engine, not asserted in prose.

One asterisk remains, now tracked as **Feature #121**: the workspace itself is `state.meta` with no registry row, so it is the only level with no entity view.

features.name: Rich slash menu: grouped, glyphed, and teaching its syntax
features.description:
Kyle, with a mockup of the intended menu: "we are missing this rich slash command capability". The mockup showed a menu grouped INSERT / ALL COMMANDS / REFERENCE / FORMAT · APPLIES TO SELECTION, each row a glyph + name + the markdown syntax on the right.

## Shipped

**The menu.** One catalogue of 20 visible commands with `icon`, `label`, `hint` (the syntax column) and `aliases`, grouped by what a command does. `slashRows(query)` promotes the strongest matches into an INSERT group at the top (score >= 70: prefix on the label, prefix on an alias, or a word-start) and leaves the rest of the catalogue in place, so a near-miss narrows the menu instead of emptying it. Group headers ride inside the first row of their group — a hint item is always a button — and the highlight is painted on the row, so a group title never lights up.

**New commands.** Text, Raw HTML, Table reference (`[[table:…]]`), Space/workspace reference (`[[space:…]]`). The renderer already understood all of these; the menu could not reach them. Headings are one row with six hidden aliases behind it, so /h4 and /heading 4 both write a level-4 heading.

**References** share one picker: `openCommandK` now takes `kinds` (and a placeholder) instead of an `entitiesOnly` flag, and `referenceFor(kind, hit)` emits the shape the mention parser accepts for that kind.

**FORMAT applies to the selection, literally.** Typing / replaces the selection before any command can see it, so the editor remembers the last non-empty selection (15s window, collapsed selections ignored) and Bold on a selected "vermilion" writes `**vermilion**`.

Tests: browser suite covers every command, the group structure, promotion, and formatting a real selection; ui-contract + vditor cover the catalogue shape, the CSS and the vendored patch.

features.name: The workspace is not yet an entity: a Workspace registry row so every level has an entity view
features.description:
## The gap

The ontology's spine is that **workspaces, spaces, tables and rows are all entities** — same kind, different level, each with fields and a dedicated entity view. The engine honours that at four levels out of five: a space is a row in `Workspace/Spaces`, a table in `Workspace/Tables`, a field in `Workspace/Fields`, and a row is the data itself.

The **workspace is the exception**. It lives in `state.meta` — a name, a logo, a `requireAuth` flag — with no registry row, so it has no entity view, no fields you can add, no documents, no activity. You cannot open the workspace the way you open a table.

## What it would take

A fourth registry in the `Workspace` system space: `Workspace/Workspaces`, holding exactly one row that IS this workspace, synced by the same one-verb-per-mutation rule as the other three (`#syncSpaceRow` / `#syncTableRow` / `#syncFieldRow` → `#syncWorkspaceRow`). Renaming the row renames the workspace; its Description becomes the workspace's own document; `Spaces` gains a relation to it.

Open questions for Kyle:

- One row, or one row per workspace known to the multi-workspace hub? A workspace file that lists its siblings has to read files it does not own — probably one row, and the hub stays a directory listing.
- Does the workspace row accept **custom fields**? If yes, that is where per-workspace settings could live as data instead of as `meta` keys.
- What happens on hard-delete of that row — refuse (like other system rows), or treat it as "delete this workspace"?

## Why it matters

Until this lands, `docs/ONTOLOGY.md` has to carry an asterisk: five levels, four of which are really entities. Closing it makes the sentence unconditional.

Raised 2026-08-23 alongside the ontology (Feature #119).

features.name: # is the entity search: one step, inline, arrow-navigable
features.description:
Kyle: "today /entity and then entity search are two steps, lets make this one, after # you can start search across all entities, when you select an entity a rich inline linked text with chips appears like fibery."

A second `hint.extend` key on the editor: `#` runs `entityHint(query)`, which searches the workspace (entities only, cached per query) and returns rows the menu renders like any other. ↑/↓ move, Enter writes `[[Space/Table#id|Name]]` at the caret, and the existing chip layer paints it as a chip. Minimum two characters after the # so `# Heading` is a heading, never a search — verified in the browser suite.

The /entity, /table and /space commands still open the ⌘K palette for anyone who reaches for the menu instead; the palette takes the cursor and answers arrow keys (verified: activeElement is #cmdk-input, typing lands in it, ArrowDown moves the selection).

features.name: An unlabelled code block detects its own language
features.description:
Kyle: "lean on Code slash command to autodetect and show mmd json html and all other code as plain text."

The slash Code block stopped naming a language for the writer (it inserted ```js on whatever they pasted). An unlabelled fence is detected instead.

**Why rules, not hljs.highlightAuto().** Measured in a live browser against the vendored bundle:

| sample | subset answer | full-set answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `function add(a,b){return a+b}` | css (4) | ada (5) |
| `const x = 1;` | javascript (1) | ebnf (2) |
| `SELECT id FROM users…` | sql (4) | sql (4) |
| `def add(a,b):` | python (3) | livecodeserver (4) |
| `graph TD  A --> B` | css (3) | less (3) |
| `/Users/kyle/…/app.js` | bash (2) | solidity (7) |

A scorer that confident and that wrong colours code as a lie.

**The rules** (public/editor-lib.js, `detectCodeLanguage`, precision first): JSON that parses is JSON; markup that closes its tags is xml; a diff header is a diff; a mermaid/diagram head is NOT code — plain text, because a Code block displays and never renders; SQL, shell, python, css and javascript are claimed only on their own shapes; everything else is plain text. Deterministic, which was the original objection to auto-detection (a scorer can rank differently as a document grows).

One implementation, three surfaces: the editor decorator colours the rendered half of the block (the markdown lives in the editable pre beside it, so nothing here can change the document) and /doc.html loads the same library and asks the same question. Unit tests in test/code-detect.test.mjs carry the measurements above.

features.name: Flat icons replace emoji across the chrome
features.description:
Kyle: "use flat icons not emojis."

🗺 (relation map, map button), 📎 (files field), 📄 (row documents toggle), ⚙ (fields), 🗑 (delete field), 🖼/🔗 (slash menu), 🌐 (relation map webhook node) now draw from the vendored Iconly flat set through `iconEl()`, which inherits currentColor and the theme — a colour picture does neither, and renders differently on every platform. Typographic marks (H, B, I, S, backtick, ¶, •, ▦, ◇) stay: in a markdown menu they ARE the icon. The one glyph the free set lacks — a chain, for Link — is drawn inline.

Guarded: a ui-contract test fails on any emoji codepoint in public/app.js. One browser test that clicked the 📄 button by its text now finds it by title, which is what it should have keyed on.

features.name: Editor: table keys (Enter/⇧Enter/Tab), /Line break, markdown edits in fullscreen
features.description:
## Follow-up 2026-08-23 (commit 86badd5, Gerrit change 37)
- **Divider → yaml code block, root-caused:** an inserted `---` pair is YAML front matter to Lute (`data-type="yaml-front-matter"`, language-yaml block). The item now inserts `***` — same thematic break, no front-matter reading; server renderer draws `<hr>` for both.
- **Slash link glyph** is Feather's interlocked chain (MIT); the hand-drawn arcs are gone.
- **Menu clamp:** the hint panel could open past the top of the window, hiding the promoted row (measured top −145px on a mid-page caret) — `attachHintClamp` pushes it into the viewport and lets it scroll.

Verified live: /div → highlighted Divider visible at top, click → `<hr>` (no yaml node); /link row wears the chain. Suite 584/584.

features.name: Every level is a table: table configuration as fields on its registry row
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 2e7362b)

Kyle: *"lets make it clear that a workspace, and space are also structured as tables with fields … the description that is at the top of the table and what fields are visible in what order should both be fields at the space level referring to a specific table."*

### What landed

The claim "everything is an entity" got its twin: **every level is itself structured as a table with fields.** The workspace is a table of spaces (`Workspace/Spaces`); a space is a table of tables (`Workspace/Tables`, scoped by the `Space` relation); a table is a table of rows.

And a table's configuration is now **fields on its registry row**, synced two-way:

| Field on the Tables row | Configures |
| --- | --- |
| `Description` | the description at the top of the table (already round-tripped) |
| `Field Order` | visible column order — comma-separated full permutation |
| `Hidden Fields` | hidden columns, incl. system columns; empty clears |

Editing `Field Order` on the row IS `updateTable({ fieldOrder })` — a partial order is refused on the row exactly as at the schema verb. `addField`, `addRelation` (both ends) and `deleteField` (both ends of a pair) refresh the row so it never goes stale. Legacy workspaces backfill on open; this one did.

`docs/ONTOLOGY.md` gains the "Every level is a table" section; the ontology gate checks the section exists and that every config field it names is a real field of the Tables registry. meta-model 10 → 14 tests; 649 green in the main tree.

features.name: Space and workspace views are the registry grids; opening a row opens the structure
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 62f5e4a)

Kyle: *"this should be reflected not just in the document but in the view of tables within a space and view of spaces within a workspace, these should be tables with all relevant fields; opening them opens the space or table which is the entity of the workspace."*

Follows Feature #126 (table configuration as fields on the registry row) — this lands the same truth in the UI.

### What landed

- **The space page IS the Tables registry grid**, scoped to the space by the `Space` relation: Name, Description, Space, Fields, Field Order, Hidden Fields — every column editable in place, through the same engine sync (renaming the row renames the table; editing Field Order reorders it, with the full-permutation validation).
- **The workspace page IS the Spaces registry grid**, above the system card: Name, Description, Tables.
- **Opening a registry row opens its structure.** Row clicks and the `#N ↗` open link both route through `registryHref()` / `openRegistryRow()`, navigating by the row's `sysId` — which `readEntity`/query now expose for system-registry rows (plain rows carry none).
- The hand-rolled `space-table-row` list and the home page's flat table list are gone. Both themes verified in the live browser; row-click → space → table → row loop verified end to end.

### Notes

- Cells still behave as cells: clicking Field Order edits it; the row surface and the `#N ↗` link are the navigation affordances.
- ui-contract's row-click routing contract now allows the registry hop (still exactly 3 routed surfaces).

features.name: Workflows system table: workspace-level workflow registry with script, state, health, diagram
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 16e9dad)

Kyle: *"Lets create a new system table like activity at the workspace level called Workflows"* — each row is a workflow: related tables it touches, related spaces it touches, the executable automation script itself as a field, version, state (Draft, Active, Deactivated), health (Healthy, Warning, Failed), last run datetime, and a document field holding a mermaid diagram of the workflow. A Type field ships with **no types yet** — types get designed and rolled out later.

### Shape (all system fields)

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tables | relation m:m → `Workspace/Tables` | inverse `Workflows` on the registry |
| Spaces | relation m:m → `Workspace/Spaces` | inverse `Workflows` |
| Script | document, kind `code` | the executable itself |
| Version | number, 0 decimals | |
| State | workflow | Draft (default, not-started) / Active (in-progress) / Deactivated (canceled) |
| Health | select | Healthy (green) / Warning (yellow) / Failed (red) |
| Last Run | date, time on | |
| Diagram | document, markdown | mermaid renders natively |
| Type | select, **zero options** | the socket future workflow types plug into |

### Engineering notes

- Unlike the registries, **Workflows rows are ordinary data**. The meta-model interceptors now own exactly `spaces`/`tables`/`fields` and pass any other system table through to normal row CRUD — previously a row update on a non-registry system table fell into the structural branch and threw.
- Legacy workspaces grow the table on first open via `#ensureMetaTables`; this workspace did.
- New suite `test/workflows-table.test.mjs` (5 tests); engine's count test expects the sixth system table. 694 green; verified rendering live (filter strip shows the three states, Docs (2) carries Script + Diagram).

### Open for the types rollout

Type options, per-type Script contracts, what flips Health, and what runs Last Run — all deliberately unbuilt.

features.name: One relation map, drawn at the workspace and at a space
features.description:
**Raised by Kyle, 2026-08-24**: "the relation map directly accessible from the left nav is much better design than the one under weave but the content of the mmd native is better — can we get the best of both worlds and define one relation map view which lives in the workspace and space level?" and, separately, "we also don't need a map button in each space".

Weave carried two maps:

| | content | design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mermaid card on the workspace home (Feature #51) | **right** — user tables only, grouped into their space, one labelled arrow per relation | wrong — mermaid's own palette, theme-blind, a dark box on a light page |
| SVG behind `#/map` (the left-nav entry) | wrong — the registry drawn alongside user tables, a circle layout that hid structure, most edges unlabelled | **right** — weave's own cards, chips and type, clickable nodes, automations drawn in |

**Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit f4bbf56, Gerrit change 43, Verified +1).** They are one view.

`public/relmap-layout.js` is the pure half — a column per space in schema order, the registry left out, one edge per relation pair carrying both ends' cardinality (crow's-foot order: `Owner ∗–1` reads "many Tasks to one Person"), endpoints landing on the card border so an arrowhead has somewhere to sit, and room reserved ahead of time for a self-relation's loop and for each automation pill. Passing a `spaceId` narrows it to that space plus whatever it actually touches, the guests drawn dashed and named by their own space.

`relationMapView()` in app.js draws it in three places from one renderer:

1. the `#/map` page (the left-nav entry, unchanged as an entry point),
2. a card on the workspace home — the mermaid card and `/api/relation-map.mmd` fetch are gone,
3. a card on every space page — which is why the per-space **Map** button goes too. A space shows its own map instead of linking to the workspace's.

Gate: `test/relmap-layout.test.mjs` (12 tests) covers the content rules, the space altitude, the reserved room, and the wiring — including that the mermaid map and the Map button stay gone.

features.name: Agent-complete configuration: the remaining schema and view verbs over MCP
features.description:
**Every schema and view choice an agent can make in the UI, reachable without a browser.**

Audit 2026-08-24 across engine / REST / CLI / MCP / registry rows. Most of the surface is already agent-reachable through registry-row CRUD (rename, reconfigure, reorder, hide, delete) — the gate is awareness, not capability, and that half is answered by the new Handbook guide.

Genuinely unreachable from MCP today, REST-only:

| Capability | REST | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table `icon` | `PATCH /api/tables/{id}` | the nav and every crumb read it |
| Table `noun` | same | names the create action |
| `systemFields` | same | Created/Modified/By columns |
| Space `icon` | `PATCH /api/spaces/{id}` | nav grouping |
| Saved views + share links | `POST /api/views`, `/share` | the multi-table read an agent would hand to a human |
| Automations: list, describe, update, delete | `/api/automations` | `weave_create_automation` can write one and never read it back |
| Workspace name, description, logo | `PATCH /api/workspace` | |
| Declarative apply | `PUT /api/schema` | blocked behind [[Issue#56]] until the round trip is lossless |
| Activity feed / audit | `/api/activity`, `/api/audit` | reading what changed |
| Table and space delete | `DELETE /api/tables|spaces/{id}` | (registry rows cover this with `hard: true`) |

Also stale: `weave_add_field`'s description names 13 of the 18 field types (`document`, `field`, `key`, `attachments` and `relation` are missing) and none of the costume config keys; `weave_create_table` takes no `icon`.

Proposed: `weave_update_table`, `weave_update_space`, `weave_create_view` / `weave_list_views` / `weave_share_view`, `weave_automations` (list/describe/update/delete), `weave_apply_schema` (after #56), `weave_activity`. Each lands with its tool-description vocabulary — colors, icons, formats — so the tool list itself teaches the visual meaning.

features.name: Universal reference rule: every entity answers to its unique id and id-based permalink
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit ae6b203)

Kyle: *"lets go for a more universal and durable fix ... all entities where names are referenced via the unique ID that each entity has and its permalink. This will help make sure everything is more extensible later. all entities should behave this way."*

The one-off interceptor fix (Feature #128's note) becomes a rule: **every entity — workspace, space, table, row — is referenced by its unique id and carries an id-based permalink; names are display labels.**

### What landed

| Level | Identity | Permalink | Rename-proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | `meta.id`, minted once in `#migrate` | `/w/<id>/` (name URL = alias) | ✅ verified live |
| Space | uuid (existing) | `#/space/<id>` stamped in schema | ✅ |
| Table | uuid (existing) | `#/table/<id>` stamped in schema | ✅ |
| Row | uuid (existing) | `/e/<id>` now on every `readEntity` | ✅ |

- **Mentions**: `[[<uuid>]]` resolves by id and renders the *current* name — a rename never breaks a document. `[[Task#12]]` stays as the human spelling.
- **Surfaces stop joining on names**: space page scopes its registry grid by `sysId` (was Space-name match); the workspace rail links chips by id URL and resolves the active workspace from a name-or-id segment; workspace rename navigates to the id permalink; the home permalink chip copies the id URL.
- API: `GET /api/workspace` and `GET /api/workspaces` expose `{ id, url }`.

### Contract

`test/permalinks.test.mjs` (7 tests): identity minted once and kept through export/import/rename; every level resolves by id after renames; `/w/<id>/` routes before and after a rename; the list carries ids; id mentions render current names. ui-contract gains the no-name-join gates. 710 green.

### Why extensible

A new entity kind follows the rule and gets durable identity for free — no per-surface name-joins to invent, no rename hazards to discover later.

features.name: Table row selection with a floating action bar (puck)
features.description:
**Row selection in the table view, with a floating action bar.**

Checking rows in a table opens a bar that floats over the bottom of the grid and acts on the whole selection at once. Prompted by Kyle, 2026-08-24, against the Fibery reference bar (`2 selected · Edit Fields · Convert to · Duplicate · Merge into… · Download all files · Copy as Markdown · 🗑`).

### Selection mechanics

- The checkbox is **its own column, to the left of the row's `#` link** — the link never disappears, so a row stays openable while a selection is live.
- The column holds its width at rest and reveals the box on row hover, or once any selection exists. An idle grid stays clean.
- The header box is select-all, with an indeterminate state for a partial selection.
- Clicking anywhere in a row toggles it, except on the `#` link. `Esc` clears.
- Selected rows take a soft accent tint and a 2px accent rule on the leading edge.

### The bar — five designs explored, **Puck chosen** (Kyle, 2026-08-24)

| # | Design | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Pill — Fibery-faithful, every action labelled | Readable, but 940px wide and it grows with every action |
| 2 | **Puck** — icon-only, hover labels, overflow `⋯` | **Chosen.** Fixed width, survives a narrow panel |
| 3 | Dock — selection summary segment + actions segment | Scales, at one extra click for demoted actions |
| 4 | Inked — solid ink instead of glass | Best contrast, loudest thing on a cream page |
| 5 | Command — the selection as a ⌘K scope | Never needs to grow; costs a keystroke |

Glass shell: `blur(22px) saturate(180%)`, hairline border, inset top highlight, three-layer shadow. Rises 14px with a fade on appear. The grid gains bottom padding while a selection is live so the bar never covers the last row.

### Commands (revised with Kyle, 2026-08-24)

Fibery's set was cut down — **Convert to**, **Download all files**, **Copy as Markdown** and **Merge into…** are all out. What replaces them is weave-shaped:

**On the bar** — Set state (opens the workflow chips), Set a field… (pick a field, one value across the selection), Link to… (pick a relation and a target, connect every selected row), Duplicate, and Move to trash past a hairline.

**Under `⋯`** — Move to table…, Roll up into a new entity… (create one parent and link the selection to it), Show these in the map, Select all with the same… (grows the selection instead of acting on it), Copy links.

The bar is contextual: no *Set state* on a table without a workflow field, no *Link to* without relations.

### Cut, and why

- **Convert to…** — changing a row's type is a schema decision; it belongs in the field/table dialog where you can see what breaks.
- **Download all files** — a zip across a selection is a rare ask and a slow, failure-prone job.
- **Copy as Markdown** — every weave page is already markdown, and ⌘C can carry this without a slot on the bar.
- **Merge into…** — reconciling every field and relinking every edge is a wizard, not a puck button.

### Artifact

Interactive mockup with all five bars, both themes, working popovers and select-all: `docs/mockups/table-bulk-select.html`.


---

### Revision — Kyle, 2026-08-24 (second pass)

**Set state is cut.** A table can carry more than one workflow field, so a single *Set state* button is a lie about the schema. State is a field like any other and lives inside **Set a field…**, which now opens a two-step picker: field list → value editor (state chips, select options, a text/number input, or a checked/unchecked pair). The demo table carries two workflow fields (`Status` and `Stage`) precisely to show this. The alternative Kyle named — generating one bar command per workflow field — trades the puck's fixed width for a bar that changes shape per table, and is recorded but not taken.

**Link to… no longer wears a chain-link icon.** A chain reads as a hyperlink; the glyph is now two rows joined by an edge with a junction dot, which reads as a table relation. The picker is two-step and search-first (per Feature #100's one selection dialect): relation → search the target table → pick the row.

**Show these in the map** and **Select all with the same…** are cut. The map is a place you go, not somewhere a selection pushes you; growing a selection is the filter strip's job.

**Selected rows** carry the accent tint alone — the leading accent stripe is removed.

**Checkbox alignment.** Header and body checkboxes now share one padding rule at equal specificity and sit inside an identical 34×30 label hit target, so the select-all box lands on the same vertical line as every row's box. `.grid thead th` had been out-specifying a plain `th.cb`.

Final set — **on the bar**: Set a field…, Link to…, Duplicate, and Move to trash past the hairline. **Under `⋯`**: Move to table…, Roll up into a new entity…, Copy links.


---

### Slice 1 shipped — 2026-08-26 (`b8f0a39`)

Selection state and the checkbox column are live. `public/selection-core.js` is
the pure half (toggle, range, prune, headState, selectAll, barCommands); the
DOM half is `renderTable` in `public/app.js`.

**One departure from the spec above, forced by Ledger.** This record says
"clicking anywhere in a row toggles it, except on the `#` link". Ledger landed
the same evening (`a2cca58`) with the opposite rule: a bare row click raises
THAT CELL's editor. Two meanings for one gesture is one too many, so the
checkbox owns selection outright and **shift-click extends the span from the
last box hit**. Clicking a cell leaves the selection alone; checking a row
opens no editor. Both halves are pinned by tests.

Selection is a set of entity ids, never row indices — a sort re-orders every
row and the same records stay chosen; a row that leaves the page is pruned.
Painting is not a redraw, so an open cell editor survives a click in the
column. Escape clears unless a dialog or popover owns the keystroke first.
Trashed rows get no box.

Tests: 13 pure cases (`test/row-selection.test.mjs`) + 9 browser cases
(`test/row-selection-browser.test.mjs`). `ui-contract`'s colCount pin moved to
`+ 4`; what the add-row span must EQUAL is now proved against a live header.

**Still to build:** slice 2, the puck itself, and slice 3, the commands
(Set a field…, Link to…, Duplicate, Move to trash, and the `⋯` set).

### Slice 2 shipped — 2026-08-26 (`dcddcf4`)

The puck is live. Icon only, hover labels, the count in an accent pill, trash
past a hairline, glass shell, rises 14px on appear. The grid grows a floor
while one is up so the bar never covers the last row it acts on.

**The bar carries only commands that can run.** `barCommands` takes a `built`
list; a designed-but-unbuilt button reads as broken rather than forthcoming.
Today that is **Duplicate** and **Move to trash**. `moreCommands` answers to
the same rule, so there is no `...` overflow yet.

Duplicate copies every writable field; computed fields and documents are not
copied, because a computed field is a read and recomputes on the copy. A bulk
command that half works and reports success is how a row goes missing quietly,
so the toast names what did NOT land.

Handbook gained "Working on many rows at once" under the grid section.

Tests: 16 pure + 14 browser. Full suite 901/901 on a tree carrying only this
work.

**Slice 3 remains:** Set a field... (two-step picker, field then value, state
included), Link to... (relation then search the target), and the overflow set
(Move to table..., Roll up into a new entity..., Copy links). Each wants a
batch write at the engine or route layer rather than the current per-row loop.

features.name: The grid is a record: the Ledger table view
features.description:
**Chosen by Kyle 2026-08-24** from the grid study (three directions, then two): Records was cut, Sheet was kept in reserve, Ledger was built.

The grid read as a form. Every cell wore a control, hovering drew a box around each one — so a row looked ruled between its fields — and a row click fought the cell it landed on.

**Shipped 2026-08-24 (commit 289fa64, Gerrit change 49, Verified +1).**

## The rule

**The `#id` link navigates, every cell edits.** A bare row click no longer opens the entity; it raises that field type's own editor and places the cursor. `WeaveEditorLib.cellActivation()` is the pure half:

| Field type | A click on the cell |
| --- | --- |
| text · number · url · email · key · date | focus the input, caret at the end |
| select · multiselect · workflow | open its picker |
| relation · attachments | open the record search / file chooser |
| checkbox | toggle it |
| formula · rollup · lookup · document · field | nothing — not edited from the grid |

⌘-click opens the row in the **side peek**, so the table keeps its place.

## The skin

- Chips stay chips — a value from a set of options still wears one (Kyle) — they lose the border and the box, not the tint.
- The × and + link are chrome about the row: hidden until it is hovered or holds focus.
- Computed cells drop the tinted ground and keep their glyph.
- **No cell draws itself a border on hover** (Kyle's correction). The row's tint is the feedback; the focused control is the only thing wearing one.
- The leading column is set heavier — it carries the row's identity.

## Density

Comfortable (46px rows) or Compact (32px), a segmented control in the toolbar, remembered per table per person in `localStorage` — a way of reading the table, not a property of it. Rows came down from 68px on the way: an input at rest is text, so it is sized like text (`min-height: 0`), and a relation's chips stopped wrapping onto a second line.

## Overflow

A capped column says what it is hiding. Clipped is **measured after layout**, never assumed, so the marker always means there is more. A clipped cell wears a ⤢ and opens the whole value on hover — as a **copy** in a layer over the grid (`.cell-pop-layer` off `.table-wrap`). The cell itself is never touched, so no column can move; verified live, `gridMoved: false`.

## Gates

`test/ledger-grid.test.mjs` (14 tests) pins all four of Kyle's corrections plus the skin and density. `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` rewrote the two assertions the old row-click contract owned — the board and embedded related rows still route the old way. `test/column-fit.test.mjs` now starts from a deliberately squeezed column: its "the width must move" wait measured against whatever auto-layout handed out, which stopped meaning anything once the name column got heavier, and failed on a fit that was correct (312 → 317, covering a 297px value).

Verified live at :4400 — row heights 46/32, density persisted, all five field types raising the right editor with the caret placed, read-only cells inert, peek 920px carrying the right entity.

features.name: Grid interaction: arrows navigate, cells rest, selection comes free
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-24 (Kyle), over four rounds. The last one decides the shape.

1. "mock up at least 5 UX interact pattern sets that include row select, cell edit, tab/arrow/return to navigate, shift-enter to create new item" → seven sets, A–G.
2. "click to select, click again to edit… what do we lose with this?" → G, two-click, and its seven costs.
3. "check boxes should not need double click. what if on hover you can always single click into the edit, command click and shift click always de/select multiple. rebuild the mock ups with only 3" → selection moved onto the modifiers; G retired.
4. **"I want to nav with L and R and tab"**

## Why round 4 is structural, not a tweak

`←` and `→` cannot navigate while a cell is a live text input — the caret is already using them. The round-3 direction claimed both and could only have one. Wanting the horizontal arrows for navigation means cells **rest as values** and open on purpose.

Two things fall out that Kyle did not ask for, and both are wins:

- **Keyboard row selection comes free.** `Space` is unclaimed at rest, so it picks a row up, `⇧↑`/`⇧↓` extend and `⌘A` takes the table. Round 3 needed a whole extra direction (K, a nav mode behind `Esc`) to buy exactly this. The H-versus-K question dissolves.
- **Hover finally has a job** — showing the control a click would open, rather than every cell wearing one at once.

## The three

| | | ← → at rest | ← → in an open cell | Row select | Build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NOW** | What ships (#133 Ledger) | the caret, always | the caret | none | — |
| **REST** | Resting cursor; the caret takes them back | **navigate** | the caret, until Tab/Return/Esc | keyboard + pointer | S |
| **EDGE** | Edge-through; they never stop navigating | **navigate** | caret, then **out at the text edge** | keyboard + pointer | S+ |

Both give Kyle what he asked for at rest. They differ on one axis only: whether `←`/`→` ever stop navigating.

## Still true from earlier rounds

One click edits whatever the type and a **checkbox flips on that one click**; `⌘`-click toggles a row and `⇧`-click takes the run; `Return` commits down the column; `⇧Return` makes the next item; `⌘Return` opens the record **as a page** — the side peek is not carried forward (verdict below).

## The peek

Counted, not argued. #39 built the side peek as every row's click target; #117 replaced that with the entity page and kept `peekEntity` only "for callers that want a slide-over on top of a page". No such caller was ever written. The one call site left is the `⌘`-click row target added by #133 — the exact case #117 had ruled out. Dropping it frees `⌘`-click outright and removes `peekEntity` (~56 lines), 17 CSS rules and 5 `inPeek` branches threaded through `renderEntityView`. The one honest argument for keeping it — the table holds its scroll position — is the trade #117 already made.

## Recommendation

**Build REST. Ship EDGE behind a setting if the corridor proves worth it.**

REST never surprises anyone: the caret owns the horizontal arrows inside an open cell exactly as it does in every text field on the machine. EDGE is the stricter reading and its appeal is real — a row of short values walks end to end on one key — but the keypress that leaves the cell is indistinguishable from the one before it, and an **empty cell is at both edges at once**, so a run of blanks becomes a corridor you fall through. That is worth having deliberately, which is what a setting is for. It is one branch in the open-cell keymap.

1. Cells rest as values; hover arms them. The click path is unchanged, so `activateCell` is already correct — it just runs on an armed cell rather than a permanently live one.
2. One keymap. At rest: arrows and `Tab` move, `Space` selects, `Return` or any character opens. Open: `Return` commits down, `Tab` commits across, `Esc` reverts.
3. Selection from both hands — `⌘`/`⇧`-click and `Space`/`⇧↑↓`.
4. Drop the peek in the same change; that is what makes `⌘`-click free.
5. Then the puck bar of #132, which now has a selection to act on.
6. EDGE as a per-table or per-user setting once REST is in.

## Still open

- **Do `←`/`→` step out of an open cell?** The only thing separating REST from EDGE, and a setting rather than a verdict.
- Does `⇧`-click take a run of rows or a rectangle of cells? Rows is smaller and matches #132; cells opens fill-down and paste later and cannot be retrofitted cheaply.
- Where does the docs-chips column sit in the arrow and Tab order? Documents are not cells.
- Does a resting grid still read as editable on a table of mostly-empty fields?

## Artifact

`docs/mockups/table-grid-keymaps.html` (beside `table-bulk-select.html` from #132) — three live grids with real checkbox, select-picker and date-calendar columns. **An open text cell is a real `<input>`**, so EDGE's "step out at the end of the text" is measured from `selectionStart` rather than mimed, and a caret readout above the grid shows which edge the keymap is seeing.

## Test coverage

`test/grid-patterns.test.mjs` — 20 cases, Quality suite #42. The mockup carries ONE pure keymap core in `<script id="pattern-core">`; the test extracts and presses it, so the page and the asserted behaviour cannot drift. Asserts all four arrows plus `Tab` navigate at rest in both challengers; that neither can be `always-live`, because that is what would take `←`/`→` back; that the resting state hands over `Space`/`⇧↑↓`/`⌘A` for free while `Space` inside an open cell is still a space; that REST gives the horizontal arrows to the caret even at the text edge; that EDGE steps out only at an edge, passes straight through an empty cell (at both edges at once), and keeps `⇧←`/`⇧→` selecting text; and that the demo reads a real `selectionStart` rather than faking the edge.

features.name: Agent surface coverage is a test, not a promise
Attachments chip uses paperclip emoji, not flat icon
features.description:
## Pain Point

The attachments chip (`.k-attach`, built in `public/app.js`) leads with a paperclip EMOJI (📎), which renders in colour and sits inconsistently beside the monochrome glyphs used by every other chip since the tiered chip/pill design system (value / pointer / computed) landed on 2026-08-24.

## Problem Statement

weave already vendors a flat icon set at `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js`, surfaced via the `iconEl('iconly:paper', 'wv-icon')` helper in `public/app.js` — that helper is the intended replacement for emoji glyphs, but the attachments chip wasn't switched over when the design system shipped.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Swap the 📎 emoji for the vendored flat paper-clip icon via `iconEl(...)` in the `.k-attach` chip build in `public/app.js`, matching how other chip tiers already render their leading glyph.

features.name: Expand STATE_ICONS glyph vocabulary (14 entries, now shared by select/multiselect)
features.description:
## Pain Point

`STATE_ICONS` in `public/field-dialog-core.js` has only 14 entries (`''  ○ ◔ ◑ ◕ ● ✓ ✕ ⏸ ⚑ ★ ! ? →`), surfaced via the `.opt-icon` button on each option row in the field tray — and since the 2026-08-24 chip/pill design system landed, that same picker is now offered to select and multiselect field options, not just workflow states.

## Problem Statement

14 glyphs is thin coverage for the union of workflow states plus every select/multiselect option across every field in the app. Authors will run out of distinct, meaningful icons and start reusing glyphs for unrelated options, undermining the point of the picker.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Expand `STATE_ICONS` with additional monochrome glyphs. Do NOT remove or reorder any of the existing 14 entries — authors may already have chosen them for existing options/states — only append.

features.name: files/url field types use emoji icons, not flat icons
features.description:
## Pain Point

In `FIELD_TYPES` (`public/field-dialog-core.js`), the `files` field type icon is 🗂 and the `url` field type icon is 🔗 — both colour emoji sitting among the otherwise-monochrome tiles in the field tray's type grid.

## Problem Statement

Same inconsistency as the attachments-chip emoji: the tiered chip/pill design system (2026-08-24) established a monochrome flat-icon vocabulary via `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js` and the `iconEl(...)` helper in `public/app.js`, but these two `FIELD_TYPES` entries were never migrated off emoji.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Replace both the `files` and `url` icons in `FIELD_TYPES` with flat icons from `public/vendor/iconly-flat.js` via the existing `iconEl(...)` helper, matching the treatment used elsewhere in the type grid.

features.name: Define a first-class person field type with a real avatar
features.description:
## Pain Point

The weave chip system landed 2026-08-24 as Gerrit change 61 (repo grunion-ai/weave, files public/chip-core.js, public/style.css, public/app.js). It has three tiers — value (filled tint, no border), pointer (1px outline plus ↗), computed (glyph then value). Kyle's requirement during the design review was: "person field type should have an avatar no matter the chip style." That shipped, but on a heuristic, because weave has no person concept to hang it on.

## Problem Statement

* weave has no `person` field type. `VALUE_TYPES` in src/engine.js is text, number, date, daterange, checkbox, url, email, select, multiselect, workflow, relation, field, key, attachments. A colleague is just a `relation` to whatever table happens to hold people.
* weave also has no users/members concept at all — the only system table kind in src/engine.js is `workspace` (spaces and tables as rows). There is no identity to attach a photo, a display name, or a handle to.
* So `personAvatar()` in public/app.js decides person-ness by matching the RELATION'S TARGET TABLE NAME against a regex, `PERSON_TABLE = /^(people|persons?|members?|users?|contacts?|owners?|team|staff|employees?)$/i` in `relationIsPerson()`.
* That is wrong in both directions: a table called "Reviewers" or "Assignees" or anything in another language gets no avatar, and a table called "Team" that holds squads rather than humans gets avatars it should not have. It also silently changes behaviour when someone renames a table.
* The avatar today is initials on a hue hashed from the display name (`hueForName` and `initialsFor` in public/chip-core.js, hashing into the 9-entry RAMP_ORDER). There is no photo path at all — `.av img` exists in the CSS and nothing ever populates it.

## Proposed Solution / Solution Shape

Direction, not a spec to follow blindly:

* Add `person` to the field types as a first-class type, so person-ness is declared rather than guessed. `relationIsPerson()` in public/app.js is the single function that changes — it was written to be that seam, and the comment in the source says so.
* Decide what a person IS in weave: probably a designated people table per workspace, or a built-in system table alongside the existing `workspace` one. This is the real design question and should be settled before any code.
* Give a person a photo. `.av img` styling already exists in public/style.css and the files API (`/api/files/:id`) and the `attachments` field already handle uploads, so the plumbing is largely there; the missing piece is where the photo lives on the person record.
* Keep initials-on-a-hashed-hue as the fallback when there is no photo — that behaviour is already tested and Kyle liked it.
* Add the type to the tray's `FIELD_TYPES` grid in public/field-dialog-core.js so it is selectable, with a flat icon (see sibling ticket #1875 about emoji-vs-flat icons in that same grid).

Known limitations to carry forward:

* Nine ramp hues plus a name hash means two colleagues sometimes get the same avatar colour. Initials still separate them and a photo removes the question, but it is worth deciding whether the hash should widen when the person type lands.
* Contract tests for the current behaviour live in test/chip-system.test.mjs (the avatar, initials and hash tests). Those pin the fallback and should survive; the test asserting the target-table heuristic is the one that changes.

Sibling of the other weave chip-system follow-ups filed the same day: Task Name #1873 [[#^be16b3a5-c5a3-4083-a021-d2a8b0b5d6dc/01a0371a-42e3-7d42-8d5d-28b2587e1b03]], Task Name #1874 [[#^be16b3a5-c5a3-4083-a021-d2a8b0b5d6dc/01a0371a-4b0e-77e2-a8a0-dcbc4ace5fd1]], Task Name #1875 [[#^be16b3a5-c5a3-4083-a021-d2a8b0b5d6dc/01a0371a-5364-723c-a6f6-01ca84af0e43]].

features.name: The picker is a token box: chips live with the cursor
features.description:
**Requested:** 2026-08-25 (Kyle) — *"selected chips should be in the cursor box so user can navigate around with arrows to quckly delete and type to add with the top fit autoselected on search and added with enter up down arros to navigate options enter to select. pressing enter with none selected updates the select field. true for multi select and linked fileds, single select and states are slickly different since selection overwrites"*

## What changed

The chosen values moved **inside** the search field. One box now carries both halves of the edit — the chips already chosen, then the caret — instead of a chosen-list stacked above a separate search bar. Everything that picks from a list opens it: multiselect, linked records, select, workflow states, field types, formats.

## The grammar

| Key | multi (multiselect, linked records) | single (select, workflow state) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| typing | filters the list with the **top fit armed** | same |
| `Enter` | adds the armed option (a second `Enter` takes it back out), clears the search, stays open | picks it — a selection **overwrites**, so it commits and closes |
| `Enter` on an empty search | saves the set | closes; the field already carries what is in the box |
| `↑` `↓` | move the arming through the visible list | same |
| `←` `→` | walk the chips in the box, from the caret leftward | walks its one chip |
| `Backspace` | takes the last chip, or the one the cursor sits on | picks the field's empty value (`—`); a workflow state has none, so it is refused |
| `Delete` | takes the chip under the cursor, cursor stays put | same |
| `Esc` | closes without saving | closes |
| outside click | saves (unchanged) | closes |
