**Top fit** is a ranking, not "first one containing the letters": exact label, then prefix, then word-prefix, then anywhere in the label, then a hint-only match (a record's `#id` on a link picker). Typing `do` against Backlog / To do / Doing / Done arms **Doing**.

## Where it lives

| Layer | File |
| --- | --- |
| The grammar, pure | `public/picker-core.js` — `keyDown` returns `{state, effect}`; effects are `pick` / `commit` / `close` |
| The DOM | `searchPicker` in `public/app.js` — feeds it keys plus whether the text caret sits at position 0 |
| The box | `.picker-box` / `.picker-chips` (`display:contents`) / `.picker-chip.sel` in `public/style.css` |
| Tests | `test/picker-core.test.mjs` (16 cases) + two contract cases in `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` |

Chips redraw as their own element so a redraw never detaches the focused input; `display:contents` keeps them flowing in the box's own row, so a full box wraps with the caret rather than clipping.

## Verified live (127.0.0.1:4400, Product/Task, both themes)

| Field | Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Tags` multiselect | `ch` → Enter, `bu` → Enter, `←` `←` Backspace, Enter | `['design','feature','bug']` persisted |
| `Priority` select | `p2` → Enter | `P2` written and closed |
| `Priority` select | Backspace on its chip | cleared to empty |
| `State` workflow | `rev` → Enter | `Review`; the chip carries no `×` and Backspace is refused |
| `Project` linked | `←` Backspace then `Esc` | edit discarded, link intact |


## Amended 2026-08-26 (change 67, commit 7a1cfe8) — three rows of the grammar above are now wrong

Kyle used the shipped box and filed [[Issue#63]], [[Issue#64]] and
[[Issue#65]]. The first two were one defect: chosen options stayed in the list
wearing a ✓, so `↓` from a fresh box usually armed something already chosen and
Enter took it back out. Read these rows in place of the ones in the table:

| Key | multi (multiselect, linked records) | single (select, workflow state) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the list | holds only what is **not** already a chip in the box | unchanged — the current value stays listed and ticked |
| `Enter` | adds the armed option and disarms the list; it can no longer take one back out | unchanged |
| `Enter` after a pick | nothing is armed, so it saves — pick-then-Enter is the whole edit | n/a |
| `Enter` on a search matching only what is chosen | nothing (it used to fall through and save) | nothing |
| `⌥1`–`⌥9` | takes the row that number names | same |
| un-picking | `⌫` on the chip, or its × | unchanged |

The `✓` on a multi row is gone with the row itself. An emptied list says
"Everything is chosen" rather than "No matches". Every visible row carries its
number; Option is the modifier because the box is a search field and a bare
digit has to keep typing.

New gate: `test/picker-browser.test.mjs` drives the box through real key
presses in Chromium. The "Verified live" table below was a hand check, and a
hand check is what let [[Issue#63]] ship.

features.name: Users: identity, auth, permissions, sharing (design-only spec)
features.description:
# Users — complete spec (outline; details intentionally blank)

Design-only feature request. Nothing here is scheduled for implementation. Each section below gets filled in one at a time, in review with Kyle; a section is done when its **Decisions** block replaces its **Open questions** block. The spec is complete when no section still says TBD.

**Existing substrate (v0.4, Feature #14):** `wv_` bearer tokens (sha256 stored, minted once), roles admin/writer/reader, `requireAuth` workspace switch, structural audit log with actor, `createdBy`/`modifiedBy` strings on entities. Deliberately deferred then: account rows as a registry table, per-space permissions. This spec is the full build-out that deferral pointed at.

---

## 1. Identity model — who a "user" is

Scope: the User as a first-class record; the relationship between User (person or agent), Account (credential holder), and Actor (audit attribution). Whether agents are users with a flag or a separate kind.

Open questions: user vs account — one thing or two? Are agents users? Is identity server-wide or per-workspace? Canonical identifier (handle, email, id)?

Details: TBD.

## 2. System table of users

Scope: Users as a registry/system table visible in the UI like Spaces/Tables/Fields — queryable, relatable, but lifecycle-managed by the system, not row CRUD.

Open questions: which space does it live in? What is user-editable vs system-owned? Does it depend on a key/sensitive field type so tokens can never render? Export behavior?

Details: TBD.

## 3. Authentication

Scope: how a human signs in to the web app and how an agent authenticates to the API/MCP. Sessions vs bearer tokens. The `requireAuth` switch's final semantics.

Open questions: password, magic link, OAuth/OIDC, or token-only? Session storage and expiry? Local single-user mode — does auth stay optional forever on localhost? Interplay with hosting (Fly.io SaaS vs BYOC), where auth is the known blocker.

Details: TBD.

## 4. Keys: CLI + MCP keygen and association

Scope: full `wv_` token lifecycle — mint, list, rotate, revoke, expire, scope — via CLI, MCP, and UI; every key bound to a user; per-agent keys.

Open questions: scoped keys (read-only, one space, one table)? Expiry defaults? Rotation UX? How does an MCP session name its user? Key display safety (needs the key field type)?

Details: TBD.

## 5. User levels (roles)

Scope: the role ladder. Today admin/writer/reader; decide the final set and what each rung means globally.

Open questions: add owner? guest/viewer distinct from reader? Are roles global, per-workspace, or both? Can a user hold different roles in different workspaces?

Details: TBD.

## 6. Permissions & access control

Scope: the enforcement model — what a role can see and do at workspace, space, table, and entity level. Schema-vs-data split (registry-row writes already count as schema).

Open questions: per-space permissions (the deferred half of #14)? Entity-level or field-level ACLs, or explicitly out of scope? Default-open or default-closed? Inheritance and override rules? Read visibility vs write rights?

Details: TBD.

## 7. Workspace assignment & membership

Scope: one server, many workspace `.db` files — who belongs to which workspace, membership records, default workspace on login.

Open questions: where does membership live (per-workspace db vs server-level)? Can a workspace be personal vs shared? What does removing a member do to their attributions?

Details: TBD.

## 8. Invites

Scope: getting a new user in — invite creation, delivery, acceptance, expiry, and the role granted on join.

Open questions: invite = link token? email delivery or copy-paste link only (zero-dep constraint)? Who may invite? Re-invite/revoke? What happens pre-acceptance in people fields?

Details: TBD.

## 9. Sharing

Scope: granting access narrower than membership — share an entity, view, or document with a user, or via link; public/anonymous links.

Open questions: is sharing v1 or explicitly out of scope? Link tokens with what powers (read-only)? Does a share bypass or compose with permissions? Audit of shares?

Details: TBD.

## 10. People field type

Scope: a real field type holding user references on any entity — assignee, owner, reviewer. Single and multi. `createdBy`/`modifiedBy` graduate from strings to user refs.

Open questions: is it a relation to the Users table or a distinct primitive? Filtering/grouping semantics ("me" filter)? @-mentions in documents? Watchers as a people field?

Details: TBD.

## 11. Avatars

Scope: avatar image per user — storage in `files/`, upload paths (UI/CLI/API), rendering in chips, people fields, activity, comments; deterministic initials/color fallback; agent avatars distinguishable from humans.

Open questions: size/format limits? Generated identicon vs initials? Where do avatars render first?

Details: TBD.

## 12. Attribution, activity & audit

Scope: every write attributed to a user everywhere — entity activity feeds, comments, document edits, and the existing structural audit log — with one actor model across all of them.

Open questions: backfill of historical string actors ("web", "cli")? Does the audit log become user-queryable per user? Retention?

Details: TBD.

## 13. Notifications

Scope (not in the original list — proposed): telling a user something happened — mention, assignment, state change on a watched entity.

Open questions: in-app only, or email/webhook? Digest vs realtime? Is this deferred to its own feature once people fields exist?

Details: TBD.

## 14. Presence & concurrent editing

Scope (not in the original list — proposed): who is here now — presence dots, and how user identity interacts with concurrent edits/conflicts.

Open questions: in scope at all, or explicitly deferred? Minimum viable presence without websockets?

Details: TBD.

## 15. Admin surface

Scope: managing users — UI page, CLI (`account …` grows into `user …`), MCP tools; deactivate vs delete; what admin-only means once users exist.

Open questions: soft-deactivate semantics (keys die, attributions persist)? Last-admin protection? Impersonation for debugging — allowed or banned?

Details: TBD.

## 16. API / CLI / MCP surface

Scope: the complete external contract — REST endpoints, CLI commands, MCP tools — for everything above, named and versioned in one place.

Open questions: naming (`account` vs `user`)? Back-compat for existing `wv_` tokens and `account` CLI? What do anonymous requests see when `requireAuth` is off?

Details: TBD.

## 17. Data model & migration

Scope: sqlite tables (users, memberships, invites, shares, sessions, keys), what `exportJSON`/`importJSON` carry (never key material), migration from v0.4 accounts, JSON-workspace behavior.

Open questions: users in the workspace db or a server-level db beside it? Export portability of identity across servers? Downgrade story?

Details: TBD.

## 18. Security model

Scope: threat model and hard rules — hashing, one-time key display, rate limiting, session fixation, CSRF for the web app, injection-safe rendering of user-supplied names/avatars, secrets never in exports or logs.

Open questions: which of these are v1 gates vs hosted-only concerns? Brute-force lockout policy?

Details: TBD.

## 19. Rollout & testing

Scope: TDD gates per section, phase ordering (what unlocks what), milestone assignment, and the definition of done for the whole feature.

Open questions: likely spine — users table → people field → permissions → invites → sharing? Which milestone (v0.5 hosting wants auth early)?

Details: TBD.

---

**Walkthrough state:** none of the 19 sections reviewed yet. Next action: go through them one by one with Kyle, replacing Open questions with Decisions.

features.name: In-app bug reporter: four symptoms + a replayable action trace
features.description:
## What shipped

A bug glyph sits in the bottom-right corner of every page. Clicking it floats a small panel beside the button — no backdrop, so the broken page stays visible while the report is written.

The panel is note-first: the caret lands in the text box, so the fastest report is to start typing. Under it, four symptoms toggle as a **multi-select** — `Slow`, `Looks broken`, `Wrong data`, `Error` — because one bug is often slow *and* wrong. Either half is enough to send: a sentence alone is the "other" nobody needs a fifth button for. The Send button becomes **Sent** in place rather than relying on a toast.

## Why it is worth more than a bug form

Every session runs a ring-buffer recorder (`public/bug-core.js`). It keeps routes entered, controls clicked, requests that failed or were slow, and anything that threw. Submitting turns that into a **Replay** section: numbered steps, each stamped with how many seconds before the click on Send it happened, plus the raw trace as JSON so an agent parses instead of scraping prose.

Two rules the buffer never breaks:

- **Values are not actions.** A control is remembered by its name — a grid cell by its column and its row's entity id — never by what was typed into it. Secrets are stripped before the report leaves the page.
- **An error outranks recency.** At capacity the buffer drops an ordinary event, never the throw.

Quiet successful reads are not recorded at all. A page load fires a dozen 200-in-3ms GETs; recorded, they filled the buffer with the app working correctly and pushed the actual actions off the end (measured live: 17 requests to 5 actions). Only failures, slow calls, and real writes are evidence — and weave posts its reads, so the rule classifies by path, not by verb.

## Where it lands

`POST /api/bug-report` files into **this** workspace's `Development/Issue` whichever workspace the reporter was in — a bug in weave is not a row in somebody's data. Symptoms go into the `Symptom` multiselect so a week of reports is filterable; severity is the worst symptom picked, Medium when none is. The server stamps its own version, start time and uptime rather than trusting the page's copy — a stale build reporting its own version is how this project's most common false bug starts.

A workspace whose `Symptom` options were renamed, or that predates the field, still keeps the report: the symptom survives in the Description and the field is left alone. A label edit costs the field, not the bug.

## Tests

`test/bug-report.test.mjs` — 55 cases across the recorder, redaction, the rendered report, the route, and the UI's own source-level promises (including a parse gate, after a traced SVG path arrived with potrace's line wraps still inside a string literal and blanked the page).

features.name: Credential field: generalize key (design-only spec)
features.description:
# Credential field — generalizing `key` (design-only spec)

Design-only feature request, sibling to Feature #141 (Users). Nothing here is scheduled for implementation. It answers the one question #141 §6 left open — "field-level ACLs, or explicitly out of scope?" — with: **out of scope, permanently.** Permission moves to the credential, not the field.

**Existing substrate (v0.4, Feature #64):** the `key` field type stores the NAME of a secret; the value lives in `~/.weave/keystore.json` (chmod 600), never enters the workspace `.db`, and is deliberately unreadable over HTTP. `resolveKey` exists only for the engine's own consumers (automations, integrations). MCP promises "no tool returns a secret value."

---

## 1. The thesis: permission belongs to the secret, not the field

The two motivating use cases — a team-shared password and a stored SSN — both require that a human can get the value back out, which breaks the current never-read-back contract on purpose. The design keeps the deeper invariant instead: **the secret value never enters the table.** The field stores metadata (ordinary table data, visible to anyone with table access — no exception to "table access = see the table"). The value lives in a credential object with **its own access list**, and reveal is a separate, authorized, audited act against that object.

This is how every mature secret manager already works: 1Password gates by vault, AWS Secrets Manager by resource policy — per-secret, never per-field. It also avoids weave's first per-field read rule, which would otherwise have to be consulted by every view, formula, lookup, export, deck render, and MCP read path, and would invite row-level ACLs next.

## 2. Grain (what the field stores)

```
{
  kind: 'apikey' | 'token' | 'id' | 'password' | 'pair',
  keystore: 'local' | '1password' | 'aws-sm' | 'google-sm' | 'cloudflare' | 'apple-passwords',
  ref: string,            // keystore entry name / external ref
  parts?: [{name, secret: bool}],   // pairs: client_id (visible) + client_secret (masked)
  redacted?: bool,        // overrides the kind default
  rotatedAt?, rotatedBy?  // metadata only
}
```

* `pair` is ONE credential with named parts, only the secret part masked. Two fields pointing at two entries loses the pairing and doubles ACL bookkeeping.
* Kind sets the default posture, it does not decide masking alone: an AWS account ID is an `id` fine in the open; an SSN is an `id` that is not. `redacted` is per-credential.

## 3. Costume (how it renders)

Masked chip: kind glyph + keystore badge + label + `●●●●` in mono. Click → reveal (if permitted) with auto-rehide; copy-without-display button; inline audit note ("revealed 3× this week"). The value never renders in a normal cell path.

## 4. Access model

* **No field-level permissions.** Table access governs the metadata only.
* Per-credential ACL on the keystore entry: v1 = `owner (creator) + shared-with account list`, built on the existing v0.4 accounts (`wv_` tokens, admin/writer/reader), upgradeable when #141 lands real users.
* Kind defaults: `password`/`apikey`/`token`/`pair` → open to keystore holders (availability to the team); `id` with `redacted` → owner-only (confinement). One mechanism, opposite defaults.
* **Copy counts as reveal.** Copy-to-clipboard-without-display is the primary UX (value never hits the screen) but is identical in the access model and the audit log.
* Every reveal/copy lands in the existing `audit_log` (who, which credential, when) and is surfaced in the UI. The visible trail is what makes team sharing tolerable.

## 5. External keystores delegate

For 1Password / AWS SM / Google SM / Cloudflare refs, weave stores `{keystore, ref}` and never holds the value. Reveal = deep link into the manager, or resolution through the integration's own auth — the external manager's access model gates the value. Weave's own ACL question exists **only for the local keystore**. Apple Passwords has no server API: ref-only, "open in Passwords" affordance, full stop. This tiering is also the scope fence: weave's local keystore serves automation creds and low/mid-stakes team secrets; anything deserving a real vault gets a pointer to one. Weave never becomes 1Password.

## 6. Local keystore prerequisites

* **Encrypt at rest before widening what goes in.** Plaintext JSON at 0600 is fine for API keys on a single-user local instance; not fine once SSNs and hosted (v0.5) exist. This is a gate, not a nice-to-have.
* One new surface: `POST /api/keys/:name/reveal` (or per-credential id), ACL-checked, always audited. Admin token alone is not sufficient — the ACL is.

## 7. The exclusion invariant (kept, made explicit)

No formula, lookup, or rollup may ever reference a secret value — a formula concatenating a secret into a text field is a one-step exfiltration bypassing every reveal control. Automations receive values only as injected headers/env at execution time, never as readable intermediate state. Values never enter search index, exports, decks, or MCP reads; if a reveal MCP tool ever exists it is a deliberate, separately-scoped tool, not a widening of `weave_query`. Today all of this is free because the value is not in the db — the spec makes it a stated contract so it survives the generalization.

## 8. Migration

Existing `key` fields become `kind: 'apikey', keystore: 'local'` with **no reveal grant** — the current never-read-back promise holds for everything already stored. Reveal-ability is opt-in per credential, by its owner.

## 9. Sequencing

1. **Grain + costume.** Kind/keystore/ref/parts/redacted config, masked chip rendering. No access change — everything still non-revealable. Ships independently, pure win.
2. **Encrypt the local keystore.**
3. **Per-credential ACL + audited reveal/copy** for the local keystore, on v0.4 accounts.
4. **External keystore refs** — Cloudflare/AWS/Google first (they have APIs); Apple link-only.

## 10. Open questions

* Encryption key management for the local keystore (server key beside the db? passphrase? OS keychain?).
* Does `resolveKey` for automations need per-credential ACL too, or does "automation = workspace-level actor" hold until #141 lands?
* Reveal session shape: per-click grants vs short-lived reveal tokens.
* Whether `id`-kind non-secret values (visible account IDs) should ever store the value in-table instead of the keystore — or whether uniformity wins.

**Walkthrough state:** thesis and access model discussed with Kyle 2026-08-26 (chat); sections 2–9 drafted, not yet reviewed one-by-one.

features.name: Column ⋮ menu redesign: drawn icons, one row metric, an advertised hold
features.description:
**Asked for by Kyle, 2026-08-27**, with a screenshot of the open menu: *"redesign this dialog to match weave design language. I like the hold to delete and animation."*

The column header's ⋮ menu was the last surface still assembling itself out of characters. Five rows in one small panel and no two of them agreed.

## What the screenshot showed

| Row | What it was | Why it read wrong |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `✎ Edit field…` | a pencil **character** inside the label string | the font gives ✎ its own advance width and optical size |
| `+ Insert field…` | a plus character, same trick | a different advance width, so a different label left-edge |
| `↑ Sort ascending` | arrow character, plus a `'✓ '` prefix when the sort was live | the check shunted the whole row right whenever it was on |
| `↓ Sort descending` | ditto | — |
| `Delete field` | a Tabler `.dropdown-item`, red, no icon | another design system's padding and radius among weave's, and its label started somewhere none of the others did |

Four different left edges in a five-row menu, and four optical sizes among the glyphs. This is the exact defect **Issue #87** names — *"a unicode mark carries its own advance width and its own optical size"* — on the one surface that issue had not reached.

## What it is now

1. **Every mark is drawn.** `iconEl()` at `--wv-icon-md`, on the same `0 0 24 24` canvas as the rest of the app. `FIELD_MENU_ICONS` names them in one place. Picked by eye off a contact sheet of every candidate in both vocabularies, not by name: `iconly:arrow-up` is a solid teardrop that reads as a **map pin** at 16px, so sort uses the drawn `↑` / `↓` marks. `edit` and `delete` stay on iconly because that is what the entity command bar already draws for the same two verbs.
2. **A bare `+` joined the mark set.** Iconly's only plus is a filled rounded square, which came out the darkest thing on the panel beside a hairline pencil. `'+': line('M12 5.4v13.2M5.4 12h13.2')` — stroke 2.6, the same move Issue #87 made for the five marks it drew. Not offered in the icon picker; `STATE_ICONS` is unchanged.
3. **One row for every row.** The destructive row is a `.chip-pop-row` now, tinted, not a `.dropdown-item`. `holdToConfirm` takes a `rowClass` so the other four call sites keep theirs.
4. **Sort state is the popover's own check**, in the trailing `.chip-pop-check` slot the picker already uses — so the label never moves, and `showPopover` opens focus on the live sort for free.
5. **The panel names its column.** `Priority · SELECT` above a rule. The ⋮ paints millimetres from the *next* column's label (live check, 2026-08-16) and the hovered tint was the only thing tying panel to column.
6. **The hold is kept and advertised.** Kyle likes the gesture; a hold nobody knows about is a button that does nothing. The row carries a quiet `HOLD` chip at rest that clears once the press starts, where the swapped `Hold to delete…` label takes over. The sweep is now a `linear-gradient` off `--tblr-danger` rather than a literal `rgba(214,57,57,.25)`, darkening toward the leading edge so it reads as a front travelling across the row instead of a block growing out of the left. Still `scaleX` on a transform, still untransitioned on collapse — the Feature #75 contract is untouched.
7. **Popovers arrive rather than appear** — `wv-pop-in`, 120ms, opacity + transform only, with a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out. Shared by every `.chip-pop`.

## A bug found on the way

The delete row being a `.dropdown-item` was not only a look. `showPopover` walks `.chip-pop-row` for ↑↓, so **the one row that most deserves deliberate aim was the only one the keyboard could not reach.** Logged as its own Issue.

## Evidence

`after-light.png`, `after-dark.png`, `after-sorted.png`, `after-holding.png` (attached) — the panel in both themes, with a live sort, and mid-sweep at ~430ms. Captured with Playwright at 1200×760 @2x against a throwaway workspace.

## Gates

- `test/field-menu-browser.test.mjs` — **7 new cases, real browser.** All seven fail against the pre-change `public/` and pass after; verified by running the suite against `git show HEAD:public/{app.js,style.css}` in a scratch tree.
- `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` — 7 new source/CSS contracts (131 → 138). Same before/after check.
- `node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'` → **1108 pass, 0 fail.**

features.name: The description is a role, and it previews its first lines
features.description:
Kyle, 2026-08-27: "description should be a default field in all entities. it can be renamed or deleted but it should always show a preview of the properly formatted first few lines, not an md document chip."

Three claims, and only the first was true.

## The role

`createTable` already minted a `Description` document field on every table, but the role lived in the literal string and in the accident of sorting first. A table now carries **`descriptionFieldId`**, beside `nameFieldId` — an id, so a rename costs nothing to maintain, and `null` on delete, which is the tombstone that lets `#ensureDescriptionField` tell "the owner removed it" from "this table predates the role" (`undefined`, which adopts the first document field rather than minting a second).

Unlike `nameFieldId`, nothing is defended: renaming and deleting are the point. Every reader of "the default document" — `#resolveDocField`, `readEntity`, the append-doc automation and its label — goes through one `descriptionField(db)`, so reordering columns no longer silently reassigns which document is the description. Registry tables have no description role: their `Description` is the TEXT column mirroring the real space/table description, and Workflows' `Script`/`Diagram` are structure, not prose.

`describeSchema` emits `role: "description"` on the one field that holds it, and `applySchema` renames the minted field to match instead of skipping any descriptor literally called `Description`.

## The preview

The description leaves the `Docs (n)` cell for a **column of its own**, which reconciles the two rulings rather than reversing either. What Kyle rejected on 2026-08-24 was a flattened 90-character slice of ONE document standing in for the row ([[Issue#58]]); Spec, Model and test keep exactly the chips that ruling won. The description gets a column because it says something.

`WeaveEditorLib.docPreview(md, { lines })` is the block pass and the only one: hashes off headings, bullets off list items, quote carets dropped, tables, rules and fenced code skipped whole. Each line is then dressed through `inlineTokens`, so there is still one inline grammar in the browser, shared with `dressedText` via a new `dressTokens`. A document that is not prose is NAMED, never flattened — `HTML app` (its `<title>` when it has one), `JSON model · 2 keys`, `graph diagram` — because a doctype makes a terrible summary. Classification is `docKind`'s, so a preview and a chip can never disagree.

**Where the design could not take Kyle literally.** A row holds ONE line. `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs` requires every docs-carrying row to be the same height and at most 48px comfortable / 34px compact — caps Kyle himself drove a comfortable row down to on 2026-08-26. Two lines is ~43px of content and blows both. So the cell shows the first line and carries the rest hidden in the same DOM, and `showCellPop`'s `cloneNode` copy reveals all three on hover at 380px, wrapped. `markClippedCells` gained an OR for "carries more than one preview line", or a cell whose first line fits would never be markable and the rest would be unreachable. Empty is a dashed invitation — never opacity, never Tabler's global `.empty`.

## Bugs found and fixed on the way

[[Issue#104]] a deleted description came back on the next open. [[Issue#105]] a renamed Issue description threw the whole bug report away. [[Issue#106]] describeSchema→applySchema duplicated a renamed description and re-minted a deleted one.

## Gates

New: `test/description-field.test.mjs` (9), `test/doc-preview.test.mjs` (11). Extended: `test/schema-roundtrip.test.mjs` (+4), `test/grid-chrome.test.mjs` (+3, live Chrome — marks not syntax, hover reveals the rest, empty is dashed), `test/ui-contract.test.mjs` (+1), `test/doc-chips.test.mjs` (+1 and the ruling narrowed in its header rather than deleted), `test/bug-report.test.mjs` (+1), `test/applet.test.mjs` (+1), `test/handbook.test.mjs` (+1 — the page said "Documents never take a column of their own" and NOTHING pinned the sentence, so it could have rotted silently; that hole is closed).

Suite: **1142 pass, 0 fail.**

features.name: The task applet: one table, one screen, one thumb
features.description:
# The task applet

`/w/<ws>/t` — a passcode-gated single page over one table, built for mobile Safari and nothing else. No workspace rail, no table switcher: a view onto a table, not the web app. Kyle, 2026-08-27: *"its more like a view to a weave table than a weave web app"*.

## Where it sits

Generated by `src/applet.js`, mounted in `src/routes.js` in the block that already existed for share links — **ahead of the auth wall**, because like a share link it carries its own authorization. Not dropped in `public/`: on the Cloudflare adapter the assets binding serves `public/` before the Worker runs, so a file there would be ungated forever.

## The gate

`WEAVE_APPLET_PASSCODE`, compared in constant time, answered with a server-set `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=1y` cookie. WebKit caps *script-written* cookies at seven days; one the page never touches it leaves alone. With no passcode configured there is no applet at all — not even a gate to guess at. The passcode lives in the environment, never in the workspace, so it cannot leave through `/api/export`.

Eight wrong tries in ten minutes and the door stops answering, per workspace rather than per process.

## Field-driven

The applet bakes in no field names. The workflow field is whichever field has that type, its states are its own, and *active* is a question about categories — not about the word "Open". Every other field draws itself from its type through weave's own hue ramp (`public/chip-core.js`), so a field added to the table appears on the phone with no code change. `WEAVE_APPLET_TABLE` points it somewhere else and the page follows.

## What it does

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Create | Return creates and keeps the caret; the next task is one keystroke away |
| State | The glyph cycles not-started → in-progress → done, by category |
| Swipe | Right marks it done, left marks it in progress — absolute, not relative, and armed only past 24px so Safari's back gesture survives |
| Fields | One chip rail on the task page, 58pt where labelled rows took 370; every chip opens its editor as a sheet on the same page |
| Blanks | An empty deadline or tag set still holds a dashed chip on the row — triage happens in the list |
| Dates | Today / Tomorrow / the day after by name / Next week as chips, `parseNaturalDate` for what you type, the native picker underneath |
| Files | From the compose paperclip or the task page |
| Prose | `PUT /t/entity/:id/doc`, written in a full-height sheet |
| Defaults | `WEAVE_APPLET_DEFAULTS` applies field values to everything it creates |
| Bugs | The weave FAB, filing real `Development/Issue` rows and answering with the number |

## The keyboard

Safari grants `focus()` only inside a user gesture, and an `await` spends it. So the focus call happens first, synchronously, in the tap that enters the eighth digit — which is why the gate is an overlay on this page rather than a page of its own. A navigation would have thrown the gesture away.

Focusing *without* a gesture is actively harmful: the caret lands but no keyboard comes, and the user's first real tap is then a tap on an already-focused input, which raises nothing. A coarse pointer is left alone on open; the first tap that is not aimed at a row raises the keyboard via blur-then-focus.

One tap remains the floor. iOS grants no gesture to a page opened from a Shortcut or a Home Screen icon, and nothing in the page can conjure one.

## Hosted

Deployed to the grunion Cloudflare account as `weave-uno`, one SQLite-backed Durable Object, seeded from `uno.db` on 2026-08-28. **The hosted copy and the local file are separate copies and do not sync** — a decision still open.

## Tests

`test/applet.test.mjs`, 32 cases: the gate, the forged cookie, the rate limit, the scope of the data, the promise that the applet can only ever reach its own table, and the field-driven contract against a table whose workflow is called Stage.

features.name: Nav stats strip: workspace entity count + on-disk size
features.description:
The sidebar foot carries a quiet stats strip under "+ New space": the workspace's live entity total and what it weighs on disk, in GB (TB past 1000 GB).

## How it works

- `engine.storageStats()` — live entity count (trashed rows excluded) + size: the store's `.db` with WAL/SHM sidecars plus attachment bytes summed from each entity's own file ledger. `files/` is shared by every sibling workspace, so the directory itself is never the measure.
- `GET /api/health` ships `entities` + `sizeBytes` with the existing payload — workspace-scoped, one fetch shared with the instance chip (`state.healthP`).
- `renderNav` sums the same per-table `entityCount` figures the nav rows already show; `fmtSize` speaks GB/TB only (a small workspace reads "0.01 GB", never switches down to MB).
- `.nav-stats` in style.css: 11px monospace secondary, same register as the version chip. Verified in both themes.

Shipped in commit a87f8dc; suite `test/nav-stats.test.mjs` (5 cases) covers engine, store, health route, formatter and markup.

features.name: Fast in-app navigation: rope reserved for workspace loads, skeleton carries hash routes, 304 statics, custom 404 page
features.description:
Space/table/entity switches felt slow. Measured: the API answers in milliseconds (schema 2.6ms, table query 0.7ms) — the wait was the loader itself. withPageLoader wrapped every hash route; the rope appeared at 200ms and then always finished a full 2s cycle, and its 94%-opaque wash covered the Feature #49 skeleton it painted over.

Shipped:
- The rope is reserved for full page loads (boot — which is also every workspace switch, since those navigate to /w/<id>/). Hash routes ride the skeleton alone.
- The table skeleton draws the destination table's real column count via visibleCols(db) — the schema is already client-side, so the real shape is free.
- Statics carry Last-Modified and answer If-Modified-Since with 304: a workspace switch revalidates ~1.1MB of vendor JS/CSS instead of re-downloading it (Cache-Control stays no-cache).
- Branded 404 page (public/404.html, standalone, both themes): unknown page paths and unknown workspaces get it on GET; API callers keep the JSON error.

Verified live on :4400: hash navs never show the rope (MutationObserver count 0 across table switches), skeleton head draws 9 lines for a 9-column table, /no/such/page renders the 404 page in both themes, app.js answers 304.

Tests: test/nav-speed.test.mjs (5 cases) + reworked page-loader contracts incl. a new Function parse gate. Full suite green: 1162 pass.

Follow-up (Kyle, 2026-08-28, change 116): the rope covers ANY load expected to exceed 500ms — every route goes back through withPageLoader with LOADER_SHOW_AFTER_MS raised 200 -> 500. Routine navs still finish on the skeleton; a genuinely slow route or boot weaves the rope. Verified live: fast nav rope-free, a fetch delayed to 900ms shows the rope.

features.name: Table view config as fields: Filter and Sort on the Tables row
features.description:
## Shipped 2026-08-28
Option F: a table's view configuration is field values on its Workspace/Tables registry row, extending the Field Order / Hidden Fields precedent (2026-08-24).

- `updateTable {filters}` — `{ workflowFieldName: [stateNames] }`, validated (field must exist and be workflow, states must exist); empty clears. Replaces the per-browser localStorage filters from Feature #38: filters are table truth now, shared across browsers.
- `updateTable {sort}` — `[{ field, dir: asc|desc }]`, validated; empty clears. Replaces the ephemeral client sort that was lost on every navigation.
- The Tables row mirrors both as text — `Filter: State: Open, Doing` / `Sort: Due desc, Name asc` — and editing the row text writes back through the same verb with the same validation (#interceptUpdate → updateTable).
- describeSchema emits `filters`/`sort`; applySchema applies them (update + create paths).
- Client: filter chips and the ⋮ sort menu PATCH the table; the grid initialises sort from the schema.
- No new field types: validated text on the registry row is the established pattern. `ponytail:` a spec-valued `query` field type is the upgrade path when filters outgrow workflow states.
- Density stays per-person by design (a way of reading, not schema).

Tests: test/table-config-fields.test.mjs (6). Suite green 1168/1168.

features.name: Target-set (polymorphic) relations: one field, several legal target tables
features.description:
## What shipped

A relation field may now carry a **target set** — `targetDbs`, a list of member tables — instead of the single `targetDb`. Values may point at rows of any member. The registry's `Workspace/Spaces` and `Workspace/Tables` are legal members, so a row can point at a **space** or a **table** as easily as at another row.

## Design rulings (2026-08-28 design review)

- **One-way by design.** No inverse field is minted for a multi-target field — the alternative sprays a field across every member table. The reverse direction is a read.
- **Singleton sets collapse to the classic paired relation, bit-for-bit.** Existing fields and data are untouched; rollback is a plain revert.
- **Lookups and rollups keep the single-target contract** and refuse a target set — no one far table exists to read a field from.
- **Query traversal resolves each hop per-row** (`t.dbId`), so `Scope.Name` matches whichever member table the target lives in.
- **Chips carry their home table**; the picker searches every member; the relation map draws one edge per member.
- **Deleting a member table prunes it from every target set**; an emptied set takes its field with it.

## Evidence

- Suite: `test/polymorphic-relation.test.mjs` — 15 tests. Full run 1183/1183 green.
- Commit `c2b25b3` (v0.4.3), Gerrit change 121 (Verified +1).
- Live smoke on this server: one `Scope` field held a Note row, the `Smoke` space row, and the `Note` table row in a single value.
- Rollback: `git revert c2b25b3`; delete any multi-target fields first (or restore the pre-deploy db backup `backups/weave-pre-polymorphic-20260828-080733.db`) so old code never reads a `targetDbs` config it does not know.

See the Wiki article "Target-set relations: pointing at structure" for the full use-case walkthrough.

features.name: Editor toolbar + click-to-open outline panel
features.description:
Kyle (2026-08-29): "weave md editor needs some improvement, add tool bar and update the left side outline to only show on click not hover and float in at the midpoint fo the viewport"

**Toolbar.** The embedded editor's toolbar was deliberately empty (`toolbar: []`, the slash menu was the only chrome). Reversed: a compact strip — headings, bold, italic, strike, inline code, link · bullet/numbered/task lists · quote, code block, table, divider · undo, redo — styled as a quiet border-bottom strip on the page ground (`.doc-editor .vditor-toolbar`), `toolbarConfig: {hide:false, pin:true}`. The slash menu keeps the full catalogue (references, mermaid, raw HTML, math). Gotcha: the toolbar's headings dropdown reuses Vditor's `vditor-hint` class, so every slash-menu test selector is now scoped `.vditor-hint:not(.vditor-panel--arrow)`.

**Outline rail.** Hover-reveal removed. The resting rail stays a minimap; the first click anywhere on it (capture phase, so a closed-rail dash click opens rather than jumping blind) adds `.open`: the track goes `position:fixed; top:50%; translateY(-50%)` — vertically centred on the viewport — with its x pinned to the rail's own left, re-measured on every refresh and on window resize (a click can beat layout). A heading click jumps and closes; Escape or a click away closes.

Shipped in commit 74c9769 (1188 tests green). Suites updated: Embedded editor (renamed toolbar case), Phase 4 editor browser (16→17, click/midpoint/Escape coverage), new suite Outline dash rail (test/doc-rail.test.mjs, 15 cases). Handbook: Document formatting grew "The toolbar"; "The dash rail" rewritten for click-to-open. Verified live in both themes on :4400.

features.name: Development sync: every build ships and applies its issue list
features.description: **What ships.** Every build carries `docs/development.json` — the canonical Development space (Issues + Features, with status, severity/milestone, symptom, and description) exported at release time by `scripts/export-development.mjs`. On `weave serve` boot, `syncDevelopment()` (src/weaver-seed.js) applies the manifest to the local weave docs workspace: rows matched by name take the shipped status, unmatched manifest rows are created, and locally filed rows are never touched. A stamp on workspace meta makes the pass one write per build. Gate: test/development-sync.test.mjs pins the manifest to the package version, so a release without a fresh export fails the suite.
